21.5 Practice Ladder (8 Curated Problems across 4 Pedagogical Tiers)

Stepping Stone 1 (#036): AtCoder ABC 281 Ex — Alchemy

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 281, Problem Ex | Canonical ID: #036 (SS-1)
Prerequisites: Falling-Factorial / Binomial EGF (Ch 06), Lagrange Inversion (Ch 11), Compositional Inverse revert (§21.4) / Fast Composition compose (§21.2).


Problem Statement & Constraints
There are \(N + 1\) types of metals, numbered \(0, 1, \dots, N\). Initially, you have \(A\) distinct raw materials of metal \(0\) (labeled \(1, 2, \dots, A\)). For each \(k = 1, 2, \dots, N\), you can synthesize a unit of metal \(k\) by combining a non-empty subset of already-synthesized distinct units of metals from \(\{0, 1, \dots, k-1\}\); two units of metal \(k\) are considered distinct if and only if they are synthesized from different subsets of ingredients. Tracking the number of active equivalence classes of needed ingredients from metal \(N\) down to metal \(0\) via Stirling numbers of the second kind \(\left\{\begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix}\right\}\), the exponential generating function \(\widehat{F}(x) = \sum_{n=0}^N f_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\) of valid synthesis plans is given by the composition: \[
\widehat{F}(x) = G(e^x - 1), \qquad \text{where } G(u) = \prod_{k=0}^{N-1} \Big(1 + (A - k) u\Big).
\] Compute \(f_N = [x^N] G(e^x - 1)\) (and simultaneously all \(f_1, \dots, f_N\)) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5\), \(1 \le A \le 10^{18}\) (reduce \(A \bmod 998244353\) first), Time Limit \(3.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 2, A = 2\)):

Falling-factorial polynomial: \(G(u) = \prod_{k=0}^{1} (1 + (2 - k)u) = (1 + 2u)(1 + u) = 1 + 3u + 2u^2\).
Substituting \(u = e^x - 1 = x + \frac{1}{2}x^2 + \dots\): \[G(e^x - 1) = 1 + 3\left(x + \frac{1}{2}x^2 + \dots\right) + 2\left(x^2 + \dots\right) = 1 + 3x + \frac{7}{2}x^2 + O(x^3).\]
Thus \([x^1] G(e^x - 1) = 3\), \([x^2] G(e^x - 1) = \frac{7}{2} \equiv 499122180 \pmod{998244353}\), and \(2! [x^2] G(e^x - 1) = 7\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

Model the synthesis process top-down from metal \(N\) down to metal \(0\). At step \(k \in \{0, 1, \dots, N-1\}\), each new equivalence class of ingredients can be assigned one of \((A - k)\) available base choices, while partitioning \(n\) requests into \(k\) non-empty equivalence classes is governed by the Stirling subset EGF \(\frac{(e^x - 1)^k}{k!}\). How does this express the EGF \(\widehat{F}(x)\) as a composition \(G(e^x - 1)\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Let \(G(u) = \prod_{k=0}^{N-1} (1 + (A - k)u) = \sum_{k=0}^N g_k u^k\), which can be expanded in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time via a binary D&C NTT product tree (Ch 01 / Ch 20). Since \(u(x) = e^x - 1 \in \mathcal{G}_1(\mathbb{F}_p)\) has constant term \(0\) and its compositional inverse is \(u^{\langle -1 \rangle}(y) = \ln(1 + y)\), we can extract \([x^n] G(e^x - 1)\) in two ways (Revisited #12):

Single-\(N\) via Residue Change of Variables (Ch 11): Substitute \(u = e^x - 1 \iff x = \ln(1 + u)\) with \(dx = \frac{du}{1 + u}\).
All-\(n\) (\(1 \le n \le N\)) via Fast Composition (§21.2): Call fps_compose(e^x - 1, G, N + 1) directly!




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Single-\(N\) Extraction (\(O(N \log^2 N)\) tree + \(O(N \log N)\) LIF): \[[x^N] G(e^x - 1) = \operatorname{Res}_x \frac{G(e^x - 1)}{x^{N+1}}\,dx = \operatorname{Res}_u \frac{G(u)}{(\ln(1 + u))^{N+1} (1 + u)}\,du = [u^N] \left( G(u) \left(\frac{u}{\ln(1 + u)}\right)^{N+1} \frac{1}{1 + u} \right).\]
Simultaneous All-\(n\) Extraction (\(O(N \log^2 N)\) via fps_compose): After computing \(G(u) \bmod u^{N+1}\), pass \(F_{\text{inner}}(x) = e^x - 1 \bmod x^{N+1}\) and \(G(u)\) to Kinoshita–Li fps_compose(F_inner, G, N + 1)!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Falling-Factorial Product Tree for \(G(u)\): Reduce \(A \gets A \bmod 998244353\). Build the degree-\(N\) polynomial \[G(u) = \prod_{k=0}^{N-1} \Big(1 + (A - k) u\Big) = \sum_{k=0}^{N} g_k u^k\] using a binary divide-and-conquer NTT product tree in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time (or in \(O(N \log N)\) time by factoring out \(A - k\) and applying a 1D Taylor shift to the falling factorial \(x^{\underline{N}}\)).
Route A — Single-\(N\) Extraction via Lagrange Change of Variables (Ch 11): Since \(u = e^x - 1 \in \mathcal{G}_1(\mathbb{F}_p)\) has compositional inverse \(x = \ln(1 + u) = u \tilde{H}(u)\) with \(\tilde{H}(0) = 1\) and \(dx = \frac{du}{1 + u}\), the Change-of-Variables Theorem (Ch 11) gives: \[[x^N] G(e^x - 1) = \operatorname{Res}_x G(e^x - 1) x^{-N-1}\,dx = \operatorname{Res}_u G(u) (\ln(1 + u))^{-N-1} (1 + u)^{-1}\,du = [u^N] \left( \frac{G(u)}{1 + u} \left(\frac{u}{\ln(1 + u)}\right)^{N+1} \right).\] Computing \(\left(\frac{u}{\ln(1 + u)}\right)^{N+1} \bmod u^{N+1}\) via one fps_ln and fps_exp extracts \([x^N] G(e^x - 1)\) in \(O(N \log N)\) additional time.
Route B — Simultaneous All-\(n\) Extraction via Kinoshita–Li fps_compose (§21.2, Revisited #12): Because \(F_{\text{inner}}(x) = e^x - 1 = \sum_{m=1}^N \frac{x^m}{m!} \bmod x^{N+1}\) satisfies \([x^0] F_{\text{inner}}(x) = 0\), a single call to Kinoshita–Li fps_compose(F_inner, G, N + 1) (§21.2) evaluates \(\widehat{F}(x) = G(e^x - 1) \bmod x^{N+1}\) for all \(0 \le n \le N\) simultaneously in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time!


Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(N \le 2 \times 10^5\) and \(A \le 10^{18}\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N + 1\).
Postconditions (Output): \([x^N] G(e^x - 1) \bmod 998244353\) (and all \([x^n] G(e^x - 1)\) for \(1 \le n \le N\)).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: Under \(u = e^x - 1\), \([x^n] u^k = \frac{k!}{n!} \left\{\begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix}\right\}\), so \([x^n] G(e^x - 1) = \frac{1}{n!} \sum_{k=0}^n g_k k! \left\{\begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix}\right\}\) evaluates the exact Stirling-weighted falling-factorial sum for every \(n \le N\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Reduce \(A \gets A \bmod 998244353\) before forming \((1 + (A - k)u)\) to prevent 64-bit integer overflow; requires \(N + 1 < p\) so that \(m!\) in \(e^x - 1\) and \(\ln(1 + u) \bmod u^{N+2}\) have invertible denominators.









Stepping Stone 2 (#045): AtCoder ABC 345 G — Sugoroku 5

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 345, Problem G | Canonical ID: #045 (SS-2)
Prerequisites: Formal Laurent Residues (Ch 11), Compositional Inverse revert (§21.4) & Fast Composition compose (§21.2).


Problem Statement & Constraints
You are at square \(0\) of a board with squares \(0, 1, \dots, N\). In each step, you roll a fair \(K\)-sided die that advances you by \(j \in \{1, 2, \dots, K\}\) squares with probability \(\frac{1}{K}\) each. Any move that lands on or beyond square \(N\) finishes at square \(N\). For every \(n = 1, 2, \dots, N\), compute the probability that you reach square \(N\) in at most \(n\) steps, modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le K \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), Time Limit \(2.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(p = 998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 3, K = 2\)):

Die step PGF: \(F(x) = \frac{1}{2}(x + x^2)\). We want \(1 - S_n\) where \(S_n = \sum_{i=0}^2 [x^i] F(x)^n\) is the probability of staying at \(< 3\) after \(n\) steps.
\(n = 1\): \(F(x)^1 = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}x^2 \implies S_1 = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} = 1 \implies \text{Ans}_1 = 1 - 1 = 0\).
\(n = 2\): \(F(x)^2 = \frac{1}{4}x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x^3 + \frac{1}{4}x^4 \implies S_2 = \frac{1}{4} \implies \text{Ans}_2 = 1 - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}\).
\(n = 3\): \(F(x)^3 = \frac{1}{8}x^3 + \dots \implies S_3 = 0 \implies \text{Ans}_3 = 1 - 0 = 1\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

Instead of summing the probabilities of first hitting \(\ge N\) at step \(1, 2, \dots, n\), compute the complementary probability \(S_n\) that after \(n\) rolls of the die, your total displacement is still strictly less than \(N\). Express \(S_n\) in terms of the \(n\)-th power of the single-step probability generating function \(F(x) = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{j=1}^K x^j\).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

For each \(n = 1, \dots, N\), \(S_n = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} [x^i] F(x)^n = [x^{N-1}] \frac{F(x)^n}{1 - x}\). We have TWO clean \(O(N \log^2 N)\) ways to compute this for all \(n\) simultaneously:

Direct Power Projection (§21.1): Notice \(S_n = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w_i [x^i] F(x)^n\) with weight vector \(w_i = 1\) for all \(0 \le i < N\)!
Nyaan’s Laurent Residue Trick via revert (§21.4): Write \(S_n = \operatorname{Res}_x \frac{F(x)^n}{x^N(1 - x)}\,dx\) and substitute \(x = G(y) := F^{\langle -1 \rangle}(y)\) so \(F(G(y))^n = y^n\)!




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Under Method 1, one call to power_projection(F, ones, N) returns \(S_0, \dots, S_{N-1}\) directly in \(O(N \log^2 N)\). Under Method 2, since \(F(x) = \frac{x(1 - x^K)}{K(1 - x)}\), its compositional inverse \(G(y) = F^{\langle -1 \rangle}(y) = y \tilde{G}(y)\) satisfies the sparse equation \(G - G^{K+1} - Ky(1 - G) = 0\) (solvable by 1D Newton iteration in \(O(N \log N)\) or fps_revert in \(O(N \log^2 N)\)), and \(S_n = [y^{N-1-n}] \left(\frac{G'(y)}{1 - G(y)} \tilde{G}(y)^{-N}\right)\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Complementary Prefix Sum Formulation: Let \(F(x) = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{j=1}^K x^j = \frac{x(1 - x^K)}{K(1 - x)} \in \mathcal{G}_1(\mathbb{F}_p)\) be the PGF of a single die roll. Since every roll advances by at least \(1\) square, after \(N\) rolls we are guaranteed to be at \(\ge N\) (\(S_N = 0\)). For \(1 \le n \le N - 1\), the probability of remaining at \(< N\) after \(n\) steps is \[S_n = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} [x^i] F(x)^n, \qquad \text{Ans}_n = 1 - S_n \pmod{998244353}.\]
Route 1 (Direct Kinoshita–Li power_projection in \(O(N \log^2 N)\)): Comparing \(S_n = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} 1 \cdot [x^i] F(x)^n\) with the definition of Power Projection (§21.1), we simply set \(\mathbf{w} = (1, 1, \dots, 1)^\top \in \mathbb{F}_p^N\) and call power_projection(F, w, N)! Since \([x^0] F(x) = 0\), no constant-term shift is needed, and the output array gives \(S_0, S_1, \dots, S_{N-1}\) immediately.
Route 2 (Nyaan’s Laurent Geometric Series Trick via revert in \(O(N \log N)\) / \(O(N \log^2 N)\)): Write \(S_n\) as a formal Laurent residue: \[S_n = [x^{N-1}] \frac{F(x)^n}{1 - x} = \operatorname{Res}_x \frac{F(x)^n}{x^N (1 - x)}\,dx.\] Let \(G(y) = F^{\langle -1 \rangle}(y) = y \tilde{G}(y) \in \mathcal{G}_1(\mathbb{F}_p)\) be the compositional inverse of \(F(x)\) (\(\tilde{G}(0) = K \ne 0\)). Substituting \(x = G(y)\) via the Change-of-Variables Theorem (Ch 11) replaces \(F(G(y))^n\) with the pure monomial \(y^n\): \[S_n = \operatorname{Res}_y \frac{y^n}{G(y)^N (1 - G(y))} G'(y)\,dy = \operatorname{Res}_y y^{n - N} \frac{G'(y)}{1 - G(y)} \tilde{G}(y)^{-N}\,dy = [y^{N - 1 - n}] \left( \frac{G'(y)}{1 - G(y)} \tilde{G}(y)^{-N} \right).\] Because \(F(G) = \frac{G(1 - G^K)}{K(1 - G)} = y \iff G - G^{K+1} - Ky(1 - G) = 0\), we can compute \(G(y) \bmod y^{N+1}\) either by calling fps_revert(F, N + 1) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) or via 1D Newton iteration \(G \gets G - \frac{G - G^{K+1} - Ky(1 - G)}{1 - (K+1)G^K + Ky}\) in \(O(N \log N)\), followed by one polynomial power \(\tilde{G}(y)^{-N} \bmod y^N\).


Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(1 \le K \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\); \([x^0]F(x) = 0\) and \([x^1]F(x) = K^{-1} \not\equiv 0 \pmod{998244353}\).
Postconditions (Output): Probabilities \(\text{Ans}_1, \dots, \text{Ans}_N \bmod 998244353\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time via power_projection / fps_revert, or \(O(N \log N)\) time via sparse algebraic Newton + fps_pow, \(O(N)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: For all \(1 \le n < N\), \(S_n = [y^{N-1-n}]\big(\frac{G'(y)}{1-G(y)}\tilde{G}(y)^{-N}\big) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} [x^i] F(x)^n\), and \(S_N = 0\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Because \(F(x) = \frac{x(1 - x^K)}{K(1 - x)}\) has \(F(0) = 0\), the inverse \(G(y)\) has valuation \(1\) and \(G(y)^{-N}\) has a pole of order \(N\) at \(y = 0\); always factor out \(G(y) = y \tilde{G}(y)\) with \(\tilde{G}(0) = K\) before raising \(\tilde{G}(y)\) to the power \(-N\).









Intermediate 1 (#047): AtCoder ABC 387 G — Prime Circuit

Source: AtCoder Beginner Contest 387, Problem G | Canonical ID: #047 (Int-1)
Prerequisites: Block-Cut Tree & Cactus EGF (Ch 12), Lagrange Inversion (Ch 11), Compositional Inverse revert (§21.4).


Problem Statement & Constraints
Count the number of connected simple labeled undirected graphs on \(N\) vertices \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) such that the length of every simple cycle in the graph is a prime number \(p \ge 3\), modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), Time Limit \(2.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 1, 2, 3, 4\)):

\(N = 1\): \(1\) graph (single vertex, no cycles).
\(N = 2\): \(1\) graph (\(K_2\), no cycles).
\(N = 3\): \(3\) trees + \(1\) triangle \(C_3\) (length \(3\) is prime) \(= 4\) valid graphs.
\(N = 4\): \(16\) trees + \(\binom{4}{3} \cdot 1 \cdot 3 = 12\) graphs consisting of a \(C_3\) plus \(1\) pendant edge \(= 28\) valid graphs (note \(C_4\) has composite length \(4\), and two \(C_3\)’s sharing an edge create a \(C_4\)!).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

Can two simple cycles in a valid graph ever share an edge? Suppose two cycles share an edge, forming a theta-graph with three internally disjoint paths of lengths \(a, b, c \ge 1\) between two branch vertices. What are the lengths of the three simple cycles \(a+b, b+c, c+a\), and can all three be odd primes?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Since \((a+b) + (b+c) + (c+a) = 2(a+b+c)\) is even, at least one of \(a+b, b+c, c+a\) must be an even integer \(> 2\), which is composite! Therefore, no two cycles can share an edge: every valid graph is a cactus graph in which every cycle has odd prime length \(p \ge 3\). By the Block-Cut Tree Theorem (Ch 12), what is the fixed-point equation for the vertex-rooted EGF \(T(x)\)?



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

A block incident to the root is either a bridge edge (\(T(x)\)) or a prime cycle \(C_p\) of length \(p \ge 3\) (\(\frac{T(x)^{p-1}}{2}\), since the cycle can be traversed in \(2\) directions repealed by symmetry). Thus \(T(x) = x \exp\!\left(T(x) + \sum_{3 \le p \le N \text{ prime}} \frac{T(x)^{p-1}}{2}\right)\). Extract \([x^N] T(x)\) for a single \(N\) via 1D Lagrange Inversion in \(O(N \log N)\), or for all \(1 \le n \le N\) via fps_revert in \(O(N \log^2 N)\)!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Structural Characterization (Prime-Cycle Cactus Graphs): Any 2-connected component (block) with at least two cycles contains a subdivision of \(K_{2,3}\) (three internally disjoint paths of lengths \(a, b, c \ge 1\) connecting two vertices \(u, v\)). The three cycles have lengths \(a+b, b+c, c+a \ge 3\). Since their sum \(2(a+b+c)\) is even, at least one of the three cycle lengths is even; since \(a, b, c \ge 1\) and the graph is simple, any shared-edge cycle of even length has length \(\ge 4\), which is composite! Hence every block of a valid graph is either:

A single bridge edge \(K_2\) (1 non-root vertex \(\implies\) EGF \(u\)), or
A simple cycle \(C_p\) of odd prime length \(p \ge 3\) (\(p - 1\) non-root vertices arranged in a cycle up to reversal \(\implies\) EGF \(\frac{(p-1)!}{2} \frac{u^{p-1}}{(p-1)!} = \frac{u^{p-1}}{2}\)).

Block-Cut EGF Fixed-Point Equation: Let \(B'(u) := u + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{3 \le p \le N \text{ prime}} u^{p-1}\). By the Fundamental Block-Cut Equation (Ch 12), the vertex-rooted connected EGF \(T(x) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty n c_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\) satisfies \[T(x) = x \exp\!\Big(B'\big(T(x)\big)\Big).\]
Single-\(N\) Extraction (\(O(N \log N)\) via LIF) & All-\(n\) Extraction (\(O(N \log^2 N)\) via revert):

For a single \(N\): By Classical LIF (Ch 11) with \(\Phi(u) = \exp(B'(u))\), \[c_N = \frac{N!}{N} [x^N] T(x) = \frac{(N-1)!}{N} [u^{N-1}] \Phi(u)^N = \frac{(N-1)!}{N} [u^{N-1}] \exp\!\Big(N \cdot B'(u)\Big) \pmod{998244353}.\]
For all \(1 \le n \le N\) simultaneously: Compute \(F(u) := u \exp(-B'(u)) \bmod u^{N+1}\) via one fps_exp, then call fps_revert(F, N + 1) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time (or Logarithmic Newton in \(O(N \log N)\)) to obtain \(T(x) = F^{\langle -1 \rangle}(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\), and read \(c_n = (n-1)! [x^n] T(x)\) for every \(n = 1, \dots, N\).



Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\); linear sieve primes up to \(N\); for \(N = 1\), output \(1\) directly.
Postconditions (Output): Number of connected prime-cycle graphs \(c_N \bmod 998244353\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time (single \(N\) via 1 fps_exp) or \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time (all \(n \le N\) via fps_revert), \(O(N)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: \([u^{k-1}] B'(u)\) equals \(1\) for \(k = 2\), \(\frac{1}{2}\) for odd prime \(k \ge 3\), and \(0\) otherwise, counting unlabeled cyclic arrangements of \(k-1\) child subtrees inside a single block.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Including \(p = 2\) as a cycle length in \(B'(u)\) double-counts bridges (which are \(K_2\) blocks of size \(2\), not cycles, and have symmetry factor \(1\) rather than \(\frac{1}{2}\)); also handle \(N = 1\) separately before dividing by \(N\) in \([u^{N-1}] \exp(N B'(u))\).









Intermediate 2 (#059): AtCoder ARC 137 F — Overlaps

Source: AtCoder Regular Contest 137, Problem F | Canonical ID: #059 (Int-2)
Prerequisites: Implicit Form 4 Monomial Bundling (Ch 11), Riccati ODE (Ch 10), Compositional Inverse revert (§21.4) & Fast Composition compose (§21.2).


Problem Statement & Constraints
In a random chord-diagram overlap process of size \(N\), each irreducible chord block of order \(m \ge 0\) has weight \(g_m\) (where \(G(w) = \sum_{m=0}^N g_m w^m\) with \(g_0 = 1\) satisfies the first-order Riccati differential equation \(G'(w) = (1 + w) G(w)^2\) of irreducible interval blocks) and creates \(2m\) attachment slots for sub-diagrams. Consequently, the ordinary generating function \(F(z) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty f_n z^n\) of total overlap configurations is governed by the Form 4 monomial-bundled implicit functional equation: \[
F(z) = G\!\big(z F(z)^2\big).
\] Given the block series \(G(w) \bmod w^{N+1}\) (with \(g_0 = 1\)) and target degree \(N\), compute all coefficients \(f_0, f_1, \dots, f_N\) of \(F(z) \bmod z^{N+1}\) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(g_0 = 1\), Time Limit \(4.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 2\) with \(G(w) = 1 + w + 2w^2 \bmod w^3\)):

Set \(W(z) = z F(z)^2 \implies W(z) = z G(W(z))^2 = z(1 + 2W + 5W^2 + \dots)\).
Expanding up to \(z^3\): \(W(z) = z + 2z^2 + 9z^3 + O(z^4)\).
Recovering \(F(z) = G(W(z)) = 1 + W(z) + 2 W(z)^2 \equiv 1 + z + 4z^2 \pmod{z^3}\), so \((f_0, f_1, f_2) = (1, 1, 4)\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

Look at the argument inside \(G(\cdot)\) on the right-hand side of \(F(z) = G(z F(z)^2)\): it is the bundled product \(z F(z)^2\), not \(F(z)\) alone. Why can’t you apply standard univariate Lagrange Inversion directly to \(F(z)\), and what auxiliary series \(W(z)\) turns this into a standard Form 1 equation?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Define the bundled series \(W(z) := z F(z)^2 \in z K[[z]]\). Squaring both sides of \(F(z) = G(W(z))\) and multiplying by \(z\) gives \[W(z) = z G\big(W(z)\big)^2 \iff \frac{W(z)}{G(W(z))^2} = z.\] This is a standard compositional inverse equation! Once \(W(z)\) is found, \(F(z) = G(W(z))\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


For all coefficients \(0 \le n \le N\): Compute \(H(w) := \frac{w}{G(w)^2} \bmod w^{N+1}\) in \(O(N \log N)\), invert it via W = fps_revert(H, N + 1) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\), and recover \(F(z) = G(W(z)) \bmod z^{N+1}\) via fps_compose(W, G, N + 1) (or \(\sqrt{W(z)/z}\))!
For a single coefficient \([z^n] F(z)^r\): Apply Form 4 Derivative-Free LIF: \[[z^n] F(z)^r = [z^n] G(W(z))^r = [w^n] \left( G(w)^{2n + r} \left(1 - \frac{2 w G'(w)}{G(w)}\right) \right) = \frac{r}{2n + r} [w^n] G(w)^{2n + r}.\]








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Monomial Bundling Reduction (Form 4 \(\to\) Form 1): In interval overlap and chord diagram problems (authored by Elegia in ARC 137 F), each primitive block of \(m\) chords creates \(2m\) attachment slots for sub-diagrams, yielding \(F(z) = G(z F(z)^2)\) with \(G(0) = 1\). Define \(W(z) := z F(z)^2\). Since \(F(z) = G(W(z))\), squaring and multiplying by \(z\) gives \[W(z) = z G(W(z))^2 \iff H(W(z)) = z, \qquad H(w) := \frac{w}{G(w)^2}.\] Since \(G(0) = 1\), we have \([w^0] H(w) = 0\) and \([w^1] H(w) = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\).
All-Coefficients Pipeline via revert + sqrt / compose (\(O(N \log^2 N)\)):

Step 1: Compute the chord-block series \(G(w) \bmod w^{N+1}\) from its Riccati ODE / EGF recurrence in \(O(N \log N)\) time.
Step 2: Form \(H(w) = w G(w)^{-2} \bmod w^{N+2}\) via one polynomial squaring and inversion (fps_inv).
Step 3: Call W = fps_revert(H, N + 2) (§21.4) to obtain \(W(z) = H^{\langle -1 \rangle}(z) \bmod z^{N+2}\) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time.
Step 4: Recover \(F(z) \bmod z^{N+1}\) either by calling fps_compose(W, G, N + 1) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time, or even faster in \(O(N \log N)\) time by noting \(W(z) / z = F(z)^2\) with \(F(0) = 1\) and taking one polynomial square root \(F(z) = \sqrt{W(z) / z} \bmod z^{N+1}\)!

Single-Coefficient Pipeline via Form 4 LIF (\(O(N \log N)\)): Applying Derivative-Free LIF (Ch 11) to \([z^n] \Psi(W(z))\) with \(\Phi(w) = G(w)^2\) and \(\Psi(w) = G(w)^r\): \[[z^n] F(z)^r = [w^n] \left( G(w)^r \cdot G(w)^{2n} \left(1 - \frac{2 w G'(w)}{G(w)}\right) \right) = \frac{r}{2n + r} [w^n] G(w)^{2n + r},\] evaluated in \(O(N \log N)\) via a single polynomial pow.


Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Series \(G(w) \bmod w^{N+1}\) with \(G(0) = 1 \not\equiv 0 \pmod p\), target degree \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\). Note that the division-free identity \([z^n]F(z)^r = [w^n]G(w)^{2n+r} - 2[w^{n-1}]\big(w G'(w) G(w)^{2n+r-1}\big)\) combined with Route B revert works even when \(p \le 2n + r\).
Postconditions (Output): \(F(z) \bmod z^{N+1}\) satisfying \(F(z) = G(z F(z)^2)\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time for all \(0 \le n \le N\) (or \(O(N \log N)\) for a single \(n\)), \(O(N)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: \(W(z) = z F(z)^2\) satisfies \(W(z) G(W(z))^{-2} = z\), decoupling the quadratic inner argument into a degree-1 compositional inverse.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Because \(F(z) = \sqrt{W(z)/z} \bmod z^{N+1}\) shifts \(W(z)\) down by one degree, \(W(z) = H^{\langle -1 \rangle}(z)\) must be computed modulo \(z^{N+2}\) (length \(N + 2\)) rather than \(z^{N+1}\) if recovering \(F(z)\) via fps_sqrt(W / z); alternatively, recover \(F(z) = G(W(z)) \bmod z^{N+1}\) via fps_compose.









Advanced 1 (#065): AtCoder ARC 154 F — Dice Game

Source: AtCoder Regular Contest 154, Problem F | Canonical ID: #065 (Adv-1)
Prerequisites: Probability Generating Functions (Ch 13), Rational Sum of Simple Fractions / Transposed Multipoint Evaluation (Ch 20), Exponential Composition \(P(e^z)\) (§21.2).


Problem Statement & Constraints
You roll a fair \(N\)-sided die repeatedly until all \(N\) faces have appeared at least once. Let \(T\) be the total number of rolls required. For every integer \(k = 1, 2, \dots, M\), compute the \(k\)-th raw moment \(\mathbb{E}[T^k] \bmod 998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N, M \le 2 \times 10^5\), Time Limit \(4.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 2, M = 2\)):

Waiting time \(T = 1 + G_{1/2}\) where \(G_{1/2}\) is geometric with success probability \(\frac{1}{2}\): \(P(x) = \sum_{t \ge 2} \mathbb{P}(T=t) x^t = x \cdot \frac{\frac{1}{2}x}{1 - \frac{1}{2}x} = \frac{x^2}{2 - x}\).
\(k = 1\): \(\mathbb{E}[T] = 1 + 2 = 3\).
\(k = 2\): \(\mathbb{E}[T^2] = \sum_{t \ge 2} t^2 2^{-(t-1)} = 4(\frac{1}{2}) + 9(\frac{1}{4}) + 16(\frac{1}{8}) + \dots = 11\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

By the standard coupon collector decomposition, when \(i\) distinct faces have already been seen (\(0 \le i \le N-1\)), the number of additional rolls \(T_i\) to see the \((i+1)\)-th new face is a geometric random variable with success probability \(\frac{N - i}{N}\), independent of previous phases. What is the Probability Generating Function \(P(x) = \mathbb{E}[x^T] = \prod_{i=0}^{N-1} \mathbb{E}[x^{T_i}]\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

We have \[P(x) = \prod_{i=0}^{N-1} \frac{\frac{N - i}{N} x}{1 - \frac{i}{N} x} = \frac{\frac{N!}{N^N} x^N}{\prod_{i=1}^{N-1} \left(1 - \frac{i}{N} x\right)} = \frac{A(x)}{B(x)}.\] How do we extract \(\mathbb{E}[T^k]\) for all \(1 \le k \le M\) from \(P(x)\)? Recall that \((x \frac{d}{dx})^k P(x) \big|_{x=1} = \mathbb{E}[T^k]\). Under the exponential change of variables \(x = e^z\), the differential operator \(x \frac{d}{dx}\) becomes \(\frac{d}{dz}\), so the Moment Generating Function is the composition \[P(e^z) = \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \mathbb{P}(T = t) e^{tz} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \mathbb{E}[T^k] \frac{z^k}{k!} = \frac{A(e^z)}{B(e^z)} \pmod{z^{M+1}}.\]



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

First expand \(B(x) = \prod_{i=1}^{N-1} (1 - \frac{i}{N} x) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j x^j\) via a binary D&C NTT product tree in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time. Next, instead of calling general \(O(M \log^2 M)\) fps_compose to evaluate \(B(e^z)\), exploit the exponential structure of \(e^z\): \[B(e^z) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j e^{j z} = \sum_{k=0}^{M} \left( \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j j^k \right) \frac{z^k}{k!},\] where the power sums \(s_k = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j j^k = [z^k] \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \frac{b_j}{1 - j z}\) are computed in \(O((N + M) \log^2(N + M))\) via a single Rational Sum of Simple Fractions (Ch 20)! Finally, compute \(A(e^z) B(e^z)^{-1} \bmod z^{M+1}\).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






PGF of the Coupon Collector Waiting Time: The waiting time \(T = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} T_i\) has PGF \[P(x) = \mathbb{E}[x^T] = \prod_{i=0}^{N-1} \frac{\frac{N - i}{N} x}{1 - \frac{i}{N} x} = \frac{A(x)}{B(x)}, \qquad A(x) := \frac{N!}{N^N} x^N, \quad B(x) := \prod_{i=1}^{N-1} \left(1 - \frac{i}{N} x\right).\]
Moment Generating Function via Exponential Composition \(x = e^z\): Substituting \(x = e^z\) turns \(x^t\) into \(e^{tz} = \sum_{k \ge 0} t^k \frac{z^k}{k!}\), so \[M(z) := P(e^z) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \mathbb{E}[T^k] \frac{z^k}{k!} = \frac{A(e^z)}{B(e^z)}.\] Notice that \(P(1) = 1\), whereas \(B(1) = \prod_{i=1}^{N-1} \left(1 - \frac{i}{N}\right) = \frac{(N-1)!}{N^{N-1}} \ne 0\) in \(\mathbb{F}_{998244353}\) (since \(N < 998244353\)). Thus \(B(e^z)\) has non-zero constant term \([z^0] B(e^z) = B(1) \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) and is directly invertible in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[z]] / (z^{M+1})\)!
Fast Evaluation of \(A(e^z)\) and \(B(e^z) \bmod z^{M+1}\):

Step 1: Multiply the \(N - 1\) linear factors of \(B(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j x^j\) using a D&C NTT product tree in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time.
Step 2: For any polynomial \(B(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j x^j\), its composition with \(e^z\) satisfies \[k! [z^k] B(e^z) = \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} b_j j^k = [z^k] \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \frac{b_j}{1 - j z} \qquad (0 \le k \le M).\] Summing the \(N\) simple fractions \(\frac{b_j}{1 - jz} = \frac{\mathcal{P}(z)}{\mathcal{Q}(z)}\) via a binary D&C NTT tree (Ch 20) and one polynomial inversion \(\mathcal{P}(z) \mathcal{Q}(z)^{-1} \bmod z^{M+1}\) yields all coefficients of \(B(e^z) \bmod z^{M+1}\) in \(O(N \log^2 N + M \log M)\) time. (Alternatively, shift \(B(x)\) to \(B(1 + y)\) via a 1D Taylor shift and compose with \(y = e^z - 1\) via Kinoshita–Li fps_compose in \(O((N + M) \log^2(N + M))\) time.)
Step 3: Since \(A(e^z) = \frac{N!}{N^N} e^{Nz} = \frac{N!}{N^N} \sum_{k=0}^M \frac{N^k}{k!} z^k\), compute \(M(z) = A(e^z) B(e^z)^{-1} \bmod z^{M+1}\) via one fps_inv and convolution, and output \(\mathbb{E}[T^k] = k! [z^k] M(z) \bmod 998244353\) for \(1 \le k \le M\).



Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(1 \le N, M \le 2 \times 10^5\) with \(N, M < p = 998244353\) so that \(B(1) = \frac{(N-1)!}{N^{N-1}} \not\equiv 0 \pmod p\) and \(k!\) is invertible.
Postconditions (Output): Moments \(\mathbb{E}[T^1], \dots, \mathbb{E}[T^M] \bmod 998244353\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O((N + M) \log^2(N + M))\) time and \(O(N + M)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: The Laplace-to-OGF bridge \(k!\,[z^k] B(e^z) = [z^k] \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \frac{b_j}{1 - jz}\) replaces general series composition with a rational sum of simple fractions.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Notice that \(1 - x\) is cancelled between numerator and denominator when forming \(B(x) = \prod_{i=1}^{N-1} (1 - \frac{i}{N}x)\) (since the \(i = 0\) factor \(\frac{N}{N}x = x\) has no denominator and the \(1 - x\) from geometric sums is already absorbed); failing to cancel \((1 - x)\) before substituting \(x = e^z\) makes the denominator vanish at \(z = 0\)!









Advanced 2 (#218): LibreOJ 171 / QOJ 6504 — 幂投影 (Power Projection & Transposed Implicit Tree Sums)

Source: LibreOJ 171 / QOJ 6504 — 幂投影 (Power Projection) | Canonical ID: #218 (Adv-2)
Prerequisites: Kinoshita–Li 2D Bostan–Mori Power Projection (§21.1), Bivariate Generating Function Duality (Ch 10), Flat 1D Kronecker NTT Packing (§21.1).


Problem Statement & Constraints
You are given a formal power series \(F(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} f_i x^i \in \mathbb{F}_{998244353}[[x]]\) (not necessarily having \(f_0 = 0\)) and a linear-functional weight vector \(w_0, w_1, \dots, w_{N-1} \in \mathbb{F}_{998244353}\). Compute the Power Projection sequence \(p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{M-1}\) defined by: \[
p_k = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w_i \, [x^i] F(x)^k \pmod{998244353} \qquad \text{for all } k = 0, 1, \dots, M - 1.
\]

Constraints: \(1 \le N, M \le 2 \times 10^5\), \(0 \le f_i, w_i < 998244353\), Time Limit \(2.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(p = 998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 3, M = 3, F(x) = 1 + 2x + 3x^2, \mathbf{w} = (1, 1, 1)\)):

\(k = 0\): \(F(x)^0 = 1 \implies p_0 = w_0(1) = 1\).
\(k = 1\): \(F(x)^1 = 1 + 2x + 3x^2 \implies p_1 = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6\).
\(k = 2\): \(F(x)^2 \equiv 1 + 4x + 10x^2 \pmod{x^3} \implies p_2 = 1 + 4 + 10 = 15\).
Constant-Term Split Verification (\(c = f_0 = 1, \tilde{F}(x) = 2x + 3x^2\)): First compute \(\tilde{p}_j = \sum_{i=0}^2 w_i [x^i] \tilde{F}(x)^j\) for \(j = 0, 1, 2\): \(\tilde{p}_0 = 1\), \(\tilde{p}_1 = 2 + 3 = 5\), \(\tilde{p}_2 = 4\). Then binomial convolution \(p_k = \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j} c^{k-j} \tilde{p}_j\) gives \(p_0 = 1\), \(p_1 = 1(1) + 1(5) = 6\), \(p_2 = 1(1) + 2(5) + 1(4) = 15\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

Notice that \(F(x) = c + \tilde{F}(x)\) may have a non-zero constant term \(c = [x^0] F(x) \ne 0\), in which case \(\frac{1}{1 - y F(x)}\) is not a well-defined formal power series in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x, y]]\). How can you reduce the general case \(f_0 = c \ne 0\) to the nilpotent case \(\tilde{F}(0) = 0\) using a single 1D EGF convolution?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Write \(F(x) = c + \tilde{F}(x)\) where \(\tilde{F}(0) = 0\). By the Binomial Theorem, \(F(x)^k = \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j} c^{k-j} \tilde{F}(x)^j\). By linearity of the functional \(\langle \mathbf{w}, \cdot \rangle\): \[
p_k = \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j} c^{k-j} \tilde{p}_j \iff \frac{p_k}{k!} = \sum_{j=0}^k \frac{c^{k-j}}{(k-j)!} \cdot \frac{\tilde{p}_j}{j!},
\] where \(\tilde{p}_j = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w_i [x^i] \tilde{F}(x)^j\) has \(\tilde{F}(0) = 0\) and vanishes for all \(j \ge N\)!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Strip \(c = f_0\) and set \(\tilde{F}(x) = F(x) - c\) so \([x^0]\tilde{F}(x) = 0\).
Run Kinoshita–Li 2D Bostan–Mori power_projection (§21.1) on \((\tilde{F}, \mathbf{w})\) to obtain \(\tilde{p}_0, \dots, \tilde{p}_{\min(N, M)-1}\) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time: at each of the \(\lceil \log_2 N \rceil\) rounds, multiply \(P^{(r)}(x, y)\) and \(Q^{(r)}(x, y)\) by \(Q^{(r)}(-x, y)\) using 1D Kronecker-packed NTTs of length \(4 N\) and the DFT frequency-block swap identity (Lemma 21.2).
If \(c \ne 0\), convolve \(\frac{\tilde{p}_j}{j!}\) with \(\frac{c^r}{r!}\) up to degree \(M - 1\) in \(O(M \log M)\) time!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Decoupling the Constant Term \(c = [x^0] F(x)\): Let \(c = f_0\) and \(\tilde{F}(x) = F(x) - c \in x \mathbb{F}_p[[x]]\). Since \(\tilde{F}(x)^j\) has valuation \(\ge j\), \([x^i] \tilde{F}(x)^j = 0\) for all \(j > i\), so \(\tilde{p}_j := \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w_i [x^i] \tilde{F}(x)^j = 0\) for all \(j \ge N\). Once \(\tilde{p}_0, \dots, \tilde{p}_{\min(N, M)-1}\) are computed, expanding \((c + \tilde{F}(x))^k\) gives: \[
p_k = k! [z^k] \left( e^{cz} \sum_{j=0}^{\min(N, M)-1} \frac{\tilde{p}_j}{j!} z^j \right) \qquad (0 \le k < M),
\] which is a single 1D NTT convolution of length \(M\).
Kinoshita–Li 2D Bostan–Mori Recursion for \(\tilde{p}_0, \dots, \tilde{p}_{N-1}\) (§21.1): Pad \(N\) to a power of \(2\) so that \(n = N - 1\) has binary expansion \(11\dots1_2\) (every bit of \(n\) is \(1\)). Initialize: \[
P^{(0)}(x, y) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} w_i x^{n - i}, \qquad Q^{(0)}(x, y) = 1 - y \tilde{F}(x) \pmod{x^{n+1}},
\] so that \(\sum_{j=0}^{n} \tilde{p}_j y^j = [x^n] \frac{P^{(0)}(x, y)}{Q^{(0)}(x, y)} \bmod y^{n+1}\). In round \(r = 0, 1, \dots, \log_2 N - 1\), let \(d_x = N / 2^r - 1\) and \(d_y = 2^r\). Pack \(P^{(r)}\) and \(Q^{(r)}\) into 1D arrays of stride \(S = 2^{r+1}\) in \(y\) (Lemma 21.1), execute one forward NTT of length \(L = 4N\) on each, obtain \(\operatorname{DFT}(Q^{(r)}(-x, y))\) in \(O(N)\) time by swapping the lower and upper frequency halves (Lemma 21.2), multiply pointwise, and apply one inverse NTT to extract: \[
P^{(r+1)}(x, y) = \mathcal{E}_1\!\big(P^{(r)}(x, y) Q^{(r)}(-x, y)\big) \bmod y^{2^{r+1}}, \qquad Q^{(r+1)}(x, y) = \mathcal{E}_0\!\big(Q^{(r)}(x, y) Q^{(r)}(-x, y)\big) \bmod y^{2^{r+1}}.
\] After \(\log_2 N\) rounds, \(P^{(\log_2 N)}(0, y) Q^{(\log_2 N)}(0, y)^{-1} \bmod y^N\) yields \(\tilde{p}_0, \dots, \tilde{p}_{N-1}\) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time!


Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Series \(F(x) \bmod x^N\), weight vector \(\mathbf{w} \in \mathbb{F}_p^N\), target length \(M \le 2 \times 10^5\) (\(N, M \ge 1\)); pad \(N\) to the next power of \(2\) before running the 2D Bostan–Mori loop.
Postconditions (Output): Power projection values \(p_0, p_1, \dots, p_{M-1} \bmod 998244353\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N + M \log M)\) time (\(\approx 2 \log_2 N\) NTTs of size \(4N\)) and \(O(N + M)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: After round \(r\), \(\deg_x P^{(r)}, \deg_x Q^{(r)} < N / 2^r\) and \(\deg_y P^{(r)}, \deg_y Q^{(r)} \le 2^r\), preserving \([x^{N/2^r - 1}] \frac{P^{(r)}(x, y)}{Q^{(r)}(x, y)} \equiv \sum_{j=0}^{2^r - 1} \tilde{p}_j y^j \pmod{y^{2^r}}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Calling 2D Bostan–Mori directly on \(F(x)\) when \(c = [x^0] F(x) \ne 0\) corrupts \([y^0] Q^{(0)}(x, y) = 1 - c y \ne 1\); always strip \(c = f_0\) first, run power_projection on \(\tilde{F}(x) = F(x) - c\), and restore \(c\) via EGF binomial convolution with \(e^{cz}\).









Mastery 1 (#235): QOJ 8528 — Polynomial Composition (fps_compose via Tellegen Transposition)

Source: QOJ 8528 — Polynomial Composition | Canonical ID: #235 (Mas-1)
Prerequisites: Kinoshita–Li 2D Bostan–Mori (§21.1), Tellegen’s Transposition Principle (Ch 20 & §21.2), Taylor Shift (Ch 05).


Problem Statement & Constraints
You are given two dense formal power series \(F(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} f_i x^i\) and \(G(y) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} g_k y^k\) over \(\mathbb{F}_{998244353}\) of degree \(< N\), where \(f_0 = [x^0] F(x)\) is arbitrary (if \(f_0 \ne 0\), \(G(y)\) is treated as a degree-\((N-1)\) polynomial in \(\mathbb{F}_{998244353}[y]\)). Compute the composite formal power series \[
H(x) = G\big(F(x)\big) \bmod x^N = \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} h_i x^i \pmod{998244353}.
\]

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2 \times 10^5\), \(0 \le f_i, g_k < 998244353\), Time Limit \(2.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(p = 998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 3, F(x) = 1 + 2x + 3x^2, G(y) = 2 + y + y^2\)):

Step 1 (Taylor Shift for \(c = f_0 = 1\)): Shift \(\tilde{G}(y) = G(y + 1) = 2 + (y + 1) + (y + 1)^2 = 4 + 3y + y^2\), and strip \(\tilde{F}(x) = F(x) - 1 = 2x + 3x^2\).
Step 2 (Nilpotent Composition \(\tilde{G}(\tilde{F}(x)) \bmod x^3\)): \[\tilde{G}(\tilde{F}(x)) = 4 + 3(2x + 3x^2) + (2x + 3x^2)^2 \equiv 4 + 6x + 13x^2 \pmod{x^3}.\]




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

At \(N = 2 \times 10^5\), why does Brent–Kung’s \(O((N \log N)^{3/2} + N^2)\) baby-step giant-step algorithm exceed the time limit, and how do you preprocess \(F(x)\) and \(G(y)\) when \(c = [x^0] F(x) \ne 0\) so that the inner series has zero constant term?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Since \(G(y)\) is a polynomial of degree \(< N\), \(G(F(x)) = G(c + (F(x) - c)) = \tilde{G}(\tilde{F}(x))\) where \(\tilde{G}(y) = G(y + c)\) is computed by a single 1D Polynomial Taylor Shift (Ch 06 / Ch 20) in \(O(N \log N)\) time, and \(\tilde{F}(x) = F(x) - c\) has \([x^0] \tilde{F} = 0\). Now apply the Kinoshita–Li forward and backward passes (§21.1–§21.2) on \(\tilde{F}(x)\) and \(\tilde{G}(y)\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Pack a 2D polynomial \(A(x, y)\) with \(\deg_x < L_x\) and \(\deg_y \le L_y\) into a 1D array of length \(4 L_x L_y = 4N\) using Kronecker stride \(2 L_y\) (index(i, j) = i * (2 * Ly) + j). In the forward pass, use Nachia’s frequency half-swap (k_x ^ Lx) to compute \(Q_{t+1}(x, y)\) in only two 1D NTTs of length \(4N\) (or 2D NTTs of size \(2L_x \times 2L_y\)) per level; in the backward pass, transpose each step via mulT in the same number of NTTs.







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Constant-Term Reduction via Taylor Shift: Let \(c = [x^0] F(x)\). Even when \(c \ne 0\), because \(G(y) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} g_k y^k\) is a finite polynomial of degree \(< N\), the substitution \(G(F(x)) \bmod x^N\) is well-defined over \(\mathbb{F}_p\). Setting \(\tilde{F}(x) := F(x) - c\) (so \([x^0] \tilde{F}(x) = 0\)) and \(\tilde{G}(y) := G(y + c) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} \tilde{g}_k y^k\) where \[\tilde{g}_k = \frac{1}{k!} \sum_{j=k}^{N-1} (j! g_j) \frac{c^{j-k}}{(j - k)!}\] is evaluated via one 1D Middle Product (mulT) in \(O(N \log N)\) time, we have \(G(F(x)) \equiv \tilde{G}(\tilde{F}(x)) \pmod{x^N}\).
Kronecker-Packed 2D Bostan–Mori Forward Pass (\(t = 0 \to m - 1\)): Pad \(N\) up to \(2^m\). At level \(t\), \(L_x = 2^{m-t}\) and \(L_y = 2^t\), so \(L_x L_y = N\). Represent \(Q_t(x, y)\) (\(\deg_x < L_x, \deg_y \le L_y\)) in a flat array of dimensions \(2 L_x \times 2 L_y\) (total size \(4N\)):

Apply a forward 2D NTT of dimensions \(2 L_x \times 2 L_y\) to \(Q_t(x, y)\).
By Nachia’s optimization (§21.1), the 2D NTT of \(Q_t(-x, y)\) is \(\widehat{Q_t}[r_x \oplus L_x, r_y]\).
Store \(\widehat{Q_t(-x, y)}\) for the backward pass, multiply \(\widehat{Q_t}[r_x, r_y] \cdot \widehat{Q_t}[r_x \oplus L_x, r_y]\), and run the inverse 2D NTT to extract the even \(x\)-powers \(\mathcal{S}_0\) truncated to \(\deg_x < L_x / 2, \deg_y \le 2 L_y\), yielding \(Q_{t+1}(x, y)\).

Transposed 2D Bostan–Mori Backward Pass (\(t = m - 1 \downarrow 0\)): Initialize \(\hat{P}_m(0, y) = \tilde{G}(y)\) (\(L_x = 1, L_y = N\)). For \(t = m - 1\) down to \(0\) (\(L_x = 2^{m-t}, L_y = 2^t\)):

Interleave zeros at even \(x\)-indices: \(\hat{U}_t(x, y) = x \hat{P}_{t+1}(x^2, y)\) (\(\deg_x < L_x, \deg_y < 2 L_y\)).
Compute \(\hat{P}_t(x, y) = \operatorname{mulT}_{x, y}\big(\hat{U}_t(x, y), Q_t(-x, y)\big) \bmod (x^{L_x}, y^{L_y})\) by reversing the active \((x, y)\) indices of \(\hat{U}_t\) (or multiplying by the frequency-reversed DFT of \(Q_t(-x, y)\) cached from the forward pass!) and running one forward + one inverse 2D NTT of size \(2 L_x \times 2 L_y\).
At \(t = 0\), output \(h_i = [x^{N-1-i} y^0] \hat{P}_0(x, y)\) for \(0 \le i < N\).



Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Dense polynomials \(F(x), G(y) \in \mathbb{F}_{998244353}[x] / (x^N)\) with \(N \le 2 \times 10^5\). If \([x^0]F \ne 0\), requires \(N < p\) for the factorial Taylor shift \(G(y + c)\); if \([x^0]F = 0\), requires only \(2 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\).
Postconditions (Output): \(H(x) = G(F(x)) \bmod x^N\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time (\(\approx 300\text{ ms}\) at \(N = 2 \times 10^5\)) and \(O(N \log N)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At level \(t\), the 2D FFT grid size is \(2 L_x \times 2 L_y = 2^{m-t+1} \times 2^{t+1} = 4N\), which is strictly constant across all \(\log_2 N\) levels.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: Packing the 2D array \((i, j)\) with Kronecker stride \(L_y\) instead of \(2 L_y\) causes cyclic wrap-around in the \(y\)-variable during 1D NTT multiplication (Failure Mode #1); also, if \(c = [x^0] F(x) \ne 0\), you must Taylor-shift \(G(y) \mapsto G(y + c)\) before calling the nilpotent Kinoshita–Li kernel.









Mastery 2 (#017): AtCoder fps_24_x — Functional Square Root (関数的平方根)

Source: AtCoder FPS 24: 24 Problems on Formal Power Series — Problem X | Canonical ID: #017 (Mas-2)
Prerequisites: Functional Square Roots & Artin–Schreier Obstruction (§21.4), Kinoshita–Li compose (§21.2), Linear First-Order Compositional Perturbation (Ch 09).


Problem Statement & Constraints
Given a formal power series \(F(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} f_k x^k \in \mathbb{F}_{998244353}[[x]] / (x^N)\) with \(f_0 = 0\) and \(f_1 = 1\) (or general \(f_0, f_1\)), find a formal power series \(G(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{N-1} g_k x^k \in \mathbb{F}_{998244353}[[x]] / (x^N)\) such that \[G(G(x)) \equiv F(x) \pmod{x^N},\] or report that no such series exists.

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 8000\) (solvable in \(O(N^2)\) via indeterminate extraction or in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) up to \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\) via Newton + Kinoshita–Li compose), Time Limit \(2.0\text{ s}\), Modulo \(p = 998244353\).
Sample Trace (\(N = 4, F(x) = x + 2x^2 + 5x^3\)):

Set \(G(x) = x + g_2 x^2 + g_3 x^3\).
\(G(G(x)) = (x + g_2 x^2 + g_3 x^3) + g_2(x + g_2 x^2)^2 + g_3 x^3 \equiv x + 2 g_2 x^2 + (2 g_2^2 + 2 g_3) x^3 \pmod{x^4}\).
Matching \([x^2]\): \(2 g_2 = 2 \implies g_2 = 1\).
Matching \([x^3]\): \(2(1)^2 + 2 g_3 = 5 \implies g_3 = \frac{3}{2} \equiv 499122178 \pmod{998244353}\).




Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model (Spoiler-Free)

Suppose \(G(x) = g_1 x + g_2 x^2 + \dots\) satisfies \(G(G(x)) \equiv F(x) \pmod{x^N}\) where \(F(x) = x + f_2 x^2 + \dots\) is tangent to the identity (\(f_0 = 0, f_1 = 1\), choosing \(g_1 = 1\)). Expand \(G(G(x))\) when \(G(x) = G_s(x) + \Delta(x)\) with \(\operatorname{val}_x(\Delta) \ge 2^s\). Why do BOTH \(G_s'(\cdot) \Delta(x)\) and \(\Delta(G_s(x))\) survive modulo \(x^{2^{s+1}}\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

When \(G_{s+1}(x) = G_s(x) + \Delta(x)\) with \(\Delta(x) \equiv 0 \pmod{x^L}\) (\(L = 2^s\)), applying Taylor expansion to the outer \(G\) and substituting \(G_s + \Delta\) inside gives: \[G_{s+1}(G_{s+1}(x)) = (G_s + \Delta)(G_s(x) + \Delta(x)) \equiv G_s(G_s(x)) + G_s'(G_s(x)) \Delta(x) + \Delta(G_s(x)) \pmod{x^{2L}}.\] How do we simplify \(\Delta(G_s(x)) \bmod x^{2L}\) when \(\operatorname{val}_x(\Delta) \ge L\) and \(G_s(x) = x + g_2 x^2 + \dots\) has leading term \(1 \cdot x\)?



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Look at \(\Delta(G_s(x))\) when \(\Delta(x) = x^L \tilde{\Delta}(x)\) and \(G_s(x) = x \tilde{G}_s(x)\) with \(\tilde{G}_s(0) = 1\): \[\Delta(G_s(x)) = G_s(x)^L \tilde{\Delta}(G_s(x)).\] Because \(G_s(x) = x + O(x^2)\), we have \(\tilde{\Delta}(G_s(x)) \equiv \tilde{\Delta}(x) \pmod{x^L}\)? Not quite—for general \(\tilde{\Delta}\) we use the conjugation trick or observe that if we write \(G_s(x)\) via Schröder/Abel coordinates (or for \(g_1 = 1\), notice that \(G_s'(x) \Delta(x) = \Delta(G_s(x))\) after dividing by the Lie generator \(A(x)\) of the flow \(G_s\))! Specifically, let \(A_s(x)\) satisfy \(A_s(G_s(x)) = G_s'(x) A_s(x) \bmod x^L\) (the infinitesimal generator / Julia equation). Or for \(N \le p\): by Theorem 7.2 (§21.4), \(G(x) \equiv F^{\circ ((p+1)/2)}(x) \pmod{x^{p+1}}\)!







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






Classification of Degree-\(0\) and Degree-\(1\) Coefficients: If \([x^0] F(x) = 0\):

Case A (\(f_1 = 1\), Tangent to Identity): Choose \(g_1 = 1\). As proved in §21.4, for every \(k \ge 2\), the degree-\(k\) coefficient equation is \[2 g_k = f_k - [x^k] \sum_{m=2}^{k-1} g_m G_{<k}(x)^m,\] which has a unique solution in \(\mathbb{F}_p\) for every odd prime \(p\).
Case B (\(f_1 \not\equiv 0, 1 \pmod p\)): Check whether \(f_1\) is a quadratic residue modulo \(p\) via Tonelli–Shanks / Cipolla (\(g_1^2 \equiv f_1 \pmod p\)). If so, test both roots \(\pm g_1\): at each degree \(k \ge 2\), \(g_1(1 + g_1^{k-1}) g_k = \text{RHS}_k\).
Case C (\(f_1 = 0\)): If \(F(x) \equiv 0 \pmod{x^N}\), then \(G(x) = 0\) works; otherwise, let \(v = \operatorname{val}_x(F) \ge 2\). Since \(\operatorname{val}_x(G \circ G) = (\operatorname{val}_x G)^2\), no solution can exist unless \(v = d^2\) is a perfect square (or \(v \ge N\), in which case \(G(x) = c x^{\lceil \sqrt{N} \rceil}\) has \(G(G(x)) \equiv 0 \pmod{x^N}\)).

Method 1 — \(O(N^2)\) Indeterminate Extraction / Online Relaxed Convolution (for \(N \le 8000\)): Maintain the powers \(G(x)^2, G(x)^3, \dots, G(x)^{N-1} \bmod x^N\) incrementally: as soon as \(g_k\) is solved from \(g_1(1 + g_1^{k-1}) g_k = f_k - [x^k] \sum_{m=2}^{k-1} g_m G(x)^m\), update \([x^j] G(x)^m\) for \(m \le j \le N-1\), running in \(O(N^2)\) operations (\(\approx 15\text{ ms}\) for \(N = 8000\)).
Method 2 — \(O(N \log^2 N)\) Newton / Lie-Flow Iteration via Kinoshita–Li compose (for \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5, p > N\)): When \(f_0 = 0, f_1 = 1\) and \(\operatorname{char}(K) = 0\) or \(p > N\), every tangent-to-identity series \(F(x) = x + f_2 x^2 + \dots \in \mathcal{G}_{1,1}(K)\) is the time-\(1\) flow \(\exp(v(x) \frac{d}{dx})(x)\) of a unique formal vector field \(v(x) \frac{d}{dx}\) (\(v(x) = v_2 x^2 + v_3 x^3 + \dots\)), and its functional square root \(G(x)\) is the time-\(\frac{1}{2}\) flow \(\exp(\frac{1}{2} v(x) \frac{d}{dx})(x)\)! Even better, in Newton’s method \(G_{s+1} = G_s + \Delta\) (\(\Delta \equiv 0 \pmod{x^L}, L = 2^s\)), the linearized equation is \[G_s'(G_s(x)) \Delta(x) + \Delta(G_s(x)) \equiv F(x) - G_s(G_s(x)) \pmod{x^{2L}}.\] Because \(\Delta(x) = \delta_L x^L + \dots + \delta_{2L-1} x^{2L-1}\) has valuation \(\ge L\) and \((G_s(x))^k = x^k (G_s(x)/x)^k\) has a \(k\)-dependent exponent across \(L \le k < 2L\), we factor \(\Delta(x) = A_s(x) U(x)\) where \(U(x) \equiv 0 \pmod{x^L}\) and \(A_s(x)\) is the Julia / Lie generator satisfying \(A_s(G_s(x)) = G_s'(x) A_s(x)\). Equivalently, parameterizing \(F(x) = \Psi^{\langle -1 \rangle}(\Psi(x) + 1)\) via Abel’s equation \(\Psi(F(x)) = \Psi(x) + 1\) (solved by Newton iteration + Kinoshita–Li compose) yields \(G(x) = \Psi^{\langle -1 \rangle}\!\big(\Psi(x) + \frac{1}{2}\big) \bmod x^N\) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time!


Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: \(F(x) \in \mathbb{F}_p[[x]]/(x^N)\) (\(N \le 8000\) for \(O(N^2)\) all-case solver; \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\) for \(O(N \log^2 N)\) tangent-to-identity solver); odd prime \(p = 998244353\) (\(2 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\)).
Postconditions (Output): \(G(x) \bmod x^N\) satisfying \(G(G(x)) \equiv F(x) \pmod{x^N}\), or -1 if none exists.
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N^2)\) time for general \(f_0, f_1\) at \(N \le 8000\); \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time for tangent-to-identity \(F(x) = x + \dots\) at \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(O(N)\) space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At each degree \(k \ge 2\), \([x^k] G(G(x)) = g_1(1 + g_1^{k-1}) g_k + [x^k] \sum_{m=2}^{k-1} g_m G_{<k}(x)^m\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases: When \(g_1 \ne 1\), if \(g_1^{k-1} \equiv -1 \pmod p\) at some degree \(k \ge 2\), the leading coefficient \(g_1(1 + g_1^{k-1}) \equiv 0 \pmod p\) vanishes (resonance); if the right-hand side is non-zero at that \(k\), no solution exists for that branch of \(g_1\), so both square roots \(\pm \sqrt{f_1} \bmod p\) must be tested.

text:
21.6 Diagnostic Signals, Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad, Pre-Submission Checklist & Historical Notes

Summary Table of Diagnostic Signals









Structural Feature in Problem
Diagnostic Signal
Target Operator / Reduction
Time Complexity




Linear functional \(\sum_{i=0}^{N-1} w_i [x^i] F(x)^k\) needed for all \(0 \le k < N\)
Matrix-vector product \(M_F^\top \mathbf{w}\)
Kinoshita–Li power_projection on \([x^{N-1}] \frac{\sum w_i x^{N-1-i}}{1 - y F(x)} \bmod y^N\) (§21.1)
\(O(N \log^2 N)\)


Composite series \(H(x) = G(F(x)) \bmod x^N\) for dense \(F, G\)
Matrix-vector product \(M_F \mathbf{g} = (M_F^\top)^\top \mathbf{g}\)
Kinoshita–Li fps_compose via Tellegen transpose of power_projection (§21.2)
\(O(N \log^2 N)\) (all \(p \ne 2\) when \(F(0)=0\))


Coupled binomial sum \(S_n = \sum_{k=0}^n f_k \binom{\alpha n + \beta k + \gamma}{n - k}\) for all \(n \le N\)
Both \(n\) and \(k\) appear linearly in upper index
Elegia’s Linearization (Theorem 21.1): \(z = u(1+u)^{-\alpha} \iff u = A(z)\), 1 call to fps_compose (§21.3)
\(O(N \log^2 N)\)


Compositional inverse \(G = F^{\langle -1 \rangle} \bmod y^N\) when \(p > N\)
\([x^0]F = 0, [x^1]F \in K^\times, p > N\)
Route A (noshi91 LIF + Power Projection): \([y^{n-k}](G/y)^{-n} = \frac{n}{k}[x^n]F(x)^k\) + pow(-1/n) (§21.4)
\(O(N \log^2 N)\)


Compositional inverse \(G = F^{\langle -1 \rangle} \bmod y^N\) when \(p \le N\)
Small prime \(p \le N\) (\(\frac{n}{k}\) and pow crash!)
Route B (Newton + fps_compose): \(G_{s+1} = G_s - \frac{F(G_s)-y}{F'(G_s)} \bmod y^{2^{s+1}}\) (§21.4)
\(O(N \log^2 N)\) (all \(p \ne 2\))


Functional square root \(G(G(x)) \equiv F(x) \pmod{x^N}\) (\(F(x) = x + \dots\))
Tangent-to-identity iterative composition
Degree-by-degree \(2 g_k = \dots\), or \(F^{\circ((p+1)/2)}(x)\) when \(N \le p+1\), or Newton + compose (§21.4)
\(O(N^2)\) or \(O(N \log^2 N)\)





Pre-Submission Checklist for Chapter 21 Problems

Constant-Term Check (\([x^0] F(x) = 0\)):

In power_projection, if \(c = [x^0] F(x) \ne 0\), did you strip \(c\) upfront and apply the binomial shift \(\sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j} c^{k-j} \widetilde{\text{proj}}_j\), or invert \(Q_m(0, y) = (1 - cy)^{2^m} \bmod y^N\) at the bottom of the recursion?
In fps_compose, if \(c = [x^0] F(x) \ne 0\), did you apply a 1D Polynomial Taylor Shift \(G(y) \gets G(y + c)\) before calling the \(F(0) = 0\) kernel?
In fps_revert, is \([x^0] F(x) = 0\) and \([x^1] F(x) \in K^\times\)?

Power-of-Two Padding (\(N = 2^m\)):

Did you pad \(N\) to a power of two \(2^m\) before setting \(n_0 = 2^m - 1\)? If \(N\) is not a power of two, \(n_t = \lfloor (N-1)/2^t \rfloor\) can be even (\(b_t = 0\)) at some levels \(t\), so you must branch on \(b_t = n_t \bmod 2\) in both the forward extraction \(\mathcal{S}_{b_t}\) and backward zero-interleaving \(x^{b_t} \hat{P}_{t+1}(x^2, y)\).

Characteristic-\(p\) Safety (\(p \le N\) vs. \(p > N\)):

If the prime modulus \(p \le N\), did you use Route B (revert_newton_compose) instead of Route A (revert_lif_proj), avoiding all divisions by \(1, 2, \dots, N-1\)?




Historical & Pedagogical Notes

From Brent–Kung (1978) to Kinoshita–Li (FOCS 2024): R. P. Brent and H. T. Kung (Fast Algorithms for Manipulating Formal Power Series, JACM 1978) established the \(O((N \log N)^{3/2})\) baby-step giant-step algorithm for composition and inversion, as well as the duality between composition and power projection via the transposition principle. While Kedlaya and Umans (FOCS 2008 / SICOMP 2011) achieved theoretical \(N^{1 + o(1)}\) algebraic complexity over finite fields via multimodular reduction, no quasi-linear algebraic algorithm (using only ring/field operations) was known until Yasunori Kinoshita (noshi91) and Baitian Li (Elegia / EI) published Power Projection and Composition of Formal Power Series in \(O(n \log^2 n)\) Operations at FOCS 2024.
Competitive Programming Optimizations (noshi91 & Nachia, 2024): Within days of the preprint’s release, Nachia introduced the frequency-domain half-swap optimization (k_x ^ Lx), reducing the 2D FFT count per level from \(5\) to \(3\) (and \(2\) in the denominator tree), making Kinoshita–Li compose faster than Brent–Kung for all \(N \ge 2048\).
Curriculum Reference Registry & Verification Benchmarks (R-32, R-33, R-34, R-35): The Kinoshita–Li \(O(N \log^2 N)\) algorithms in this chapter correspond to R-32 (Kinoshita and Li (FOCS 2024) — Power Projection and Composition of Formal Power Series in \(O(n \log^2 n)\) Operations) and R-33 (noshi91 & Nachia (2024) — \(O(N \log^2 N)\) FPS Composition and Compositional Inverse Blog Notes), and can be unit-tested on the Library Checker benchmarks R-34 (composition_of_formal_power_series_large) and R-35 (compositional_inverse_of_formal_power_series_large).




Where to Go Next

Proceed to Checkpoint V: Part V Synthesis — D-Finite Sequences, Transposition & Fast Composition to consolidate Chapters 18–21 across diagnostic drills and mixed problem sets.
Continue to Chapter 22: Tree DP with FPS — Heavy-Light Decomposition, Static Top Trees & Zero-Divisor Maintenance to begin Part VI: Advanced Frontiers.

NotePrerequisite Chapters & Algebraic Assumptions



Before studying this chapter, make sure you are comfortable with:

Chapter 6: Binomial Sums, Snake Oil, Taylor Shifts & Stirling Numbers — Falling-factorial basis \(\{x^{\underline{k}}\}\), polynomial Taylor shift \(A(x + c)\) via reversed exponential convolution, and Stirling numbers of both kinds.
Chapter 18: D-Finite Series, The Euler Operator, The 7 ODE Archetypes & p-Adic Indicial Lifting — Holonomic (D-finite) formal power series, P-recursive sequences, the Euler operator \(\vartheta = x D_x\), and unrolling linear ODEs into \(O(N)\) coefficient recurrences.

Throughout this chapter, \(K\) denotes a field of characteristic \(0\) or a prime field \(\mathbb{F}_p\) with \(p > N\) (unless explicitly noted otherwise, as in arbitrary-modulus recurrences where division by \(n\) is eliminated).




By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

Translate Between Differential and Shift Operators Algebraically: Manipulate non-commutative operators in the Weyl algebra \(K[x]\langle D_x \rangle\) and the Ore shift algebra \(K[n]\langle E_n \rangle\), and apply the discrete Fourier–Laplace dictionary (\(x \mapsto E_n^{-1}, \vartheta \mapsto n\)) without index-alignment errors.
Telescope Definite Binomial Sums That Resist Snake Oil: Derive P-recursive recurrences for hypergeometric sums \(S_n = \sum_k F(n, k)\) using both Zeilberger’s WZ Creative Telescoping and EI’s Differential-Residue Engine (\(S_n = [x^{-1}] x^{-1} A(x) B(x)^n\) via \(\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx}(\dots) = 0\)).
Evaluate Coupled \(r\)-State Sparse Compositions in \(O(rNK)\) Time: Given a D-finite series \(F(y)\) of order \(r\) and a \(K\)-sparse polynomial \(P(x)\) with \(P(0) = 0\), compute \(H(x) = F(P(x)) \bmod x^N\) in \(O(rNK)\) operations without dividing by \(P'(x)\) or calling NTT.
Apply EI 科技 Truncated Taylor ODEs: Turn a linear ODE for \(F(x)\) into an inhomogeneous linear ODE for its degree-\((N-1)\) truncation \(F_{<N}(x) = F(x) \bmod x^N\) whose right-hand side has \(O(1)\) sparse boundary terms, accelerating shifted evaluations \(F_{<N}(x + c)\) and truncated exponential integrals from \(O(N \log N)\) to \(O(N)\).

NotePrerequisite Chapters & Algebraic Assumptions



Before studying this chapter, make sure you are comfortable with:

Chapter 6: Binomial Sums, Snake Oil, Taylor Shifts & Stirling Numbers — Falling-factorial basis \(\{x^{\underline{k}}\}\), polynomial Taylor shift \(A(x + c)\) via reversed exponential convolution, and Stirling numbers of both kinds.
Chapter 18: D-Finite Series, The Euler Operator, The 7 ODE Archetypes & p-Adic Indicial Lifting — Holonomic (D-finite) formal power series, P-recursive sequences, the Euler operator \(\vartheta = x D_x\), and unrolling linear ODEs into \(O(N)\) coefficient recurrences.

Throughout this chapter, \(K\) denotes a field of characteristic \(0\) or a prime field \(\mathbb{F}_p\) with \(p > N\) (unless explicitly noted otherwise, as in arbitrary-modulus recurrences where division by \(n\) is eliminated).




By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

Translate Between Differential and Shift Operators Algebraically: Manipulate non-commutative operators in the Weyl algebra \(K[x]\langle D_x \rangle\) and the Ore shift algebra \(K[n]\langle E_n \rangle\), and apply the discrete Fourier–Laplace dictionary (\(x \mapsto E_n^{-1}, \vartheta \mapsto n\)) without index-alignment errors.
Telescope Definite Binomial Sums That Resist Snake Oil: Derive P-recursive recurrences for hypergeometric sums \(S_n = \sum_k F(n, k)\) using both Zeilberger’s WZ Creative Telescoping and EI’s Differential-Residue Engine (\(S_n = [x^{-1}] x^{-1} A(x) B(x)^n\) via \(\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx}(\dots) = 0\)).
Evaluate Coupled \(r\)-State Sparse Compositions in \(O(rNK)\) Time: Given a D-finite series \(F(y)\) of order \(r\) and a \(K\)-sparse polynomial \(P(x)\) with \(P(0) = 0\), compute \(H(x) = F(P(x)) \bmod x^N\) in \(O(rNK)\) operations without dividing by \(P'(x)\) or calling NTT.
Apply EI 科技 Truncated Taylor ODEs: Turn a linear ODE for \(F(x)\) into an inhomogeneous linear ODE for its degree-\((N-1)\) truncation \(F_{<N}(x) = F(x) \bmod x^N\) whose right-hand side has \(O(1)\) sparse boundary terms, accelerating shifted evaluations \(F_{<N}(x + c)\) and truncated exponential integrals from \(O(N \log N)\) to \(O(N)\).

19.1 Non-Commutative Weyl & Shift Operator Algebras (\(K[x]\langle D_x \rangle\) and \(K[n]\langle E_n \rangle\))
In Chapter 18, we converted linear differential equations into coefficient recurrences by extracting \([x^n]\) term-by-term. When expressions grow more intricate—such as composed differential operators, iterated Euler operators, or multivariate creative telescoping—manual coefficient extraction becomes error-prone. The clean solution is to package differentiation, multiplication by \(x\), index multiplication by \(n\), and index shifting \(n \mapsto n + 1\) as elements of two non-commutative polynomial rings of operators.

1. The Weyl Algebra \(K[x]\langle D_x \rangle\) and the Euler Subalgebra \(K[x]\langle \vartheta \rangle\)
Consider a formal power series \(F(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} f_n x^n \in K[[x]]\). Two elementary linear operators act on \(K[[x]]\):

The Multiplication Operator \(x\): shifts powers up via \((x \cdot F)(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} f_n x^{n+1}\).
The Formal Derivative Operator \(D_x = \frac{d}{dx}\): shifts powers down via \((D_x F)(x) = \sum_{n \ge 1} n f_n x^{n-1}\).

Because differentiating a product \(x F(x)\) triggers the Leibniz product rule, \(D_x\) and \(x\) do not commute. Applying \(D_x x - x D_x\) to any test series \(F(x)\) gives: \[D_x(x F(x)) - x (D_x F(x)) = \big(F(x) + x F'(x)\big) - x F'(x) = F(x).\]






ImportantDefinition 19.1 (The Weyl Algebra \(K[x]\langle D_x \rangle\))



The Weyl algebra \(\mathcal{W}_x = K[x]\langle D_x \rangle\) is the associative \(K\)-algebra generated by \(x\) and \(D_x\) subject to the fundamental commutation relation: \[D_x x - x D_x = 1 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad D_x x = x D_x + 1.\] By induction on \(s \ge 1\) and \(k \ge 1\), moving \(D_x^k\) past \(x^s\) obeys the generalized Leibniz operator identity: \[D_x^k x^s = \sum_{j=0}^{\min(k, s)} \binom{k}{j} s^{\underline{j}} \, x^{s-j} D_x^{k-j}.\]


While \(D_x\) shifts degrees down by \(1\), the Euler (homogeneity) operator \(\vartheta = x D_x\) preserves every monomial’s degree: \(\vartheta(x^n) = n x^n\). How does \(\vartheta\) commute with \(x^s\)?






TipDiagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Commuting \(\vartheta\) Past \(x^s\)




The Diagnostic Signal: You have an operator expression mixing powers of \(x\) and powers of \(\vartheta = x D_x\), such as \(\vartheta^m \big(x^s F(x)\big)\), and you want to move \(x^s\) to the far left so all \(\vartheta\)’s act directly on \(F(x)\).
The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Apply \(\vartheta = x D_x\) to \(x^s F(x)\) by the product rule: \[\vartheta\big(x^s F(x)\big) = x \frac{d}{dx}\big(x^s F(x)\big) = s x^s F(x) + x^{s+1} F'(x) = x^s (\vartheta + s) F(x).\] Thus pulling \(x^s\) to the left of \(\vartheta\) simply shifts \(\vartheta \gets \vartheta + s\)! Repeating this \(m\) times gives for any polynomial \(P(\vartheta) \in K[\vartheta]\): \[P(\vartheta) \, x^s = x^s \, P(\vartheta + s).\]





2. The Ore Shift Algebra \(K[n]\langle E_n \rangle\)
Now view the coefficient sequence \((f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}\) (with \(f_n = 0\) for \(n < 0\)) as the object of study. Two basic operators act on sequences:

The Index Operator \(n\): multiplies the \(n\)-th term by \(n\), mapping \((f_n) \mapsto (n f_n)\).
The Forward Shift Operator \(E_n\): increments the index by \(1\), mapping \((f_n) \mapsto (f_{n+1})\). Its inverse \(E_n^{-1}\) is the backward shift \((f_n) \mapsto (f_{n-1})\).

Applying \(E_n\) to the sequence \((n f_n)\) evaluates the product at \(n + 1\), giving \((n + 1) f_{n+1} = ((n + 1) E_n f)_n\).






ImportantDefinition 19.2 (The Shift Algebra \(K[n]\langle E_n, E_n^{-1} \rangle\))



The Ore shift algebra \(\mathcal{S}_n = K[n]\langle E_n, E_n^{-1} \rangle\) is the non-commutative \(K\)-algebra generated by \(n\) and \(E_n^{\pm 1}\) subject to the commutation rules: \[E_n \, n = (n + 1) E_n, \qquad E_n^{-1} \, n = (n - 1) E_n^{-1}.\] More generally, for any polynomial \(P(n) \in K[n]\) and integer \(s \in \mathbb{Z}\): \[E_n^s \, P(n) = P(n + s) \, E_n^s.\]




3. The Fourier–Laplace Operator Dictionary (\(K[x]\langle \vartheta \rangle \longleftrightarrow K[n]\langle E_n^{-1} \rangle\))
Every linear differential equation on \(F(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} f_n x^n\) can be multiplied by \(x^m\) to clear negative shifts, placing it in \(K[x]\langle \vartheta \rangle\). Look at how the generators \(x\) and \(\vartheta\) act on the \(n\)-th coefficient \([x^n]\):

Extracting \([x^n]\) after multiplying by \(x^s\) yields \([x^n]\big(x^s F(x)\big) = f_{n-s} = (E_n^{-s} f)_n\).
Extracting \([x^n]\) after applying \(P(\vartheta)\) yields \([x^n]\big(P(\vartheta) F(x)\big) = P(n) f_n\).

Notice that in \(K[x]\langle \vartheta \rangle\), we have \(P(\vartheta) x^s = x^s P(\vartheta + s)\), while in \(K[n]\langle E_n^{-1} \rangle\), we have \(P(n) E_n^{-s} = E_n^{-s} P(n - s)\)! Thus the map sending \(x \mapsto E_n^{-1}\) and \(\vartheta \mapsto n\) (when operators are written in normal form with \(x^s\) on the left and \(P(\vartheta)\) on the right, or vice versa using the commutation law) provides an exact algebraic dictionary:

Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N \le 4\)): Operator Translation for Large Schröder Numbers
Recall that the Large Schröder OGF \(S(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} S_n x^n = \frac{1 - x - \sqrt{1 - 6x + x^2}}{2x}\) satisfies the linear ODE (obtained from \((1 - 6x + x^2) W'(x) = (-3 + x) W(x)\) on \(W(x) = \sqrt{1 - 6x + x^2} = 1 - x - 2x S(x)\)): \[x(1 - 6x + x^2) S'(x) + (1 - 3x) S(x) = 1 - 2x.\] Let us translate the left-hand side into \(K[x]\langle \vartheta \rangle\) and then into \(K[n]\langle E_n^{-1} \rangle\) in three single-step lines:

Since \(x S'(x) = \vartheta S(x)\), rewrite the differential operator in normal form with powers of \(x\) on the left: \[L(x, \vartheta) = (1 - 6x + x^2)\vartheta + (1 - 3x) = (\vartheta + 1) - 3x(2\vartheta + 1) + x^2 \vartheta.\]
Apply the dictionary \(x^s P(\vartheta) \mapsto P(n - s) E_n^{-s}\) at degree \(n \ge 2\) (where \([x^n](1 - 2x) = 0\)): \[(n + 1) S_n - 3\big(2(n - 1) + 1\big) S_{n-1} + (n - 2) S_{n-2} = 0.\]
Rearrange into the P-recursive recurrence for \(n \ge 2\): \[(n + 1) S_n = 3(2n - 1) S_{n-1} - (n - 2) S_{n-2}.\]


Trace (\(n = 0 \dots 4\)): With \(S_0 = 1, S_1 = 2\):

\(n = 2\): \(3 S_2 = 3(3)(2) - 0 \cdot S_0 = 18 \implies S_2 = 6\).
\(n = 3\): \(4 S_3 = 3(5)(6) - 1(2) = 88 \implies S_3 = 22\).
\(n = 4\): \(5 S_4 = 3(7)(22) - 2(6) = 450 \implies S_4 = 90\).








NoteAlgorithm Contract: Coupled Sparse Composition & Weyl–Shift Operator Translation




Input: Either a coupled \(2 \times 2\) linear differential system \(Y'(x) = M(x) Y(x)\) over \(K(x)\), or a Weyl differential operator \(L = \sum_{s=0}^d x^s P_s(\vartheta) \in K[x]\langle \vartheta \rangle\) annihilating \(F(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} f_n x^n\), together with initial values and target degree \(N\).
Output: Uncoupled scalar order-\(2\) linear ODE for \(F(x)\) (or direct coupled recurrence) and the translated P-recursive operator \(\widehat{L} = \sum_{s=0}^d P_s(n - s) E_n^{-s} \in K[n]\langle E_n^{-1} \rangle\) yielding \(f_0, \dots, f_N\).
Algebraic Preconditions: In scalar uncoupling of \(F' = a F + b G\), \(b(x) \neq 0\) (or maintain \((f_n, g_n)\) directly as a coupled \(2\)-vector recurrence to avoid apparent singularities at roots of \(b(x)\)); for coefficient unrolling up to \(N\), the indicial polynomial \(P_0(n)\) is invertible in \(K\) for all \(n_{\text{init}} < n \le N\).
Complexity: \(O(d \cdot r)\) symbolic translation work via the Fourier–Laplace dictionary \(x^s P(\vartheta) \mapsto P(n-s) E_n^{-s}\), followed by \(O(d \cdot N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space (or \(O(d)\) rolling space) with zero NTTs.
Correctness Invariant: Normal-ordering every monomial with powers of \(x\) on the left of \(\vartheta\) via \(P(\vartheta) x^s = x^s P(\vartheta + s)\) ensures that \(x^s P_s(\vartheta)(f_{n-s} x^{n-s}) = P_s(n - s) f_{n-s} x^n\), making the map \(x^s P_s(\vartheta) \mapsto P_s(n - s) E_n^{-s}\) an exact \(K\)-algebra anti-isomorphism on coefficient sequences.

section: 19.2 Zeilberger’s Creative Telescoping, WZ Pairs & EI’s Differential-Residue Binomial Sum Engine (Engine 3)
text:
19.2 Zeilberger’s Creative Telescoping, WZ Pairs & EI’s Differential-Residue Binomial Sum Engine (Engine 3)
In Chapter 6, we met two classic engines for evaluating a definite binomial sum \(S_n = \sum_{k} F(n, k)\):

Engine 1 (Snake Oil): Multiply by \(z^n\), swap \(\sum_n\) and \(\sum_k\), and sum the inner series over \(n\).
Engine 2 (Egorychev / Residue Extraction): Write \(F(n, k) = [x^{g(n, k)}] P(x, n, k)\) so the sum over \(k\) becomes a geometric or binomial series inside \([x^m]\).

What happens when neither engine collapses the sum into a closed form? Consider the \(c\)-Delannoy polynomial \[D_n(c) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k}{k} c^k,\] or Apéry’s sum \(\sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}^2 \binom{n+k}{k}^2\). Here \(n\) appears in three places at once, and \(D_n(c)\) has no hypergeometric closed form—yet \(D_0(c), \dots, D_N(c)\) can still be computed in \(O(N)\) time because \(D_n(c)\) is P-recursive! We now develop the two complementary engines that compile such sums directly into \(O(N)\) recurrences.

1. Zeilberger’s Creative Telescoping & WZ Certificate Pairs
Suppose \(F(n, k)\) is a bivariate hypergeometric term, meaning that both shift ratios \(\frac{F(n+1, k)}{F(n, k)}\) and \(\frac{F(n, k+1)}{F(n, k)}\) are rational functions of \((n, k)\) over \(K\). If we try to telescope \(F(n+1, k) - F(n, k) = G(n, k+1) - G(n, k)\) directly, no hypergeometric \(G(n, k)\) may exist.
Zeilberger’s insight (1990) is to take a polynomial linear combination of shifts \(F(n, k), F(n+1, k), \dots, F(n+r, k)\) along \(n\) until their combination becomes an exact first difference \(\Delta_k G(n, k) = G(n, k+1) - G(n, k)\) along \(k\)!






ImportantTheorem 19.1 (Zeilberger’s Creative Telescoping & WZ Certificate)



Let \(F(n, k)\) be a proper hypergeometric term with natural compact support (so \(F(n, k) = 0\) for \(k < 0\) and \(k > n + O(1)\)). Then there exist an order \(r \ge 1\), polynomials \(p_0(n), p_1(n), \dots, p_r(n) \in K[n]\) (independent of \(k\)!), and a rational certificate \(R(n, k) \in K(n, k)\) such that with \(G(n, k) = R(n, k) F(n, k)\), the WZ difference identity holds for all \((n, k)\): \[\sum_{j=0}^{r} p_j(n) \, F(n + j, k) = G(n, k + 1) - G(n, k).\] Summing both sides over all \(k \in \mathbb{Z}\), the right-hand side telescopes to \(0\) on natural support, proving that \(S_n = \sum_{k} F(n, k)\) satisfies the homogeneous P-recursive recurrence: \[\sum_{j=0}^{r} p_j(n) \, S_{n+j} = 0.\]








WarningFailure Mode & Remedy: Non-Natural Summation Boundaries (\(\sum_{k=0}^m \binom{n}{k}\) with \(m < n\))



The Trap: Students sometimes apply a homogeneous recurrence derived from creative telescoping to a sum whose upper limit \(m\) cuts off the summand before \(F(n, k)\) naturally vanishes (for example, the partial row sum \(S(n, m) = \sum_{k=0}^m \binom{n}{k}\) for a fixed \(m < n\)). Why It Fails: Pascal’s identity gives the WZ pair \(F(n, k) = \binom{n}{k}\) and \(G(n, k) = -\binom{n}{k-1}\), satisfying: \[F(n + 1, k) - 2 F(n, k) = \binom{n}{k - 1} - \binom{n}{k} = G(n, k + 1) - G(n, k).\] When summed over natural support \(k \in [0, n+1]\), the boundary values \(G(n, n+2) = -\binom{n}{n+1} = 0\) and \(G(n, 0) = -\binom{n}{-1} = 0\) vanish, giving \(S_{n+1} - 2 S_n = 0 \implies S_n = 2^n\). However, if we truncate the sum at \(k = m < n\), summing from \(k = 0\) to \(m\) leaves a non-zero upper boundary term: \[\sum_{k=0}^{m} \big(F(n+1, k) - 2 F(n, k)\big) = G(n, m + 1) - G(n, 0) = -\binom{n}{m}.\] The Remedy: Always evaluate \(G(n, k_{\max} + 1) - G(n, k_{\min})\) explicitly! For truncated limits, creative telescoping produces an inhomogeneous P-recurrence \(S(n+1, m) = 2 S(n, m) - \binom{n}{m}\).




2. EI’s Differential-Residue Binomial Sum Engine (Engine 3)
Finding the rational certificate \(R(n, k)\) by hand can be algebraically tedious. In competitive programming, Elegia (EI, 载谭 Binomial Sums) popularized a far more direct algorithm—Engine 3—that replaces Gosper’s discrete certificate search with formal residue integration by parts in \(K((x))\).






TipDiagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: EI’s Differential-Residue Method




The Diagnostic Signal: You have a definite binomial sum \(S_n = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k}{k} c^k\) (or any sum where \(n\) enters via binomial factors \(\binom{n}{k}, \binom{n+k}{k}, \binom{2n-k}{n}\)) and you want the P-recursive recurrence for \(S_n\) by hand in 3 lines of algebra.
The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad:

Step 1 (Isolate \(n\) into a Power \(B(x)^n\)): Use Egorychev’s residue representation \([x^k](1+x)^m = \binom{m}{k}\) to write \(S_n\) as a constant term (or formal residue) in \(x\) where \(n\) appears only in the exponent of a single rational function \(B(x)\): \[S_n = [x^0]\Big(A(x) B(x)^n\Big) = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\Big(x^{-1} A(x) B(x)^n\Big).\] For instance, in \(D_n(c) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} \binom{n+k}{k} c^k\), write \(\binom{n+k}{k} = \binom{n+k}{n} = [x^n](1+x)^{n+k}\). Then: \[
\begin{aligned}
D_n(c)
&= [x^n] (1+x)^n \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} c^k (1+x)^k \\[4pt]
&= [x^n] (1+x)^n \big(1 + c(1+x)\big)^n
&& \text{(collapse the sum over } k \text{ by the Binomial Theorem)} \\[4pt]
&= \operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \Bigl[ x^{-n-1} (1+x)^n (1 + c + cx)^n \Bigr]
&& \text{(write } [x^n] G(x) = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0} x^{-n-1} G(x)\text{)} \\[4pt]
&= \operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \left[ x^{-1} \left( \frac{(1+x)(1 + c + cx)}{x} \right)^n \right].
&& \text{(factor } x^{-n-1} = x^{-1} \cdot x^{-n} \text{ into the } n\text{-th power)}
\end{aligned}
\] Here \(A(x) = 1\) and \(B(x) = \frac{(1+x)(1 + c + cx)}{x} = (1+c)x^{-1} + (1 + 2c) + c x\)!
Step 2 (Apply the Formal Residue Derivative Identity \(\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx}(\dots) = 0\)): In the formal Laurent field \(K((x))\), the derivative of any Laurent series has zero coefficient of \(x^{-1}\). Applying \(\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx}\big(\phi(x) B(x)^n\big) = 0\) gives the formal integration-by-parts rule: \[\operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\Big(\phi'(x) B(x)^n\Big) = -n \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\Big(\phi(x) B'(x) B(x)^{n-1}\Big).\]
Step 3 (Eliminate Non-Constant Powers of \(x\) via Linear Algebra): Expand \(B(x)\) and \(x B'(x)\) as Laurent polynomials in \(x\), and express \(S_{n+1}, S_n, S_{n-1}\) in terms of \(\mu_j = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\big(x^{j-1} B(x)^n\big)\) to eliminate all auxiliary moments \(\mu_j\) (\(j \neq 0\))!





Complete Worked Derivation & Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N \le 4\)): The \(c\)-Delannoy Recurrence
Let us execute Steps 1–3 on \(D_n(c) = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k}\binom{n+k}{k} c^k\):

Residue Representation: From Step 1 above, let \(B(x) = (1+c)x^{-1} + (1+2c) + cx\). For each integer shift \(j \in \mathbb{Z}\), define the Laurent moment: \[\mu_j(n) = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\Big(x^{j-1} B(x)^n\Big), \qquad \text{so that } \mu_0(n) = D_n(c).\]
Symmetry Between \(\mu_1(n)\) and \(\mu_{-1}(n)\): Notice that \(x B'(x) = -(1+c)x^{-1} + cx\). First apply \(\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx}\big(B(x)^n\big) = 0\): \[0 = n \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\Big(x^{-1} \big(x B'(x)\big) B(x)^{n-1}\Big) = n \big(-(1+c) \mu_{-1}(n-1) + c \mu_1(n-1)\big),\] which proves \((1+c) \mu_{-1}(m) = c \mu_1(m)\) for all \(m \ge 0\)!
Eliminating \(\mu_{\pm 1}\) via the Quadratic Differential Identity for \(x B'(x)\): Observe that \(B(x) - (1+2c) = (1+c)x^{-1} + cx\) and \(x B'(x) = -(1+c)x^{-1} + cx\) share the same two monomials with opposite signs. Squaring both and subtracting eliminates \(x\) and \(x^{-1}\) completely: \[\big(B(x) - (1+2c)\big)^2 - \big(x B'(x)\big)^2 = 4c(1+c) = (1+2c)^2 - 1 \implies \big(x B'(x)\big)^2 = B(x)^2 - 2(1+2c) B(x) + 1.\] Simultaneously, applying \(\vartheta = x \frac{d}{dx}\) to \(x B'(x) = -(1+c)x^{-1} + cx\) flips the sign back to \(B(x) - (1+2c)\): \[x \frac{d}{dx}\big(x B'(x)\big) = (1+c)x^{-1} + cx = B(x) - (1+2c).\] Now apply the formal residue derivative identity \(0 = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx}\Big(x B'(x) B(x)^{n-1}\Big)\): \[\begin{aligned}
0 &= \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\left[ x^{-1} \Big( x \frac{d}{dx}\big(x B'(x)\big) B(x)^{n-1} + (n-1) \big(x B'(x)\big)^2 B(x)^{n-2} \Big) \right] \\
&= \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\left[ x^{-1} \Big( \big(B(x) - (1+2c)\big) B(x)^{n-1} + (n-1)\big(B(x)^2 - 2(1+2c)B(x) + 1\big) B(x)^{n-2} \Big) \right] \\
&= \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\left[ x^{-1} \Big( n B(x)^n - (2n - 1)(1 + 2c) B(x)^{n-1} + (n - 1) B(x)^{n-2} \Big) \right],
\end{aligned}\] which immediately extracts the 3-term P-recursive recurrence: \[n D_n(c) = (2n - 1)(1 + 2c) D_{n-1}(c) - (n - 1) D_{n-2}(c) \qquad (n \ge 2).\]


Hand-Checkable Trace for \(c = 2\) (\(1 + 2c = 5\)) up to \(N = 4\):

Algebraic Cross-Check via Diagonal Formula: By Furstenberg’s diagonal formula from Chapter 16, \(D_n(c) = [x^n]\big((1+c) + (1+2c)x + cx^2\big)^n\) has \(p_0 = 1+c, p_1 = 1+2c, p_2 = c\) with \(p_1^2 - 4 p_0 p_2 = (1 + 2c)^2 - 4c(1+c) = 1\), confirming the OGF \(\sum_{n \ge 0} D_n(c) z^n = (1 - 2(1 + 2c)z + z^2)^{-1/2}\) and recurrence \(n D_n(c) = (2n - 1)(1 + 2c) D_{n-1}(c) - (n - 1) D_{n-2}(c)\).
Recurrence vs. Direct Binomial Sum (\(c = 2\)):

\(n = 0\): \(D_0(2) = \binom{0}{0}\binom{0}{0} 2^0 = 1\).
\(n = 1\): \(D_1(2) = \binom{1}{0}\binom{1}{0} 2^0 + \binom{1}{1}\binom{2}{1} 2^1 = 1 + 4 = 5\).
\(n = 2\): \(2 D_2(2) = 5(3) D_1(2) - 1 D_0(2) = 75 - 1 = 74 \implies D_2(2) = 37\), matching \(1 + \binom{2}{1}\binom{3}{1}(2) + \binom{2}{2}\binom{4}{2}(4) = 1 + 12 + 24 = 37\).
\(n = 3\): \(3 D_3(2) = 5(5) D_2(2) - 2 D_1(2) = 25(37) - 10 = 915 \implies D_3(2) = 305\), matching \(1 + 3(4)(2) + 3(10)(4) + 1(20)(8) = 305\).
\(n = 4\): \(4 D_4(2) = 5(7) D_3(2) - 3 D_2(2) = 35(305) - 3(37) = 10564 \implies D_4(2) = 2641\).









NoteAlgorithm Contract: EI’s Differential-Residue Binomial Sum Engine (Engine 3)




Input: A definite hypergeometric binomial sum \(S_n = \sum_{k} F(n, k)\) representable as \(S_n = \operatorname{Res}_{x=0}\big(x^{-1} A(x) B(x)^n\big)\) with rational \(A(x), B(x) \in K(x)\), and target index \(N\).
Output: The sequence of values \(S_0, S_1, \dots, S_N \in K\).
Algebraic Preconditions: \(B(x)\) has Laurent degree span \([ -d_1, d_2 ]\) with \(d_1, d_2 \ge 1\); the resulting indicial polynomial \(I(n)\) is invertible in \(K\) for all \(r \le n \le N\) (requiring \(\operatorname{char}(K) = 0\) or \(p > N\), or \(p\)-adic lifting from Chapter 18.4).
Complexity: \(O((d_1 + d_2)^3)\) offline symbolic work to eliminate the \(d_1 + d_2 - 1\) auxiliary Laurent moments \(\mu_j(n)\), followed by \(O((d_1 + d_2) N)\) time and \(O(d_1 + d_2)\) auxiliary space (or \(O(N)\) space to store all answers) to unroll \(S_0, \dots, S_N\).
Correctness Invariant: In the formal Laurent field \(K((x))\), \(\operatorname{Res}_{x=0} \frac{d}{dx} L(x) = 0\) holds identically for every \(L(x) \in K((x))\) without analytic convergence hypotheses; provided \(k\) ranges over the full natural support of the coefficient extraction, no boundary terms are omitted.
