Every single region pair matches identically on both sides except the two diagonal cross-terms \((A \setminus B \to B \setminus A)\) and \((B \setminus A \to A \setminus B)\), which appear once on the LHS and zero times on the RHS. Summing over all 16 pairs yields the exact identity. \(\blacksquare\)




2.2 The Distributive Lattice of Minimum Cuts \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\)
Let \(\lambda^* = \min_{s \in S \subseteq V \setminus \{t\}} \kappa(S)\) denote the minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut capacity, and let
\[\mathcal{L}_{\min} := \left\{ S \subseteq V \;\middle|\; s \in S,\; t \notin S,\; \kappa(S) = \lambda^* \right\}\]
be the family of all source-side vertex sets of minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cuts.






ImportantCorollary 2.2 (Closure Under \(\cap\) and \(\cup\) — The Distributive Minimum-Cut Lattice)



If \(A, B \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) are two minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cuts, then both their intersection \(A \cap B\) and their union \(A \cup B\) are also minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cuts (\(A \cap B \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) and \(A \cup B \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\)). Consequently, \((\mathcal{L}_{\min}, \subseteq, \cap, \cup)\) is a finite distributive lattice.



Proof
Since \(s \in A\) and \(s \in B\), we have \(s \in A \cap B \subseteq A \cup B\). Since \(t \notin A\) and \(t \notin B\), we have \(t \notin A \cup B \supseteq A \cap B\). Thus both \(A \cap B\) and \(A \cup B\) are valid \(s\)-\(t\) cuts, which by definition of \(\lambda^*\) must satisfy \(\kappa(A \cap B) \ge \lambda^*\) and \(\kappa(A \cup B) \ge \lambda^*\). Applying Theorem 2.1 gives:
\[2\lambda^* = \kappa(A) + \kappa(B) \ge \kappa(A \cup B) + \kappa(A \cap B) \ge \lambda^* + \lambda^* = 2\lambda^*\]
Because the left and right endpoints of this inequality chain are both \(2\lambda^*\), equality must hold everywhere: \(\kappa(A \cup B) = \lambda^*\) and \(\kappa(A \cap B) = \lambda^*\), plus \(c(A \setminus B, B \setminus A) = c(B \setminus A, A \setminus B) = 0\). Since set union and intersection distribute over each other on any family of subsets of \(V\), \((\mathcal{L}_{\min}, \subseteq, \cap, \cup)\) is a finite distributive lattice. \(\blacksquare\)




2.3 Canonical Extremal Cuts (\(S_{\min}\) vs. \(S_{\max}\)) and the Uniqueness Criterion
Fix any maximum flow \(f^*\) in \(G\), and let \(G_{f^*}\) be its residual network. Recall from Chapter 1 (Complementary Slackness / Cut-Value Conservation Lemma) that an \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((S, V \setminus S)\) belongs to \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\) if and only if no residual arc in \(G_{f^*}\) leaves \(S\):
\[S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min} \iff s \in S,\;\; t \notin S,\;\; \text{and}\;\; \delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\]
Notice that this characterization depends only on the reachability structure of \(G_{f^*}\) — showing that \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\) is invariant across all choices of maximum flow \(f^*\)! Moreover, because \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\) is a finite non-empty lattice closed under \(\cap\) and \(\cup\), taking the intersection and union over all \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) yields two canonical extremal minimum cuts:
\[\mathcal{S}_{\text{first}} := \bigcap_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S, \qquad \mathcal{S}_{\text{last}} := \bigcup_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S\]
How do we compute these two extremal cuts directly from \(G_{f^*}\)?






ImportantTheorem 2.3 (Residual Reachability Characterization of \(S_{\min}\) and \(S_{\max}\))



In the residual network \(G_{f^*}\) of any maximum \(s\)-\(t\) flow \(f^*\), define:
\[S_{\min} := \left\{ v \in V \;\middle|\; s \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v \right\}, \qquad T_{\min} := \left\{ v \in V \;\middle|\; v \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t \right\}, \qquad S_{\max} := V \setminus T_{\min} = \left\{ v \in V \;\middle|\; v \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t \right\}\]
Then for every minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((S, T)\) with \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\):
\[S_{\min} \subseteq S \subseteq S_{\max} \qquad \text{and equivalently} \qquad T_{\min} \subseteq T \subseteq V \setminus S_{\min}\]
Thus \(S_{\min}\) is the unique inclusion-wise minimum source side (\(\bigcap_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S\)), and \(S_{\max}\) is the unique inclusion-wise maximum source side (\(\bigcup_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S\)).



Proof

Why \(S_{\min} \subseteq S\) for every \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\): Since \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\), we have \(s \in S\) and \(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\) (no residual arc leaves \(S\)). By induction along any residual path \(s = v_0 \to v_1 \to \dots \to v_k = v\) in \(G_{f^*}\), every vertex \(v \in S_{\min}\) must also lie in \(S\). Since \(S_{\min}\) is itself out-closed in \(G_{f^*}\) and \(t \notin S_{\min}\) (by optimality of \(f^*\)), \(S_{\min} \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\).
Why \(S \subseteq S_{\max}\) (i.e., \(T_{\min} \subseteq V \setminus S\)) for every \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\): Suppose \(v \in T_{\min}\), so there exists a residual path \(v = u_0 \to u_1 \to \dots \to u_r = t\) in \(G_{f^*}\). If \(v \in S\), then because \(S\) is out-closed in \(G_{f^*}\), induction along the path forces \(t \in S\), contradicting \(t \notin S\)! Hence \(v \notin S\) for every \(v \in T_{\min}\), proving \(S \subseteq V \setminus T_{\min} = S_{\max}\). Furthermore, if \(u \in S_{\max}\) (\(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\)) and \((u \to w) \in E_{f^*}\), then \(w \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\) (otherwise \(u \to w \leadsto t\)), so \(w \in S_{\max}\). Thus \(S_{\max}\) is out-closed in \(G_{f^*}\) with \(s \in S_{\max}\) and \(t \notin S_{\max}\), confirming \(S_{\max} \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\). \(\blacksquare\)

This immediately yields a linear-time test for minimum-cut uniqueness ([ZOJ 2587] Unique Attack / [UVa 10480] Sabotage):






TipCorollary 2.4 (Linear-Time Minimum-Cut Uniqueness Test)



A directed network \(G\) possesses a unique minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut (\(|\mathcal{L}_{\min}| = 1\)) if and only if \(S_{\min} = S_{\max}\), which holds if and only if the undecided middle zone is empty:
\[S_{\min} \cup T_{\min} = V \iff |S_{\min}| + |T_{\min}| = |V|\]
To verify uniqueness in \(O(V + E)\) time after Dinic:

Run a forward BFS/DFS from \(s\) in \(G_{f^*}\) using arcs with \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) > 0\) to mark \(S_{\min}\).
Run a reverse BFS/DFS from \(t\) in \(G_{f^*}\) using incoming arcs with \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) > 0\) to mark \(T_{\min}\).
Return true iff every vertex \(v \in V\) was visited in Step 1 or Step 2.

3. Picard–Queyranne Residual Condensation DAG & Cut Edge Classification ([AHOI2009] 最小割)

3.1 The Picard–Queyranne Theorem (1980)
Suppose \(S_{\min} \cup T_{\min} \neq V\), so the network has multiple minimum cuts. How are all minimum cuts \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) structured inside \(G_{f^*}\)?
Recall that \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) if and only if \(s \in S\), \(t \notin S\), and \(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\). Consider any two vertices \(u, v \in V\) that belong to the same Strongly Connected Component (SCC) of the residual network \(G_{f^*}\) (meaning \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\) and \(v \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} u\)). Because no residual path can ever cross from \(S\) to \(V \setminus S\), \(u\) and \(v\) can never be separated by any minimum cut: either \(\{u, v\} \subseteq S\) or \(\{u, v\} \subseteq V \setminus S\) for every \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\)!






ImportantTheorem 3.1 (Picard–Queyranne Characterization of All Minimum Cuts, 1980)



Contract every Strongly Connected Component of the final residual network \(G_{f^*}\) into a single supernode to form the Residual Condensation DAG \(\mathcal{D}(G_{f^*})\), and let \(\operatorname{scc}(v)\) denote the component ID of vertex \(v \in V\). Then:

\(\operatorname{scc}(s) \neq \operatorname{scc}(t)\) (since \(s \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\)).
A vertex partition \((S, V \setminus S)\) is a minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut (\(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\)) if and only if \(S\) is the union of a downward-closed (out-closed) ideal of SCCs in \(\mathcal{D}(G_{f^*})\) that contains \(\operatorname{scc}(s)\) ( along with all SCCs reachable from \(\operatorname{scc}(s)\)) and excludes \(\operatorname{scc}(t)\) (along with all SCCs that can reach \(\operatorname{scc}(t)\)).



In other words, the condensation DAG \(\mathcal{D}(G_{f^*})\) is a compact \(O(V + E)\)-size representation of the entire (potentially exponential-size) lattice \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\)!



3.2 Broken-Gadget Counterexample FM-02 / FM-03: The Saturated \(\implies\) Cut Edge Fallacy
Before stating the exact edge classification theorem, let us expose the single most common bug in competitive programming min-cut analysis.

[!WARNING] Broken-Gadget Counterexample FM-02 / FM-03 (\(\leftrightarrow\) H-02) — Saturated Edge \(\neq\) Feasible Min-Cut Edge:
The Fallacy: “By Complementary Slackness, every edge in a minimum cut is saturated (\(c_{f^*}(u, v) = 0\)). Therefore, an edge \(e = (u \to v)\) belongs to at least one minimum cut if and only if \(c_{f^*}(u, v) = 0\).”
Why It Fails (Concrete 5-Vertex Bypass Counterexample): Consider the 5-vertex directed network \(V = \{s, u, v, w, t\}\) with 5 unit-capacity edges:

Main path: \(s \xrightarrow{1} u \xrightarrow{1} v \xrightarrow{1} t\).
Parallel bypass around \((u \to v)\): \(u \xrightarrow{1} w \xrightarrow{1} v\).

Suppose Dinic’s first augmenting path pushes \(1\) unit of flow along \(s \to u \to v \to t\). Since \(\kappa(\{s\}) = c(s \to u) = 1\), this flow \(|f^*| = 1\) is immediately a maximum flow!
Look at the edge \(e = (u \to v)\):

It is completely saturated: \(f^*(u \to v) = 1 = c(u \to v)\), so \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\).
Yet how many minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cuts of \(G\) contain \(e = (u \to v)\)? ZERO!
Why? Any \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((S, T)\) that cuts \(e = (u \to v)\) must place \(u \in S\) and \(v \in T\). Whether we place the bypass vertex \(w\) in \(S\) (cutting \(w \to v\)) or in \(T\) (cutting \(u \to w\)), the cut must also sever the bypass \(u \to w \to v\), giving cut capacity at least \(c(u \to v) + 1 = 2 > 1 = \lambda^*\)!
In the residual network \(G_{f^*}\), the reverse arc \(v \xrightarrow{1} u\) combines with the unused bypass \(u \xrightarrow{1} w \xrightarrow{1} v\) to form a directed residual cycle \(u \to w \to v \to u\). Thus \(\operatorname{scc}(u) = \operatorname{scc}(v)\), locking \(u\) and \(v\) onto the same side of every minimum cut!

Defensive Rule H-02: Never test \(c_{f^*}(u, v) = 0\) alone. Always run Tarjan’s SCC algorithm on \(G_{f^*}\) and verify \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\).




3.3 The [AHOI2009] Tarjan SCC Edge Classification Theorem
Given a directed network \(G = (V, E, c)\), we classify every physical edge \(e = (u \to v) \in E\) into two categories ([AHOI2009 / Luogu P4126] 最小割):

Feasible Minimum-Cut Edge (可行割边): There exists at least one minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) such that \(e \in \delta^+(S)\) (\(u \in S\) and \(v \notin S\)).
Essential Minimum-Cut Edge (必须割边): For every minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cut \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\), \(e \in \delta^+(S)\) (\(u \in S\) and \(v \notin S\)).







ImportantTheorem 3.2 (The [AHOI2009] Residual SCC Characterization Theorem)



Let \(f^*\) be any maximum \(s\)-\(t\) flow on \(G\), and let \(\operatorname{scc}(w)\) be the Strongly Connected Component ID of vertex \(w \in V\) in the residual network \(G_{f^*}\) (keeping only residual arcs with \(c_{f^*} > 0\)). Then for every physical edge \(e = (u \to v) \in E\) with \(c(e) > 0\):

Feasible Cut Edge (可行割边): \[\exists S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min} \text{ s.t. } e \in \delta^+(S) \iff c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0 \;\;\land\;\; \operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\]
Essential Cut Edge (必须割边): \[\forall S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min},\; e \in \delta^+(S) \iff c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0 \;\;\land\;\; \operatorname{scc}(u) = \operatorname{scc}(s) \;\;\land\;\; \operatorname{scc}(v) = \operatorname{scc}(t)\]




Wait — Why Doesn’t Condition (1) Need to Check \(u \not\leadsto t\) and \(s \not\leadsto v\)?
Look closely at Condition (1): to build a valid minimum cut \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) with \(u \in S\) and \(v \notin S\), we must ensure that placing \(u \in S\) does not force the sink \(t\) into \(S\) (i.e., \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\)), and keeping \(v \notin S\) does not exclude the source \(s\) from \(S\) (i.e., \(s \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\)). Why didn’t Theorem 3.2(1) have to check \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\) or \(s \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\)?
The answer is a remarkable hidden invariant of saturated cross-SCC edges: having \(f^*(u \to v) = c(u \to v) > 0\) and \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\) automatically forces \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} s\) and \(t \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\)! We give two complementary proofs of this lemma, as both techniques are indispensable for advanced flow problems.






NoteLemma 3.3 (Automatic Source/Sink Separation of Saturated Cross-SCC Edges)



If \(e = (u \to v) \in E\) satisfies \(f^*(e) = c(e) > 0\) (\(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\)) and \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\) in \(G_{f^*}\), then in \(G_{f^*}\):
\[u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} s \quad (\text{hence } u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t) \qquad \text{and} \qquad t \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v \quad (\text{hence } s \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v)\]




Proof 1 (Cut-Conservation Divergence Argument)
Because \(f^*(e) = c(e) > 0\), the reverse residual arc \(e^{\text{rev}} = (v \to u)\) has strictly positive residual capacity \(c_{f^*}(v \to u) = f^*(e) > 0\) in \(G_{f^*}\). Since \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\) and \(v \to u \in E_{f^*}\), there cannot be any residual path \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\).
Define \(R(u) := \{w \in V : u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} w\}\). By definition, \(u \in R(u)\), \(v \notin R(u)\), and no residual arc in \(G_{f^*}\) leaves \(R(u)\) (\(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(R(u)) = \emptyset\)). Consequently:

Every physical edge leaving \(R(u)\) is completely saturated (\(f^* = c\)), and every physical edge entering \(R(u)\) carries zero flow (\(f^* = 0\)).
Since \(e = (u \to v) \in \delta^+(R(u))\) has \(f^*(e) = c(e) > 0\), the net physical flow divergence out of \(R(u)\) is strictly positive: \[\sum_{w \in R(u)} \nabla \cdot f^*(w) = \sum_{e' \in \delta^+(R(u))} f^*(e') - \sum_{e' \in \delta^-(R(u))} f^*(e') \ge f^*(e) > 0\]
However, by Kirchhoff conservation, \(\nabla \cdot f^*(w) = 0\) for all \(w \in V \setminus \{s, t\}\), while \(\nabla \cdot f^*(t) = -|f^*| < 0\) and \(\nabla \cdot f^*(s) = +|f^*| > 0\). The only way \(\sum_{w \in R(u)} \nabla \cdot f^*(w) > 0\) can hold is if \(s \in R(u)\) and \(t \notin R(u)\)! Thus \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} s\) and \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\). Applying the exact same divergence argument to the reverse reachability set \(R^{-1}(v) := \{w \in V : w \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\}\) yields \(t \in R^{-1}(v)\) and \(s \notin R^{-1}(v)\). \(\blacksquare\)



Proof 2 (Flow Decomposition Path–Cycle Argument)
By the Flow Decomposition Theorem (Ch 01.4), decompose \(f^*\) into positive-weight directed \(s \leadsto t\) paths \(\mathcal{P}\) and directed cycles \(\mathcal{C}\). Since \(f^*(e) = c(e) > 0\), edge \(e = (u \to v)\) belongs either to some cycle \(C \in \mathcal{C}\) or to some \(s \leadsto t\) path \(P \in \mathcal{P}\):

If \(e \in C\), then every edge on \(C\) carries positive flow, so their reverse residual arcs in \(G_{f^*}\) form a directed path \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\) along the reversed cycle \(C\), contradicting \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\)!
Therefore, \(e\) must lie on a flow-carrying path \(P = (s \leadsto u \xrightarrow{e} v \leadsto t)\). In \(G_{f^*}\), the reverse residual arcs of the prefix \(s \leadsto u\) form a directed residual path \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} s\), and the reverse residual arcs of the suffix \(v \leadsto t\) form a directed residual path \(t \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\)! Since \(s \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\), these paths immediately imply \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\) and \(s \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\). \(\blacksquare\)



Completing the Proof of Theorem 3.2

Part 1 (Feasible Cut Edge):

\((\implies)\) If \(e \in \delta^+(S)\) for some \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\), then \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\) by complementary slackness, and since \(u \in S\), \(v \notin S\), and \(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\), we have \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\), so \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\).
\((\Longleftarrow)\) Conversely, if \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\) and \(\operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\), define \(S := \{w \in V : s \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} w \text{ or } u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} w\}\). By Lemma 3.3, \(v \notin S\) and \(t \notin S\), while \(s, u \in S\) and \(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\). Thus \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) is a valid minimum cut that severs \(e = (u \to v)\).

Part 2 (Essential Cut Edge):

Edge \(e = (u \to v)\) belongs to \(\delta^+(S)\) for every \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) if and only if \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\), \(u \in \bigcap_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S = S_{\min}\) (so \(s \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} u\)), and \(v \in \bigcap_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} (V \setminus S) = T_{\min}\) (so \(v \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\)).
Combining \(s \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} u\) with Lemma 3.3’s \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} s\) gives \(\operatorname{scc}(u) = \operatorname{scc}(s)\); combining \(v \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\) with Lemma 3.3’s \(t \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\) gives \(\operatorname{scc}(v) = \operatorname{scc}(t)\). \(\blacksquare\)






3.4 Complete Worked End-to-End Numerical Trace (Picard–Queyranne DAG & [AHOI2009])
Let us trace Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 3.2 by hand on a 6-vertex, 7-edge directed network \(G = (V, E, c)\) with \(V = \{s, u_1, u_2, v_1, v_2, t\}\):

Upper 3-edge chain: \(e_1 = (s \to u_1, c=3)\), \(e_2 = (u_1 \to u_2, c=3)\), \(e_3 = (u_2 \to t, c=3)\).
Lower 3-edge chain: \(e_4 = (s \to v_1, c=2)\), \(e_5 = (v_1 \to v_2, c=4)\), \(e_6 = (v_2 \to t, c=2)\).
Cross-chord: \(e_7 = (u_1 \to v_2, c=1)\).


Step 1: Maximum Flow \(f^*\) and Residual Capacities in \(G_{f^*}\)
Push \(3\) units along \(s \to u_1 \to u_2 \to t\) and \(2\) units along \(s \to v_1 \to v_2 \to t\), achieving the maximum flow \(|f^*| = 5\). The residual network \(G_{f^*}\) has the following arcs:

Step 2: Tarjan SCCs in \(G_{f^*}\) and the 4-Element Distributive Lattice \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\)
Let us inspect the Strongly Connected Components of \(G_{f^*}\) (using only positive-capacity residual arcs):

Because \(e_5 = (v_1 \to v_2)\) has both forward residual capacity \(2\) (\(v_1 \to v_2\)) and reverse residual capacity \(2\) (\(v_2 \to v_1\)), vertices \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) merge into a single component \(C_{v} = \{v_1, v_2\}\).
No other cycles exist in \(G_{f^*}\), so the 5 SCCs of \(\mathcal{D}(G_{f^*})\) are \(\{s\}\), \(\{u_1\}\), \(\{u_2\}\), \(C_v = \{v_1, v_2\}\), and \(\{t\}\), with directed condensation arcs: \[\{t\} \to \{u_2\} \to \{u_1\} \to \{s\}, \qquad \{t\} \to C_v \to \{s\}, \qquad \text{and the cross-arc } \{u_1\} \xrightarrow{e_7} C_v\]
Why the cross-chord \(e_7 = (u_1 \to v_2)\) matters: Because \(\{u_1\} \to C_v\) is a directed arc in \(\mathcal{D}(G_{f^*})\), Theorem 3.1 dictates that any out-closed ideal \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) containing \(u_1\) must also contain \(C_v = \{v_1, v_2\}\)! (Indeed, if \(u_1 \in S\) and \(v_2 \notin S\), then \(e_7\) would be cut in addition to \(e_2\) and \(e_4\), raising the cut capacity to \(3 + 2 + 1 = 6 > 5\).)
Thus \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\) consists of 4 minimum cuts (each of capacity \(5\)):

\(S_1 = S_{\min} = \{s\}\) — cuts \(\{e_1, e_4\}\) (\(3 + 2 = 5\)).
\(S_2 = \{s, v_1, v_2\}\) — cuts \(\{e_1, e_6\}\) (\(3 + 2 = 5\)).
\(S_3 = \{s, u_1, v_1, v_2\}\) — cuts \(\{e_2, e_6\}\) (\(3 + 2 = 5\)).
\(S_4 = S_{\max} = \{s, u_1, u_2, v_1, v_2\}\) — cuts \(\{e_3, e_6\}\) (\(3 + 2 = 5\)).

Why there are ZERO essential cut edges: Since \(\operatorname{scc}(s) = \{s\}\) and \(\operatorname{scc}(t) = \{t\}\), an essential cut edge would need to go directly from \(\{s\}\) to \(\{t\}\). None of \(e_1, \dots, e_6\) connect \(\{s\} \to \{t\}\), and indeed \(\bigcap_{i=1}^4 \delta^+(S_i) = \{e_1, e_4\} \cap \{e_3, e_6\} = \emptyset\).

title: Chapter 2 — Residual Graph Geometry, Cut Edge Classification, and Incremental Flow Rollback
section: 4. Minimum-Edge-Count Minimum Cut (\(W = M + 1\) Capacity Scaling vs. Two-Pass Residual Unit Network)
text:
4. Minimum-Edge-Count Minimum Cut (\(W = M + 1\) Capacity Scaling vs. Two-Pass Residual Unit Network)
Many problems ([USACO 4.4 / Luogu P1344] Polluted Milk, [HEOI2014] 南园满地堆轻絮) ask for a lexicographic dual objective: among all minimum \(s\)-\(t\) cuts \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\) (which minimize \(\kappa(S) = \sum_{e \in \delta^+(S)} c(e)\)), find one that simultaneously minimizes the number of cut edges \(|\delta^+(S)|\).

4.1 Method A: Lexicographic Base-\(W\) Capacity Perturbation (\(W = M + 1\))
How do we fold a secondary tie-breaking objective \(|\delta^+(S)| \in \{0, 1, \dots, M\}\) into a single scalar capacity function \(c'(e)\) without ever allowing the tie-breaker to override the primary objective \(\kappa(S)\)?
Choose base \(W := M + 1 = |E| + 1\), and define the perturbed integer capacity of every edge \(e \in E\) as:
\[c'(e) := c(e) \cdot (M + 1) + 1\]
For any \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((S, T)\), its perturbed cut capacity \(\kappa'(S)\) expands linearly as:
\[\kappa'(S) = \sum_{e \in \delta^+(S)} \big(c(e) \cdot (M + 1) + 1\big) = \underbrace{\kappa(S)}_{\text{primary weight}} \cdot (M + 1) \;+\; \underbrace{|\delta^+(S)|}_{\text{edge count } \in [0, M]}\]
Because every original capacity \(c(e)\) is an integer and the remainder satisfies \(0 \le |\delta^+(S)| \le M < M + 1\), Euclidean division of the minimum perturbed cut value \(F' = \min_{S} \kappa'(S)\) by \(W = M + 1\) uniquely recovers both answers in a single Dinic run:
\[\lambda^* = \min_{S} \kappa(S) = \left\lfloor \frac{F'}{M + 1} \right\rfloor, \qquad k^* = \min_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} |\delta^+(S)| = F' \bmod (M + 1)\]

[!CAUTION] Why Base \(W = M\) Fails When All \(M\) Edges Are Cut: If you set \(W = M\) instead of \(M + 1\) and the unique minimum cut happens to sever all \(M\) edges of the graph (\(|\delta^+(S^*)| = M\)), then \(F' = \lambda^* \cdot M + M = (\lambda^* + 1) \cdot M + 0\). Dividing by \(M\) outputs quotient \(\lambda^* + 1\) (off by \(+1\)) and remainder \(0\) (instead of \(M\))! Always use \(W = M + 1\) (or a convenient power of ten/two strictly exceeding \(M\), such as \(W = 2048\) when \(M \le 1000\)).



4.2 Method B: Two-Pass Residual Zero-Capacity / Unit-Network Reduction
What if original capacities \(c(e)\) are already up to \(10^{15}\) so multiplying by \(M + 1\) would overflow 64-bit integers (long long), or what if you want the second pass to run in fast \(O(E \min(V^{2/3}, E^{1/2}))\) unit-network time?

Pass 1: Run Dinic on the original capacities \(c(e)\) to obtain \(\lambda^* = |f^*|\) and the final residual network \(G_{f^*}\).
Pass 2 (Subtlety Warning!): It is often claimed in folklore that building a second network \(G^{(2)}\) with \(c^{(2)}(e) = 1\) if \(c_{f^*}(e) = 0\) and \(c^{(2)}(e) = \infty\) if \(c_{f^*}(e) > 0\) finds \(k^*\). Wait: what if \(G\) contains a saturated non-cut edge \(e = (u \to v)\) with \(\operatorname{scc}(u) = \operatorname{scc}(v)\) (as in FM-02), or what if cutting two non-saturated edges could falsely bypass \(\infty\)?

Because \(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\) is the exact characterization of \(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\), a partition \((S, V \setminus S)\) belongs to \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\) if and only if it cuts zero residual arcs of \(G_{f^*}\)!
Therefore, to restrict \(S\) strictly to \(\mathcal{L}_{\min}\) in Pass 2: for every residual arc \((x \to y) \in E_{f^*}\) with \(c_{f^*}(x \to y) > 0\) (including reverse residual arcs \(v \to u\) of flow-carrying edges!), add a directed arc \(x \xrightarrow{\infty} y\) in \(G^{(2)}\); and for every saturated physical edge \(e = (u \to v) \in E\) with \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\), add \(u \xrightarrow{1} v\) in \(G^{(2)}\).
Any finite-capacity \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((S, T)\) in \(G^{(2)}\) cannot cut any \(\infty\)-arc of \(E_{f^*}\), so \(\delta^+_{G_{f^*}}(S) = \emptyset\) (\(S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}\)), and its capacity in \(G^{(2)}\) is precisely \(|\delta^+_G(S)|\)!


In practice, whenever \(c(e) \cdot (M + 1) \le 4 \cdot 10^{18}\), Method A (\(W = M + 1\) perturbation) is 10 lines shorter and avoids constructing a second graph.

title: Chapter 2 — Residual Graph Geometry, Cut Edge Classification, and Incremental Flow Rollback
section: 5. Incremental Addition vs. Decremental Flow Rollback (退流) & Black-Box Contract
text:
5. Incremental Addition vs. Decremental Flow Rollback (退流) & Black-Box Contract
In dynamic or multi-query flow problems, the graph \(G\) undergoes edge additions, capacity upgrades, or edge deletions. Because Dinic maintains a valid residual network \(G_f\) at all times, we can operate directly on the live residual graph \(G_f\) instead of rebuilding from scratch.

5.1 Incremental Edge Additions & Parametric Capacity Sensitivity
Suppose we have already computed a maximum flow \(f^*\) with residual network \(G_{f^*}\):

Differential Capacity Sensitivity (\(\Delta c(e) = \pm \epsilon\) for infinitesimal \(\epsilon > 0\)):

Increasing \(c(e)\) by \(+\epsilon\) strictly increases the maximum flow (\(\lambda^*(c + \epsilon \mathbf{e}_e) = \lambda^*(c) + \epsilon\)) if and only if \(e\) belongs to every minimum cut (Essential Cut Edge: \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0 \land u \in S_{\min} \land v \in T_{\min}\)).
Decreasing \(c(e)\) by \(-\epsilon\) strictly decreases the maximum flow (\(\lambda^*(c - \epsilon \mathbf{e}_e) = \lambda^*(c) - \epsilon\)) if and only if \(e\) belongs to at least one minimum cut (Feasible Cut Edge: \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0 \land \operatorname{scc}(u) \neq \operatorname{scc}(v)\)).

Finite Incremental Addition (\(\Delta c(u \to v) = +K > 0\) or inserting a new edge):

Simply add \(+K\) to the forward residual capacity \(c_f(u \to v)\) inside the existing residual graph \(G_{f^*}\) and call dinic(s, t) without resetting prior flows!
If \(u \notin S_{\min}\) or \(v \notin T_{\min}\) (for a single edge upgrade), can a large \(+K\) increase flow if \(e\) wasn’t saturated? Only if \(e\) was already saturated (\(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\)) and \(s \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} u \land v \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} t\) (UVa 11248 / #010). Moreover, the re-augmentation pushes at most \(\min(K, \Delta F)\) units of additional flow, running in \(O(\Delta F \cdot E)\) time!




5.2 Decremental Flow Rollback (退流): Deleting an Active Edge in \(O(E)\) Time
What if we must decrease the capacity of an edge \(e = (u \to v)\) or permanently delete \(e\) (\(c(e) \gets 0\)) when \(e\) is already carrying strictly positive flow \(f_0 = f^*(u \to v) > 0\)?
If we naively set \(c_f(u \to v) = 0\) and \(c_f(v \to u) = 0\) without adjusting the rest of the network, we destroy Kirchhoff flow conservation: vertex \(u\) now has \(+f_0\) units of stranded incoming flow from \(s\) that nowhere exits \(u\), and vertex \(v\) has \(+f_0\) units of outgoing flow to \(t\) that never entered \(v\)!






ImportantAlgorithm 5.1 (The 3-Step Surgical Flow Rollback / 退流 Protocol)



To delete a physical directed edge \(e = (u \to v)\) currently carrying flow \(f_0 = c(e) - c_{f^*}(u \to v) \ge 0\) in a converged residual network \(G_{f^*}\):

Case \(f_0 = 0\) (Zero-Flow Edge): Simply zero out the forward residual arc \(c_{f^*}(u \to v) \gets 0\) (and \(c_{f^*}(v \to u) \gets 0\)). Conservation is untouched; no flow adjustments are needed.
Case \(f_0 > 0\) (Flow-Carrying Edge):

Step 1 (Reel Back Suffix & Prefix Flow): Before or immediately after zeroing out \((u, v)\), push exactly \(f_0\) units of flow from \(t\) to \(v\) (dinic_bounded(t, v, f_0)) and \(f_0\) units of flow from \(u\) to \(s\) (dinic_bounded(u, s, f_0)) in the residual network \(G_{f^*}\) (with \(e\) zeroed out: \(c_f(u \to v) = c_f(v \to u) = 0\)).

Why does this work? Pushing \(f_0\) units along residual paths \(t \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\) traverses the reverse residual arcs of \(v \leadsto t\), canceling \(f_0\) units of suffix flow from \(v\) to \(t\). Pushing \(f_0\) units along \(u \leadsto_{G_{f^*}} s\) traverses the reverse residual arcs of \(s \leadsto u\), canceling \(f_0\) units of prefix flow from \(s\) to \(u\).

Step 2 (Sever the Edge): Ensure both half-edges of \(e\) have residual capacity \(0\): cap[e] = cap[e ^ 1] = 0. Now Kirchhoff conservation holds at every vertex \(w \in V \setminus \{s, t\}\), with valid net flow \(|f| = |f^*| - f_0\).
Step 3 (Optional Re-Augmentation \(s \leadsto t\)): Run dinic(s, t) to push back any flow that can bypass \(e\).

Crucial Shortcut for Feasible Min-Cut Edges ([SDOI2014] LIS / #015): If \(e = (u \to v)\) was verified to be a Feasible Minimum-Cut Edge (\(c_{f^*}(u \to v) = 0\) and \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\)), then deleting \(e\) reduces the global minimum cut of \(G\) by exactly \(f_0 = c(e)\)! Therefore, after Step 1 reels back \(f_0\) units via dinic(t, v, f_0) and dinic(u, s, f_0), the resulting flow \(|f^*| - f_0\) is already a maximum flow of \(G \setminus \{e\}\), so Step 3 (dinic(s, t)) can be skipped entirely!







5.3 Time-Reversal for Offline Deletions (CF 1139E) & The 4-Step Compilation Pipeline
When a problem gives all edge deletions offline in advance (CF 1139E Maximize Mex / #012) and asks for the maximum flow / matching after each deletion, always ask before implementing 退流: Can we reverse time? Processing queries from day \(D\) backward to day \(1\) turns edge deletions into monotone edge insertions, allowing us to maintain a single growing residual graph where the answer only increases!









Target Structural Query
Algebraic / Residual Characterization
Mechanical Graph / Residual Compilation
Post-Dinic Time Complexity




Source-Minimal / Source-Maximal Cut (\(S_{\min}, S_{\max}\))
\(S_{\min} = \bigcap_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S\), \(S_{\max} = \bigcup_{S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}} S\)
Forward BFS from \(s\) in \(G_{f^*}\) gives \(S_{\min}\); reverse BFS from \(t\) gives \(T_{\min} = V \setminus S_{\max}\).
\(O(V + E)\)


Minimum-Cut Uniqueness (ZOJ 2587)
\(|\mathcal{L}_{\min}| = 1 \iff S_{\min} = S_{\max}\)
Check if \(S_{\min} \cup T_{\min} = V\) (\(|S_{\min}| + |T_{\min}| = |V|\)).
\(O(V + E)\)


Feasible Cut Edge (可行割边, P4126)
\(\exists S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}: e \in \delta^+(S)\)
Tarjan SCC on \(G_{f^*}\): cap[e] == 0 && scc[u] != scc[v].
\(O(V + E)\)


Essential Cut Edge (必须割边, P4126)
\(\forall S \in \mathcal{L}_{\min}: e \in \delta^+(S)\)
Tarjan SCC on \(G_{f^*}\): cap[e] == 0 && scc[u] == scc[s] && scc[v] == scc[t].
\(O(V + E)\)


Min-Edge-Count Min-Cut (P1344)
\(\operatorname{lex\ min} (\kappa(S), |\delta^+(S)|)\)
Perturb \(c'(e) = c(e)(M+1) + 1\); output \(\lfloor F'/(M+1)\rfloor\) and \(F' \bmod (M+1)\).
\(1 \times \text{Dinic}\)


Lexicographically First Min-Cut (P3308)
Commit feasible edges \(e_i\) in priority order
Test \(u \not\leadsto_{G_{f^*}} v\); if true, zero \(e_i\) and rollback dinic(t, v, c) + dinic(u, s, c).
\(O(N \cdot M\sqrt{N})\)

section: 7. Chapter 2 Verification Checklist & Failure Mode Summary
text:
7. Chapter 2 Verification Checklist & Failure Mode Summary
Before submitting any problem involving minimum-cut classification, uniqueness, edge-count minimization, or dynamic flow updates, run through this defensive audit:

Defensive Rule H-02 (No Naked Saturation Checks): Did you check cap[e] == 0 alone to classify a minimum-cut edge? Stop! A saturated edge \(e = (u \to v)\) can lie on a zero-net-cut residual cycle (FM-02). Always run Tarjan’s SCC on \(G_{f^*}\) (traversing only half-edges with cap > 0) and check:

Feasible (可行割边): cap[e] == 0 && scc[u] != scc[v].
Essential (必须割边): cap[e] == 0 && scc[u] == scc[s] && scc[v] == scc[t].

Full-Graph Tarjan Loop: In P4126 [AHOI2009], did you loop for (int i = 1; i <= N; ++i) if (!dfn[i]) tarjan(i); across all vertices? Calling tarjan(s) alone only visits \(S_{\min}\) and leaves scc[t] = 0!
Perturbation Base \(W = M + 1\): In minimum-cardinality min-cut (P1344), did you use \(W = M + 1\) (and 64-bit long long) instead of \(W = M\)?
Surgical Rollback (退流) Order of Operations: When deleting a committed feasible cut edge \(e = (u \to v)\) in [SDOI2014] LIS (P3308), did you zero out both cap[e] = 0 and cap[e ^ 1] = 0 before calling max_flow(T, v) and max_flow(u, S)?
Two-Commodity Target Swap: On an undirected 2-commodity flow problem (P3163 危桥), did you run Dinic twice—once with \((b_1 \to b_2)\) and once with \((b_2 \to b_1)\)—and require both runs to saturate \(2(a_n + b_n)\)?

title: Chapter 4 — Flows with Demands, Lower-Bound Circulations, Hoffman’s Theorem, and Matrix Rounding
text:
Prerequisites: Chapter 1 (Kirchhoff conservation, residual networks, Dinic’s algorithm, Integrality Theorem), Chapter 2 (residual reachability \(S_{\min}^*\), minimum cut extraction), and Chapter 3 (vertex splitting, time-expanded DAGs, and Rank-2 bipartite factorization).
Learning Objectives:

Derive the Affine Slack Shift \(f(e) = l(e) + \tilde{f}(e)\) from first principles, transforming box-constrained flows \(l(e) \le f(e) \le u(e)\) with vertex demands \(b(v)\) into standard \([0, u(e) - l(e)]\) flows with pre-injected nodal excess \(M(v) = \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} l(e) - b(v)\).
Master the exact 2-Phase Compilation Protocols for all four lower-bound flow variants (上下界网络流):

Variant 1: Sourceless Feasible Circulation (无源汇上下界可行流, LOJ #115).
Variant 2: Feasible \(s\)-\(t\) Flow with Lower Bounds (有源汇上下界可行流) via the feedback arc \(e_{\text{fb}} = (t \to s, [0, \infty))\).
Variant 3: Maximum \(s\)-\(t\) Flow with Lower Bounds (有源汇上下界最大流, LOJ #116) via \(F_{\max} = f_0 + \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(s, t)\).
Variant 4: Minimum \(s\)-\(t\) Flow with Lower Bounds (有源汇上下界最小流, LOJ #117) via backward residual cancellation \(F_{\min} = f_0 - \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(t, s)\).

Prove Hoffman’s Circulation Theorem (1960) using Max-Flow Min-Cut duality on the auxiliary network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\), and extract an explicit maximum-violation witness subset \(X^* = S_{\min}^* \setminus \{S^*\}\) whenever Phase 1 fails.
Compile three major non-graph problem families—Real-Valued Matrix / Contingency-Table Rounding (Baranyai's Rounding Lemma), Mixed-Graph Eulerian Circuit Orientation, and DAG Minimum Path/Fleet Cover—into lower-bound circulations without guesswork.
Guard against the canonical implementation bugs: Lower-Bound Sign Inversion (\(M(v)\) direction swap), Feedback-Edge Leakage (failing to zero out both half-edges of \(t \to s\) before Phase 2), Slack Offset Omission (FM-05), and Mixed Eulerian Parity Omission (FM-06).

title: Chapter 4 — Flows with Demands, Lower-Bound Circulations, Hoffman’s Theorem, and Matrix Rounding
section: 1. Motivation: When Edges Have Minimum Quotas and Vertices Have Mandatory Balances
text:
1. Motivation: When Edges Have Minimum Quotas and Vertices Have Mandatory Balances
In Chapters 1 through 3, every capacity constraint had the one-sided box form \(0 \le f(e) \le u(e)\) and every interior vertex obeyed homogeneous conservation \(\text{div}_f(v) = 0\). Crucially, the all-zero flow \(f \equiv 0\) was always a valid starting point in the feasible polytope, allowing Dinic’s algorithm to start at \(f = 0\) and greedily augment towards optimality.
In many contest and operations-research models, however, \(f \equiv 0\) is strictly infeasible:

Pressurized Cooling Pipes & Supply Contracts (ZOJ 2314): Every pipe \(e = (u \to v)\) in a closed nuclear reactor loop must carry at least \(l(e) > 0\) liters/sec of coolant to prevent overheating, while never exceeding its burst limit \(u(e)\).
Mandatory Edge/Vertex Coverage on a DAG (Luogu P4843 清理雪道): A fleet of snowplows must traverse a mountain trail network so that every ski trail \(e\) is cleared at least once (\(1 \le f(e) \le \infty\)), using the minimum possible number of snowplow runs from the summit \(s\) to the base lodge \(t\).
Matrix & Statistical Table Rounding (POJ 2396, BZOJ 3698): Each cell \(X_{i,j}\) of an integer matrix must lie in a prescribed interval \([L_{i,j}, R_{i,j}]\) (or \(\{\lfloor A_{i,j} \rfloor, \lceil A_{i,j} \rceil\}\)), while row and column sums must fall into target intervals \([\underline{r}_i, \overline{r}_i]\) and \([\underline{c}_j, \overline{c}_j]\).
Daily and Cumulative Quotas ([ZJOI2010] Shoot the Bullet): On day \(i\), a photographer takes between \(L_{i,j}\) and \(R_{i,j}\) photos of subject \(j\), capped at \(D_i\) total photos on day \(i\), while guaranteeing at least \(G_j\) cumulative photos of subject \(j\) across the entire season.

Whenever decision variables are bounded from both below and above (\(l(e) \le f(e) \le u(e)\) with \(l(e) > 0\)) or vertices have mandatory net demands \(b(v) \neq 0\), a single call to standard dinic(s, t) cannot even start: the zero flow violates every positive lower bound. Nor can we simply run standard Max-Flow with capacities \(u(e)\) and “hope” the flow on \(e\) exceeds \(l(e)\)—maximizing total throughput frequently starves side branches that have mandatory minimum quotas.
To compile lower-bound constraints into a standard Dinic solver, we need an algebraic transformation that shifts the origin of the flow polytope from \(0\) to \(l(e)\).

title: Chapter 4 — Flows with Demands, Lower-Bound Circulations, Hoffman’s Theorem, and Matrix Rounding
section: 2. The Affine Slack Shift \(f(e) = l(e) + \tilde{f}(e)\) and the Four Lower-Bound Flow Variants (上下界网络流)
text:
2. The Affine Slack Shift \(f(e) = l(e) + \tilde{f}(e)\) and the Four Lower-Bound Flow Variants (上下界网络流)

2.1 Step 1 & Step 2: Algebraic Derivation of Pre-Injected Nodal Excess \(M(v)\)
Consider a directed network \(\mathcal{N} = (V, E, l, u, b)\) where:

Each directed edge \(e = (u \to v) \in E\) has an integer lower bound \(l(e)\) and upper bound \(u(e)\) satisfying \(0 \le l(e) \le u(e)\). (If \(l(e) > u(e)\) for any edge, the system is immediately infeasible.)
Each vertex \(v \in V\) has a prescribed net demand/divergence \(b(v) \in \mathbb{Z}\), defined as mandatory net outflow minus inflow: \[\text{div}_f(v) \triangleq \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} f(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} f(e) = b(v) \qquad \forall v \in V\] In a pure sourceless circulation, \(b(v) = 0\) for all \(v \in V\). When \(b(v) > 0\), vertex \(v\) is a net producer (must inject \(b(v)\) units into the network); when \(b(v) < 0\), vertex \(v\) is a net consumer (must absorb \(-b(v)\) units from the network). Since every edge \(e = (u \to v)\) contributes \(+f(e)\) to \(\text{div}_f(u)\) and \(-f(e)\) to \(\text{div}_f(v)\), summing over all \(v \in V\) yields the necessary global conservation check: \[\sum_{v \in V} b(v) = \sum_{v \in V} \text{div}_f(v) = 0.\]


The Affine Slack Shift
To restore standard zero-lower-bound box constraints, we decompose the physical flow \(f(e)\) on each edge \(e \in E\) into its mandatory baseline quota \(l(e)\) plus a non-negative free slack flow \(\tilde{f}(e)\): \[f(e) = l(e) + \tilde{f}(e), \qquad 0 \le \tilde{f}(e) \le u(e) - l(e) \triangleq \tilde{c}(e).\]
Now substitute \(f(e) = l(e) + \tilde{f}(e)\) directly into the vertex balance equation \(\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} f(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} f(e) = b(v)\): \[\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \big(l(e) + \tilde{f}(e)\big) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \big(l(e) + \tilde{f}(e)\big) = b(v).\]
Separate the unknown slack variables \(\tilde{f}(e)\) on the left-hand side and move all known constants \(l(e)\) and \(b(v)\) to the right-hand side: \[\underbrace{\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \tilde{f}(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \tilde{f}(e)}_{\text{div}_{\tilde{f}}(v) \text{ (Net Slack Outflow from } v\text{)}} = \underbrace{\sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} l(e) - b(v)}_{M(v) \text{ (Pre-Injected Net Excess at } v\text{)}}.\]
We call \(M(v)\) the Pre-Injected Net Excess (or Mandatory Baseline Imbalance) at vertex \(v\): \[M(v) \triangleq \text{in}_l(v) - \text{out}_l(v) - b(v) = \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} l(e) - b(v).\]
Notice that as long as \(\sum_{v \in V} b(v) = 0\), the sum of \(M(v)\) across all vertices identically vanishes: \[\sum_{v \in V} M(v) = \sum_{e \in E} l(e) - \sum_{e \in E} l(e) - \sum_{v \in V} b(v) = 0.\]




2.2 Step 3: Mechanical Graph Compilation into Super-Terminals \(S^*\) and \(T^*\)
How do we enforce \(\text{div}_{\tilde{f}}(v) = M(v)\) for every \(v \in V\) using a standard zero-divergence max-flow solver? Let us trace the physical meaning of \(\text{div}_{\tilde{f}}(v) = M(v)\):

Case 1: \(M(v) > 0\) (Pre-Injected Surplus at \(v\)): Pre-sending \(l(e)\) along every edge delivers \(M(v)\) more mandatory units into \(v\) than are required to leave \(v\). To balance the books at \(v\), the slack flow \(\tilde{f}\) must satisfy \(\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \tilde{f}(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \tilde{f}(e) = M(v) > 0\)—that is, \(v\) must emit a net surplus of \(M(v)\) units of slack flow out into the rest of the network.

Gadget Compilation: Create an auxiliary Super-Source \(S^*\) and add a directed companion arc \(S^* \to v\) with capacity \(M(v)\). If this arc is saturated (\(\tilde{f}(S^* \to v) = M(v)\)), standard conservation at \(v\) in the augmented network forces \(\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \tilde{f}(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \tilde{f}(e) = \tilde{f}(S^* \to v) = M(v)\)!

Case 2: \(M(v) < 0\) (Pre-Injected Deficit at \(v\)): Pre-sending \(l(e)\) along every edge drains \(|M(v)| = -M(v)\) more mandatory units out of \(v\) than arrive at \(v\). To replenish this deficit, the slack flow \(\tilde{f}\) must satisfy \(\sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \tilde{f}(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \tilde{f}(e) = -M(v) > 0\)—that is, \(v\) must absorb a net inflow of \(-M(v)\) units of slack flow from the rest of the network.

Gadget Compilation: Create an auxiliary Super-Sink \(T^*\) and add a directed companion arc \(v \to T^*\) with capacity \(-M(v) = |M(v)|\). If this arc is saturated (\(\tilde{f}(v \to T^*) = -M(v)\)), standard conservation at \(v\) forces \(\sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \tilde{f}(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \tilde{f}(e) = \tilde{f}(v \to T^*) = -M(v)\)!

Case 3: \(M(v) = 0\) (Pre-Balanced Vertex): The mandatory baseline flows already balance at \(v\); no companion arc to \(S^*\) or \(T^*\) is needed.

Define the Total Mandatory Positive Imbalance: \[\Sigma^+ \triangleq \sum_{v \in V : M(v) > 0} M(v) = \sum_{v \in V : M(v) < 0} \big(-M(v)\big).\]
Since no companion arc can carry flow exceeding its capacity, \(\tilde{f}\) saturates every companion arc out of \(S^*\) (and consequently every companion arc into \(T^*\)) if and only if the maximum \(S^*\)-\(T^*\) flow in the auxiliary network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\) equals \(\Sigma^+\).

    v -->|"slack cap = u(e) - l(e)"| u["Deficit Node u\nin_l(u) - out_l(u) < 0"]

[!CAUTION] Broken-Gadget Counterexample — Reversing the Sign of \(M(v)\): The single most frequent error in 上下界网络流 is defining \(M(v) = \text{out}_l(v) - \text{in}_l(v)\) and wiring \(S^* \to v\) when \(\text{out}_l(v) > \text{in}_l(v)\).
1-Second Mnemonic Check on a 2-Node Loop: Suppose \(u \to v\) has mandatory bounds \([1, 1]\) (slack capacity \(1 - 1 = 0\)) and \(v \to u\) has free bounds \([0, 1]\) (slack capacity \(1\)).

Because \(1\) mandatory unit is pre-sent along \(u \to v\), vertex \(v\) receives \(1\) unit of baseline flow and must push \(1\) unit of slack flow back from \(v\) to \(u\) along the free return pipe \(v \to u\).
For slack flow in \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\) to travel from \(v\) to \(u\), \(S^*\) must inject flow into \(v\) (\(S^* \to v\), where \(\text{in}_l(v) - \text{out}_l(v) = 1 - 0 = +1 > 0\)) and \(u\) must drain into \(T^*\) (\(u \to T^*\), where \(\text{in}_l(u) - \text{out}_l(u) = 0 - 1 = -1 < 0\)).





2.3 Complete 2-Phase Protocols for the Four Lower-Bound Flow Variants
When the original network has a designated source \(s\) and sink \(t\) (Variants 2, 3, 4), conservation holds at all interior vertices \(v \in V \setminus \{s, t\}\), while \(s\) emits net flow \(|f|\) and \(t\) absorbs net flow \(|f|\). How do we reduce an \(s\)-\(t\) flow to a sourceless circulation (Variant 1)?
The Feedback Arc Reduction: Add a single virtual feedback arc \(e_{\text{fb}} = (t \to s)\) with lower bound \(l(e_{\text{fb}}) = 0\) and upper bound \(u(e_{\text{fb}}) = \infty\). Any flow \(f_0\) arriving at \(t\) from the physical network can now return from \(t\) to \(s\) along \(e_{\text{fb}}\), restoring strict conservation \(\text{div}_f(v) = 0\) at every vertex \(v \in V\) (including \(s\) and \(t\))! Moreover, the flow carried by the feedback arc is equal to the net \(s\)-\(t\) throughput of the physical network: \[|f| = f(e_{\text{fb}}) = \tilde{f}(t \to s) = c_{\tilde{f}}(s \to t)\] where \(c_{\tilde{f}}(s \to t) = \text{cap}[e_{\text{fb}} \oplus 1]\) is the residual capacity of the reverse half-edge of \(e_{\text{fb}}\) after Phase 1.









Variant
Problem Specification
Phase 1: Feasibility Setup on \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\)
Phase 2: Optimization & Physical Flow Reconstruction




Variant 1: Feasible Circulation (无源汇上下界可行流, LOJ #115)
\(\text{div}_f(v) = b(v) \;\;\forall v \in V\), \(l(e) \le f(e) \le u(e)\).
Add each \(e = (u \to v)\) with cap \(u(e) - l(e)\); add \(S^* \to v\) (cap \(M(v)\) if \(M(v)>0\)) and \(v \to T^*\) (cap \(-M(v)\) if \(M(v)<0\)). Run \(F_1 = \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^*, T^*)\).
Feasible \(\iff F_1 = \Sigma^+\). Physical flow on edge \(e_k\) is \(f(e_k) = l(e_k) + \tilde{f}(e_k) = l(e_k) + \text{cap}[\text{rev}(e_k)]\).


Variant 2: Feasible \(s\)-\(t\) Flow (有源汇上下界可行流)
\(\text{div}_f(v) = 0 \;\;\forall v \notin \{s, t\}\), \(l(e) \le f(e) \le u(e)\).
Add feedback arc \(e_{\text{fb}} = (t \to s)\) with \([l, u] = [0, \infty)\) and run Variant 1 Phase 1: \(F_1 = \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^*, T^*)\).
Feasible \(\iff F_1 = \Sigma^+\). Initial feasible \(s\)-\(t\) flow value is \(f_0 = \tilde{f}(e_{\text{fb}}) = \text{cap}[e_{\text{fb}} \oplus 1]\) (not \(F_1\)!).


Variant 3: Maximum \(s\)-\(t\) Flow (有源汇上下界最大流, LOJ #116)
Maximize \(|f|\) subject to Variant 2 constraints.
Run Variant 2 Phase 1 (MaxFlow(S*, T*) with \(t \xrightarrow{[0, \infty)} s\)). If \(F_1 < \Sigma^+\), return INFEASIBLE.
Read \(f_0 = \text{cap}[e_{\text{fb}} \oplus 1]\). Zero out both half-edges of \(e_{\text{fb}}\) (cap[e_fb] = cap[e_fb ^ 1] = 0). Run \(f_{\text{add}} = \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}}(s, t)\). Return \(F_{\max} = f_0 + f_{\text{add}}\).


Variant 4: Minimum \(s\)-\(t\) Flow (有源汇上下界最小流, LOJ #117)
Minimize \(|f|\) subject to Variant 2 constraints.
Run Variant 2 Phase 1 (MaxFlow(S*, T*) with \(t \xrightarrow{[0, \infty)} s\)). If \(F_1 < \Sigma^+\), return INFEASIBLE.
Read \(f_0 = \text{cap}[e_{\text{fb}} \oplus 1]\). Zero out both half-edges of \(e_{\text{fb}}\) (cap[e_fb] = cap[e_fb ^ 1] = 0). Push flow backward from \(t\) to \(s\): \(f_{\text{sub}} = \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}}(t, s)\). Return \(F_{\min} = f_0 - f_{\text{sub}}\).




Proving the Three Structural Invariants of Phase 2

Why does Phase 2 preserve every lower bound and interior conservation without touching \(S^*\) and \(T^*\)? When Phase 1 succeeds (\(F_1 = \Sigma^+\)), every companion arc \(S^* \to v\) is completely saturated (forward residual capacity \(0\), and no edge enters \(S^*\)), and every companion arc \(v \to T^*\) is completely saturated (forward residual capacity \(0\), and no edge leaves \(T^*\)). Thus in the residual network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\), no directed path from \(s\) to \(t\) (or from \(t\) to \(s\)) can ever visit \(S^*\) or \(T^*\)! Furthermore, every physical edge \(e\) has forward residual capacity \(u(e) - f(e)\) and reverse residual capacity \(f(e) - l(e)\), so augmenting in \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\) keeps \(f(e) \in [l(e), u(e)]\) invariant.
Why MUST we zero out BOTH half-edges of \(e_{\text{fb}} = (t \to s)\) before Phase 2? After Phase 1, the forward arc \(t \to s\) has residual capacity \(\infty\), and the reverse arc \(s \to t\) has residual capacity \(f_0\).

If we leave cap[e_fb] = inf during Variant 4 (MaxFlow(t, s)), Dinic will immediately push \(\infty\) units directly along \(t \to s\), yielding \(F_{\min} = -\infty\)!
If we leave cap[e_fb ^ 1] = f_0 during Variant 3 (MaxFlow(s, t)), Dinic will push \(f_0\) units along the reverse arc \(s \to t\), double-counting \(f_0\) if we compute \(f_0 + \text{MaxFlow}(s, t)\). Zeroing out both cap[e_fb] = 0 and cap[e_fb ^ 1] = 0 locks \(f_0\) in place so \(F_{\max} = f_0 + \text{MaxFlow}(s, t)\) and \(F_{\min} = f_0 - \text{MaxFlow}(t, s)\) hold symmetrically.

Why does \(F_{\min} = f_0 - \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}}(t, s)\) find the exact minimum feasible \(s\)-\(t\) flow? Any augmenting path from \(t\) to \(s\) in the residual network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\) reduces the net \(s \to t\) flow by \(1\) unit per unit pushed while keeping \(l(e) \le f(e) \le u(e)\) and \(\text{div}_f(v) = 0\) (\(\forall v \notin \{s, t\}\)). By applying the Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem to \((t, s)\) on \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\), no further reduction is possible once \(t \not\leadsto s\) in \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\), reaching the global minimum: \[F_{\min}(s, t) = \max_{(S, T) \text{ an } s\text{-}t \text{ cut}} \left( \sum_{e \in \delta^+(S)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(S)} u(e) \right).\]





2.4 Step 4: Worked Numerical Trace (Variants 2, 3, and 4) & FM-05 Trap
Let us trace all three \(s\)-\(t\) variants by hand on a 4-vertex network \(V = \{s, a, b, t\}\) with 5 bounded edges:

\(e_1 = (s \to a)\) with \([l_1, u_1] = [2, 5]\) (slack capacity \(\tilde{c}_1 = 3\))
\(e_2 = (s \to b)\) with \([l_2, u_2] = [1, 4]\) (slack capacity \(\tilde{c}_2 = 3\))
\(e_3 = (a \to b)\) with \([l_3, u_3] = [1, 3]\) (slack capacity \(\tilde{c}_3 = 2\))
\(e_4 = (a \to t)\) with \([l_4, u_4] = [1, 4]\) (slack capacity \(\tilde{c}_4 = 3\))
\(e_5 = (b \to t)\) with \([l_5, u_5] = [2, 6]\) (slack capacity \(\tilde{c}_5 = 4\))


Phase 1: Pre-Injected Imbalances \(M(v)\) and Feasibility (MaxFlow(S*, T*))
Add feedback arc \(e_{\text{fb}} = (t \to s)\) with \([0, \infty)\). Compute \(M(v) = \text{in}_l(v) - \text{out}_l(v)\) from \(l = (2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0)\):

\(M(s) = 0 - (2 + 1) = -3 < 0 \implies\) add companion arc \(s \to T^*\) with capacity \(3\).
\(M(a) = 2 - (1 + 1) = 0 \implies\) balanced (\(0\)).
\(M(b) = (1 + 1) - 2 = 0 \implies\) balanced (\(0\)).
\(M(t) = (1 + 2) - 0 = +3 > 0 \implies\) add companion arc \(S^* \to t\) with capacity \(3\).
Total positive imbalance: \(\Sigma^+ = 3\).

Suppose during MaxFlow(S*, T*), Dinic first explores an interior path \(S^* \xrightarrow{2} t \xrightarrow{e_{\text{fb}}} s \xrightarrow{e_1} a \xrightarrow{e_4} t\) (Wait—actually \(t\) is already near \(S^*\), or suppose \(M(a)\) had surplus, or suppose we had an extra edge). Here, MaxFlow(S*, T*) pushes \(3\) units along \(S^* \xrightarrow{3} t \xrightarrow{e_{\text{fb}}} s \xrightarrow{3} T^*\), achieving \(F_1 = 3 = \Sigma^+\).

Feasible \(s\)-\(t\) Flow (Variant 2): \(f_0 = \tilde{f}(e_{\text{fb}}) = 3\), with physical flows \(f^{(0)} = l + \tilde{f} = (2, 1, 1, 1, 2)\).
Lock the Feedback Arc: Set cap[e_fb] = cap[e_fb ^ 1] = 0.



Phase 2A: Maximum Flow (Variant 3)
From \(f^{(0)} = (2, 1, 1, 1, 2)\), the remaining forward slack capacities are \(\tilde{c} = (3, 3, 2, 3, 4)\). Running MaxFlow(s, t) on \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\) pushes:

\(3\) units along \(s \xrightarrow{e_1} a \xrightarrow{e_4} t\), and
\(3\) units along \(s \xrightarrow{e_2} b \xrightarrow{e_5} t\),

giving \(f_{\text{add}} = 6\) and \(F_{\max} = f_0 + f_{\text{add}} = 3 + 6 = 9\), with physical flows \(f^{\max} = l + \tilde{f} = (2+3, 1+3, 1+0, 1+3, 2+3) = (5, 4, 1, 4, 5)\).


Phase 2B: Minimum Flow (Variant 4)
What if Phase 1 had instead routed \(1\) extra unit through the interior (for instance, if an edge had forced \(f^{(0)} = (3, 1, 1, 2, 2)\) with \(f_0 = 4\))? Then in \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}\), the reverse arcs \((t \to a)\) and \((a \to s)\) would both have residual capacity \(1\). Running MaxFlow(t, s) would push \(f_{\text{sub}} = 1\) unit backward along \(t \to a \to s\), peeling the excess flow back and recovering \(F_{\min} = f_0 - f_{\text{sub}} = 4 - 1 = 3\)!

[!WARNING] Broken-Gadget Counterexample FM-05 — Lower-Bound Slack Offset Omission Trap: After Dinic finishes on \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\), the reverse half-edge cap[rev(e)] stores only the slack flow \(\tilde{f}(e) \in [0, u(e) - l(e)]\), not the physical flow \(f(e)\)!

Edge Reconstruction Trap: Printing cap[rev(e)] directly instead of \(l(e) + \text{cap}[\text{rev}(e)]\) under-reports every edge flow by \(l(e)\) (ZOJ 2314, POJ 2396).
Source-Cut / Total-Flow Offset Trap: If you compute the \(s\)-\(t\) flow value by summing cap[rev(e)] over edges leaving \(s\) without adding \(\sum_{e \in \delta^+(s)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(s)} l(e)\), your answer omits the pre-sent baseline flow! Reading \(f_0 = \text{cap}[e_{\text{fb}} \oplus 1]\) directly from the feedback arc’s reverse edge avoids this bug because \(l(e_{\text{fb}}) = 0\), so \(f(e_{\text{fb}}) = 0 + \tilde{f}(e_{\text{fb}})\) already includes all baseline flow cycling through \(t \to s\).

title: Chapter 4 — Flows with Demands, Lower-Bound Circulations, Hoffman’s Theorem, and Matrix Rounding
section: 3. Hoffman’s Circulation Theorem & Extracting Infeasibility Certificates from \(S_{\min}^*\)
text:
3. Hoffman’s Circulation Theorem & Extracting Infeasibility Certificates from \(S_{\min}^*\)
When does a sourceless network \(\mathcal{N} = (V, E, l, u)\) with \(0 \le l(e) \le u(e)\) admit a feasible circulation (\(\text{div}_f(v) = 0 \;\;\forall v \in V\))? And when Phase 1 fails (\(F_1 < \Sigma^+\)), can we extract a concrete combinatorial witness proving to the user why no circulation exists?

3.1 Theorem 3.1 (Hoffman’s Circulation Theorem, 1960)
A network \(\mathcal{N} = (V, E, l, u)\) with \(0 \le l(e) \le u(e)\) admits a feasible circulation \(f: E \to \mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(l(e) \le f(e) \le u(e)\) and \(\text{div}_f(v) = 0\) (\(\forall v \in V\)) if and only if for every vertex subset \(X \subseteq V\), the total mandatory lower bound entering \(X\) does not exceed the total upper-bound capacity leaving \(X\): \[\sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} l(e) \le \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} u(e) \qquad \forall X \subseteq V\] (or equivalently, replacing \(X\) by its complement \(V \setminus X\), \(\sum_{e \in \delta^+(Y)} l(e) \le \sum_{e \in \delta^-(Y)} u(e)\) for all \(Y \subseteq V\)). Moreover, if \(l\) and \(u\) are integral and the condition holds, an integral circulation \(f: E \to \mathbb{Z}\) exists.

Proof via Max-Flow Min-Cut Duality on \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\)

Necessity (\(\implies\)): Suppose \(f\) is a valid circulation. Summing vertex conservation \(\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} f(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} f(e) = 0\) over all \(v \in X\) cancels all internal edges with both endpoints in \(X\), leaving boundary conservation: \[\sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} l(e) \le \sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} f(e) = \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} f(e) \le \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} u(e).\]
Sufficiency (\(\impliedby\)) & Exact Cut Identity: By Section 2.2, a feasible circulation exists if and only if \(\text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^*, T^*) = \Sigma^+\). By the Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem (Chapter 1), this holds if and only if every \(S^*\)-\(T^*\) cut \((S^* \sqcup X, T^* \sqcup \bar{X})\) in \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\) (where \(\bar{X} = V \setminus X\)) has cut capacity \(\kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X) \ge \Sigma^+\). Let us expand \(\kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X)\) explicitly. An arc of \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\) crosses from \(S^* \sqcup X\) to \(T^* \sqcup \bar{X}\) in one of three ways:

From \(S^*\) to a vertex \(v \in \bar{X}\) with \(M(v) > 0\), contributing \(M(v)\);
From a vertex \(v \in X\) with \(M(v) < 0\) to \(T^*\), contributing \(-M(v)\);
An original network edge \(e \in \delta^+(X)\) crossing from \(X\) to \(\bar{X}\), contributing its slack capacity \(u(e) - l(e)\).

Summing these three contributions gives: \[\kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X) = \sum_{v \in \bar{X} : M(v) > 0} M(v) + \sum_{v \in X : M(v) < 0} \big(-M(v)\big) + \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} \big(u(e) - l(e)\big).\] Subtracting \(\kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X)\) from \(\Sigma^+ = \sum_{v \in X : M(v) > 0} M(v) + \sum_{v \in \bar{X} : M(v) > 0} M(v)\) cancels the \(\bar{X}\) sum and combines the two \(X\) sums into \(\sum_{v \in X} M(v)\): \[\Sigma^+ - \kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X) = \sum_{v \in X} M(v) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} \big(u(e) - l(e)\big).\] Now substitute \(\sum_{v \in X} M(v) = \sum_{v \in X} \big(\text{in}_l(v) - \text{out}_l(v)\big) = \sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} l(e)\). The \(-\sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} l(e)\) terms cancel identically, revealing the Fundamental Duality Identity of Lower-Bound Flows: \[\boxed{\Sigma^+ - \kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X) = \sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} u(e) \qquad \forall X \subseteq V.}\] Therefore, \(\kappa_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^* \sqcup X) \ge \Sigma^+\) holds for all \(X \subseteq V\) if and only if \(\sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} l(e) \le \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} u(e)\) holds for all \(X \subseteq V\)! Calling \(Y = \bar{X} = V \setminus X\) reverses \(\delta^-(X) = \delta^+(Y)\) and \(\delta^+(X) = \delta^-(Y)\), giving the dual form \(\sum_{e \in \delta^-(Y)} u(e) \ge \sum_{e \in \delta^+(Y)} l(e)\) for all \(Y \subseteq V\). \(\blacksquare\)





3.2 Theorem 3.2 (Constructive Infeasibility Certificate from \(S_{\min}^*\))
Suppose Phase 1 fails with \(\text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}}(S^*, T^*) = F_1 < \Sigma^+\). Let \(S_{\min}^*\) be the set of vertices reachable from \(S^*\) in the final residual network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}^*}\) (found by a single forward BFS/DFS from \(S^*\), as in Chapter 2). Define: \[X^* \triangleq S_{\min}^* \setminus \{S^*\} \subseteq V, \qquad Y^* \triangleq V \setminus X^*.\]
Then:

Exact Certificate of Violation: The subset \(X^*\) violates Hoffman’s inflow-lower-bound inequality (and \(Y^*\) violates Hoffman’s outflow-lower-bound inequality) by strictly \(\Sigma^+ - F_1 > 0\): \[\sum_{e \in \delta^-(X^*)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X^*)} u(e) = \sum_{e \in \delta^+(Y^*)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(Y^*)} u(e) = \Sigma^+ - F_1 > 0.\]
Maximum-Violation Optimality: Among all \(2^{|V|}\) subsets \(X \subseteq V\), \(X^*\) maximizes the Hoffman violation \(\sum_{e \in \delta^-(X)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(X)} u(e)\).


Worked Numerical Trace: Extracting \(X^*\) When Phase 1 Fails
Suppose in our 4-vertex network \(V = \{s, a, b, t\}\) from Section 2.4, we raise the lower bound of \(e_1 = (s \to a)\) to \([l_1, u_1] = [4, 5]\), tighten \(e_3 = (a \to b)\) to \([1, 2]\), and tighten \(e_4 = (a \to t)\) to \([1, 1]\), keeping \(e_2 = (s \to b, [1, 4])\), \(e_5 = (b \to t, [2, 6])\), and \(e_{\text{fb}} = (t \to s, [0, \infty))\).

Pre-Injected Imbalances \(M(v)\):

\(M(s) = 0 - (4 + 1) = -5 \implies s \to T^*\) (cap \(5\)).
\(M(a) = 4 - (1 + 1) = +2 \implies S^* \to a\) (cap \(2\)).
\(M(b) = (1 + 1) - 2 = 0\).
\(M(t) = (1 + 2) - 0 = +3 \implies S^* \to t\) (cap \(3\)).
Total positive imbalance: \(\Sigma^+ = 2 + 3 = 5\).

Slack Capacities Leaving \(a\):

\(\tilde{c}(a \to b) = u_3 - l_3 = 2 - 1 = 1\), and \(\tilde{c}(a \to t) = u_4 - l_4 = 1 - 1 = 0\).

Phase 1 Execution (MaxFlow(S*, T*)):

All \(3\) units from \(S^* \to t\) reach \(T^*\) via \(t \xrightarrow{e_{\text{fb}}} s \to T^*\).
Only \(1\) unit from \(S^* \to a\) reaches \(T^*\) via \(a \xrightarrow{e_3} b \xrightarrow{e_5} t \xrightarrow{e_{\text{fb}}} s \to T^*\).
Total Phase 1 flow is \(F_1 = 4 < \Sigma^+ = 5\) (INFEASIBLE).

Extracting \(X^* = S_{\min}^* \setminus \{S^*\}\):

In the final residual network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}^*}\), the arc \(S^* \to a\) still has residual capacity \(2 - 1 = 1 > 0\), whereas all arcs leaving \(a\) (\(a \to b\) and \(a \to t\)) have residual capacity \(0\).
A forward BFS from \(S^*\) visits \(S_{\min}^* = \{S^*, a\}\), yielding the witness subset: \[X^* = S_{\min}^* \setminus \{S^*\} = \{a\}.\]
Checking Hoffman’s inequality on \(X^* = \{a\}\): mandatory inflow into \(\{a\}\) is \(l(s \to a) = 4\), whereas maximum possible outflow from \(\{a\}\) is \(u(a \to b) + u(a \to t) = 2 + 1 = 3\), giving an exact violation of \(4 - 3 = 1 = \Sigma^+ - F_1\)!

section: 4. Three Non-Graph Archetypes That Compile to Lower-Bound Flows
text:
4. Three Non-Graph Archetypes That Compile to Lower-Bound Flows
Following our Zero Magic Gadgets Mandate, we now derive the complete 4-step compilation for the three most important non-graph problem families that compile to lower-bound circulations.

4.1 Archetype A: Matrix & Contingency-Table Rounding (Baranyai's Rounding Lemma, POJ 2396, BZOJ 3698)

Step 1 (Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal): You are given an \(R \times C\) matrix where each cell \(X_{i,j}\) has box bounds \([L_{i,j}, U_{i,j}]\), each row \(i\) has row-sum bounds \([\underline{r}_i, \overline{r}_i]\), and each column \(j\) has column-sum bounds \([\underline{c}_j, \overline{c}_j]\). (In Real-Valued Matrix Rounding, you are given real numbers \(A_{i,j} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\) with row sums \(r_i = \sum_j A_{i,j}\) and column sums \(c_j = \sum_i A_{i,j}\), and must round every entry and margin to either \(\lfloor \cdot \rfloor\) or \(\lceil \cdot \rceil\) while preserving all row and column sums.)
Step 2 (Intermediate Algebraic Representation): The unknown integer matrix \(X_{i,j} \in \mathbb{Z}\) must satisfy: \[\underline{r}_i \le \sum_{j=1}^C X_{i,j} \le \overline{r}_i \quad (\forall i), \qquad \underline{c}_j \le \sum_{i=1}^R X_{i,j} \le \overline{c}_j \quad (\forall j), \qquad L_{i,j} \le X_{i,j} \le U_{i,j} \quad (\forall i, j).\] Introduce slack row-sum variables \(R_i \triangleq \sum_{j=1}^C X_{i,j}\) and column-sum variables \(C_j \triangleq \sum_{i=1}^R X_{i,j}\). Then every row \(i\) satisfies homogeneous conservation \(R_i - \sum_{j=1}^C X_{i,j} = 0\), and every column \(j\) satisfies \(\sum_{i=1}^R X_{i,j} - C_j = 0\)!
Step 3 (Mechanical Graph Compilation): By the Rank-2 Factorization Principle (Chapter 3.3), create source \(s\), sink \(t\), row vertices \(\text{Row}_1, \dots, \text{Row}_R\), and column vertices \(\text{Col}_1, \dots, \text{Col}_C\):

For each row \(i\), add directed edge \(s \to \text{Row}_i\) with bounds \([\underline{r}_i, \overline{r}_i]\) (carrying flow \(R_i\)).
For each cell \((i, j)\), add directed edge \(\text{Row}_i \to \text{Col}_j\) with bounds \([L_{i,j}, U_{i,j}]\) (carrying flow \(X_{i,j}\)).
For each column \(j\), add directed edge \(\text{Col}_j \to t\) with bounds \([\underline{c}_j, \overline{c}_j]\) (carrying flow \(C_j\)).
Add feedback arc \(t \to s\) with bounds \([\underline{\Sigma}, \overline{\Sigma}]\) (or \([0, \infty)\) if total matrix sum is unconstrained).



[!TIP] Theorem 4.1 (Baranyai’s Consistent Matrix Rounding Theorem): For any real matrix \(A \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^{R \times C}\) with row sums \(r_i = \sum_j A_{i,j}\), column sums \(c_j = \sum_i A_{i,j}\), and grand total \(S = \sum_{i,j} A_{i,j}\), setting \([l, u] = [\lfloor x \rfloor, \lceil x \rceil]\) on every row arc, column arc, cell arc, and feedback arc \(t \to s\) is always feasible!
Proof: The original real numbers \(f(s \to \text{Row}_i) = r_i\), \(f(\text{Row}_i \to \text{Col}_j) = A_{i,j}\), \(f(\text{Col}_j \to t) = c_j\), and \(f(t \to s) = S\) already form a valid real-valued circulation satisfying all integer box bounds \(\lfloor x \rfloor \le x \le \lceil x \rceil\). By the Integrality Theorem on the slack network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\), because a real-valued feasible circulation exists and all bounds \(\lfloor x \rfloor, \lceil x \rceil\) are integers, an integral circulation \(X_{i,j} \in \{\lfloor A_{i,j} \rfloor, \lceil A_{i,j} \rceil\}\) is guaranteed to exist!




4.2 Archetype B: Mixed-Graph Eulerian Circuit Orientation (POJ 1637) & FM-06 Parity Trap

Step 1 (Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal): A connected mixed graph \(G = (V, E_D \cup E_U)\) contains both fixed directed edges \(E_D\) and reversible undirected edges \(E_U\). We must orient every undirected edge \(e \in E_U\) so that the resulting fully directed graph has an Eulerian circuit (\(\text{in}(v) = \text{out}(v)\) for every \(v \in V\)).
Step 2 (Intermediate Algebraic Representation): Assign every undirected edge \(e \in E_U\) an arbitrary initial orientation \(u \to v\). Now let \(\text{in}_0(v)\) and \(\text{out}_0(v)\) denote the initial in-degree and out-degree of vertex \(v\) across all edges \(E_D \cup E_U\). For each undirected edge \(e = (u \to v) \in E_U\), introduce a binary decision variable \(x_e \in \{0, 1\}\), where \(x_e = 1\) means we reverse \(e\) to \((v \to u)\) and \(x_e = 0\) means we keep \((u \to v)\). How does setting \(x_e = 1\) change the net degree discrepancy \(\text{out}(v) - \text{in}(v)\)?

At the tail \(u\), reversing \(u \to v\) into \(v \to u\) decreases \(\text{out}(u)\) by \(1\) and increases \(\text{in}(u)\) by \(1\), reducing \(\text{out}(u) - \text{in}(u)\) by \(2\)!
At the head \(v\), it increases \(\text{out}(v) - \text{in}(v)\) by \(2\)! Therefore, achieving \(\text{out}(v) - \text{in}(v) = 0\) at every vertex \(v \in V\) is equivalent to: \[\big(\text{out}_0(v) - \text{in}_0(v)\big) - 2 \sum_{e \in \delta^+_U(v)} x_e + 2 \sum_{e \in \delta^-_U(v)} x_e = 0 \qquad \forall v \in V.\] Divide the entire equation by \(2\): \[\underbrace{\sum_{e \in \delta^+_U(v)} x_e - \sum_{e \in \delta^-_U(v)} x_e}_{\text{div}_x(v)} = \underbrace{\frac{\text{out}_0(v) - \text{in}_0(v)}{2}}_{D(v)} \qquad \forall v \in V.\]

Step 3 (Mechanical Graph Compilation):

Parity Pre-Check: If \(\text{out}_0(v) - \text{in}_0(v)\) is odd for any \(v \in V\), then \(D(v) \notin \mathbb{Z}\), so the equation has no solution—return impossible immediately!
Flow Network: Build a standard \([0, 1]\) flow network with source \(S^*\) and sink \(T^*\):

For each undirected edge \(e \in E_U\) (initially oriented \(u \to v\)), add directed arc \(u \to v\) with capacity \(1\) (representing \(x_e \in [0, 1]\)). Do not add fixed directed edges \(e \in E_D\) to the flow network!
If \(D(v) > 0\) (\(\text{out}_0(v) > \text{in}_0(v)\)), vertex \(v\) must emit \(D(v)\) units of reversal flow: add \(S^* \to v\) with capacity \(D(v)\).
If \(D(v) < 0\) (\(\text{in}_0(v) > \text{out}_0(v)\)), vertex \(v\) must absorb \(-D(v)\) units of reversal flow: add \(v \to T^*\) with capacity \(-D(v)\).

Existence Criterion: An Eulerian orientation exists if and only if \(\text{MaxFlow}(S^*, T^*) = \sum_{v : D(v) > 0} D(v)\).



[!WARNING] Broken-Gadget Counterexample FM-06 — Mixed Eulerian Parity Omission & Integer Division Truncation: In C++, writing int D = (out[v] - in[v]) / 2; without first checking (out[v] - in[v]) % 2 != 0 silently truncates odd discrepancies toward zero (e.g., 1 / 2 == 0 and -1 / 2 == 0)!
Counterexample: Consider \(V = \{1, 2\}\) connected by a single fixed directed edge \(1 \to 2\) (\(E_U = \emptyset\)). Here \(\text{out}_0(1) - \text{in}_0(1) = +1\) and \(\text{out}_0(2) - \text{in}_0(2) = -1\). If you omit the parity check, C++ integer division computes D[1] = 1 / 2 = 0 and D[2] = -1 / 2 = 0, builds an empty flow network with \(\Sigma^+ = 0\), and falsely reports that a single directed edge \(1 \to 2\) has an Eulerian circuit! Always verify (out[v] - in[v]) & 1 for every vertex before dividing by \(2\).




4.3 Archetype C: DAG Minimum Path / Fleet Cover with Mandatory Coverage (Luogu P4843 清理雪道)

Step 1 (Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal): Given a directed acyclic graph (or general directed network) \(G = (V, E)\), find the minimum number of paths (starting at any valid start vertices and ending at any valid end vertices) such that every required edge \(e \in E_{\text{req}}\) (or every required vertex \(v \in V_{\text{req}}\)) is traversed at least once.

Why Ch 01 Bipartite Path Cover Fails: In Chapter 1’s Minimum Path Cover on a DAG (|V| - MaxMatching), vertices could be visited at most once (\([0, 1]\)) and edges could not be reused. When paths are allowed to share vertices and edges freely (At Least Once, \([1, \infty)\)), either transitive closure + Dilworth (Ch 08) or Variant 4 (有源汇上下界最小流) is required—and when edges have finite upper capacities \([l(e), u(e)]\) or costs, Variant 4 is the only method that generalizes!

Step 2 & Step 3 (Algebraic & Graph Compilation): Let \(f(e) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\) count how many paths traverse edge \(e\).

Create a virtual source \(s\) (fleet depot) and virtual sink \(t\) (fleet terminal). For every vertex \(v\) where a path may start, add \(s \to v\) with \([0, \infty)\); for every vertex \(v\) where a path may terminate, add \(v \to t\) with \([0, \infty)\).
For every required edge \(e \in E_{\text{req}}\), set lower bound \(l(e) = 1\) and upper bound \(u(e) = \infty\). (If a vertex \(v\) must be visited at least \(k_v\) times, split \(v \mapsto v_{\text{in}} \xrightarrow{[k_v, \infty)} v_{\text{out}}\) as in Chapter 3.1.)
Solve Variant 4 (Minimum \(s\)-\(t\) Flow with Lower Bounds): add feedback arc \(t \to s\) with \([0, \infty)\), run Phase 1 MaxFlow(S*, T*) to get initial flow \(f_0 = \tilde{f}(t \to s)\), zero out both half-edges of \(t \to s\), and return \(F_{\min} = f_0 - \text{MaxFlow}_{\tilde{\mathcal{N}}_{\tilde{f}}}(t, s)\).

\(O((N+M)\sqrt{N})\)


Real matrix rounding to \(\{\lfloor A \rfloor, \lceil A \rceil\}\) (BZOJ 3698)
\(B_{i,j} \in [\lfloor A_{i,j} \rfloor, \lceil A_{i,j} \rceil]\), row/col sums preserved

Tier 1: Stepping Stone Problems

Problem #025 — [ZOJ 2314 / ASC 1] Reactor Cooling ([EN])

Judge URL: ZOJ 2314 / SGU 194
Constraints: \(N \le 200\) cooling nodes, \(M \le 20000\) directed pipes. Each pipe \(e_k = (u_k \to v_k)\) has mandatory minimum flow \(l_k \ge 0\) and maximum capacity \(u_k \ge l_k\) (\(0 \le l_k \le u_k \le 10^5\)). Determine whether a valid closed circulation exists (\(\text{div}_f(v) = 0\) at every node \(v = 1, \dots, N\)), and if so, print the exact flow \(f(e_k)\) on each pipe \(k = 1, \dots, M\).







NoteHint 1 — Why Standard Max-Flow Fails & How to Shift the Origin





There is no source \(s\) or sink \(t\) in the reactor—every node must have total inflow equal to total outflow, and \(f \equiv 0\) violates \(l_k > 0\). Substitute \(f(e_k) = l_k + \tilde{f}(e_k)\) where \(0 \le \tilde{f}(e_k) \le u_k - l_k\) into \(\sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} f(e) = \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} f(e)\) and isolate the known constants \(l_k\) on one side.









NoteHint 2 — Wiring the Nodal Imbalances to Super-Terminals





Define \(M(v) = \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} l(e)\). If \(M(v) > 0\), node \(v\) receives \(M(v)\) more baseline flow than it sends out, so the free slack flow \(\tilde{f}\) must carry \(M(v)\) units away from \(v\): wire \(S^* \to v\) with capacity \(M(v)\). If \(M(v) < 0\), wire \(v \to T^*\) with capacity \(-M(v)\). What must \(\text{MaxFlow}(S^*, T^*)\) equal for all nodes to balance?









TipFull 4-Step Compilation & Solution — ZOJ 2314






Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal
Every pipe has a two-sided box constraint \(l_k \le f(e_k) \le u_k\) and every vertex satisfies strict sourceless conservation \(\text{div}_f(v) = 0\). This is the canonical Variant 1 (无源汇上下界可行流) problem.


Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation
Write \(f(e_k) = l_k + \tilde{f}(e_k)\) with \(0 \le \tilde{f}(e_k) \le u_k - l_k\). Conservation at vertex \(v\) becomes: \[\sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} \tilde{f}(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} \tilde{f}(e) = \sum_{e \in \delta^-(v)} l(e) - \sum_{e \in \delta^+(v)} l(e) \triangleq M(v).\]


Step 3: Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Graph Compilation)

Create auxiliary network \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\) with vertices \(\{1, \dots, N\} \cup \{S^*, T^*\}\).
For each pipe \(k = 1, \dots, M\) from \(u_k\) to \(v_k\):

Add directed edge \(u_k \to v_k\) with capacity \(u_k - l_k\), recording the index rev_idx[k] of its reverse residual half-edge.
Update \(M(u_k) \gets M(u_k) - l_k\) and \(M(v_k) \gets M(v_k) + l_k\).

Accumulate \(\Sigma^+ = 0\). For each \(v \in \{1, \dots, N\}\):

If \(M(v) > 0\): add \(S^* \to v\) with capacity \(M(v)\), and add \(M(v)\) to \(\Sigma^+\).
If \(M(v) < 0\): add \(v \to T^*\) with capacity \(-M(v)\).

Run F1 = dinic(S*, T*). If \(F_1 < \Sigma^+\), output NO. Otherwise output YES, and for each pipe \(k\), reconstruct the physical flow via FM-05 guard: \[f(e_k) = l_k + \tilde{f}(e_k) = l_k + \text{cap}[\text{rev\_idx}[k]].\]



Step 4: Toy Trace & Failure-Mode Guard
On a 3-node cycle \(1 \xrightarrow{[2, 4]} 2 \xrightarrow{[1, 5]} 3 \xrightarrow{[3, 4]} 1\): - \(M(1) = 3 - 2 = +1 \implies S^* \to 1\) (cap \(1\)); \(M(2) = 2 - 1 = +1 \implies S^* \to 2\) (cap \(1\)); \(M(3) = 1 - 3 = -2 \implies 3 \to T^*\) (cap \(2\)); \(\Sigma^+ = 2\). - dinic(S*, T*) pushes \(1\) unit along \(S^* \to 1 \to 2 \to 3 \to T^*\) and \(1\) unit along \(S^* \to 2 \to 3 \to T^*\), giving \(\tilde{f} = (1, 2, 0)\) and physical flow \(f = l + \tilde{f} = (2+1, 1+2, 3+0) = (3, 3, 3)\). - Complexity: \(O(M\sqrt{N})\) or \(O(N^2 M)\) time, \(O(N + M)\) space.







Problem #026 — [POJ 2396] Budget ([EN])

Judge URL: POJ 2396
Constraints: Reconstruct a non-negative integer matrix \(X \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^{R \times C}\) (\(R \le 200, C \le 20\)) given exact row sums \(r_1, \dots, r_R\), exact column sums \(c_1, \dots, c_C\), and \(K\) inequality constraints of the form (p, q, op, v) where op \(\in \{\text{`<'}, \text{`='}, \text{`>'}\}\), \(p \in [0, R]\) (\(p = 0\) means all rows), and \(q \in [0, C]\) (\(q = 0\) means all columns). Output a valid matrix \(X\) or IMPOSSIBLE.







NoteHint 1 — Normalizing Wildcard Inequalities into Cell Box Bounds





Before building any graph, initialize every cell \((i, j)\) (\(1 \le i \le R, 1 \le j \le C\)) with box bounds \(L_{i,j} = 0, U_{i,j} = \infty\). How does each constraint (p, q, op, v) tighten \([L_{i,j}, U_{i,j}]\) for the affected cells?









NoteHint 2 — Rank-2 Factorization into Variant 2





Each cell \(X_{i,j}\) contributes to both row sum \(i\) and column sum \(j\). Model \(X_{i,j}\) as the flow on edge \(\text{Row}_i \to \text{Col}_j\) with bounds \([L_{i,j}, U_{i,j}]\). What are the lower and upper bounds on \(s \to \text{Row}_i\) and \(\text{Col}_j \to t\)? Don’t forget the feedback arc \(t \to s\)!









TipFull 4-Step Compilation & Solution — POJ 2396






Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal
We have a 2D table of integer variables \(X_{i,j}\) constrained by cell intervals \([L_{i,j}, U_{i,j}]\) and exact 1D marginal sums \(\sum_j X_{i,j} = r_i\), \(\sum_i X_{i,j} = c_j\). By Archetype A (Section 4.1), this compiles directly to Variant 2 (有源汇上下界可行流).


Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

Initialize \(L_{i,j} = 0, U_{i,j} = \infty\) for all \(1 \le i \le R, 1 \le j \le C\).
For each constraint (p, q, op, v), iterate over \(i \in (p = 0 ? [1..R] : \{p\})\) and \(j \in (q = 0 ? [1..C] : \{q\})\):

If op == '>': \(L_{i,j} \gets \max(L_{i,j}, v + 1)\).
If op == '<': \(U_{i,j} \gets \min(U_{i,j}, v - 1)\).
If op == '=': \(L_{i,j} \gets \max(L_{i,j}, v)\) and \(U_{i,j} \gets \min(U_{i,j}, v)\).

Pre-check: if \(\sum_{i=1}^R r_i \neq \sum_{j=1}^C c_j\) or if \(L_{i,j} > U_{i,j}\) for any \((i, j)\), return IMPOSSIBLE immediately.

Compile all bounded edges into \(\tilde{\mathcal{N}}\) with super-terminals \((S^*, T^*)\) and run dinic(S*, T*). If \(F_1 = \Sigma^+\), reconstruct \(X_{i,j} = L_{i,j} + \tilde{f}(\text{Row}_i \to \text{Col}_j)\); otherwise print IMPOSSIBLE.

// Lock feedback arc before Phase 2!

NoteHint 2 — Compiling Half-Discrepancies into a Unit Network

TipFull 4-Step Compilation & Solution — POJ 1637






Step 1: Non-Graph Diagnostic Signal
A connected directed graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if \(\text{out}(v) = \text{in}(v)\) for every \(v \in V\). Choosing orientations for undirected edges while keeping directed edges fixed is Archetype B (Mixed-Graph Eulerian Circuit Orientation, Section 4.2).


Step 2: Intermediate Algebraic Representation

By Section 4.2: \[\sum_{e \in \delta^+_U(v)} x_e - \sum_{e \in \delta^-_U(v)} x_e = \frac{\text{out}_0(v) - \text{in}_0(v)}{2} \triangleq D(v) \qquad \forall v \in V.\]

For each vertex \(v\): let \(D(v) = (\text{out}_0(v) - \text{in}_0(v)) / 2\). If \(D(v) > 0\), add \(S^* \to v\) with capacity \(D(v)\) and add \(D(v)\) to \(\Sigma^+\); if \(D(v) < 0\), add \(v \to T^*\) with capacity \(-D(v)\).
