title: Chapter 04: The Labeled Symbolic Method: Exponential Generating Functions (EGFs), Boxed Products & Prüfer Sequences
text:
4.5 The 8-Problem 4-Tier Practice Ladder
Every problem below is drawn from the canonical textbook curriculum for Chapter 04 and is completely self-contained. Work through the Diagnostic Signal and Progressive Hints before opening the complete derivation.


Stepping Stone 1 (#002) — AtCoder fps_24_e: Sequence 2 (Bounded Multiset Permutations)

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_e (Sequence 2)
Prerequisite Tags: Labeled EGF Product (\(\mathcal{A} \star \mathcal{B}\)), Bounded Exponential Factors \(\sum_{j=0}^m \frac{x^j}{j!}\), Divide-and-Conquer / DP Convolution.


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Find the number, modulo \(998244353\), of integer sequences \(A = (A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N)\) of length \(N\) satisfying both of the following conditions:

\(1 \le A_i \le M\) for all \(1 \le i \le N\).
For every integer \(m \in \{1, 2, \dots, M\}\), the value \(m\) appears at most \(m\) times in the sequence \(A\).


Constraints: \(1 \le N, M \le 500\) (or up to \(N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\) in the large-scale D&C NTT regime), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \min(M, N)^2)\) or \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time, \(O(N)\) space.
Sample Trace (\(N = 3, M = 2\)): Valid sequences over \(\{1, 2\}\) of length \(3\) where \(1\) appears \(\le 1\) time and \(2\) appears \(\le 2\) times must use one \(1\) and two \(2\)’s: \((1,2,2), (2,1,2), (2,2,1)\), giving \(3! [x^3] (1 + x)\bigl(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\bigr) = 3\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

In the sequence \(A = (A_1, \dots, A_N)\), the \(N\) positions \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) are distinguishable. If value \(m\) is chosen to appear \(c_m\) times (\(0 \le c_m \le m\)) with \(c_1 + c_2 + \dots + c_M = N\), how many sequences \(A\) have this exact frequency profile \((c_1, \dots, c_M)\)? The multinomial coefficient \(\binom{N}{c_1, c_2, \dots, c_M} = \frac{N!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_M!}\)! What generating function family automatically produces \(\frac{N!}{c_1! \cdots c_M!}\) when multiplied?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Because the multinomial weight is \(\frac{N!}{c_1! \cdots c_M!}\), each value \(m \in \{1, 2, \dots, M\}\) contributes an independent truncated exponential generating function: \[\widehat{E}_m(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{m} \frac{x^j}{j!}\] The total number of valid sequences of length \(N\) is then \(N! [x^N] \prod_{m=1}^{M} \widehat{E}_m(x)\).



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Truncate all polynomial products modulo \(x^{N+1}\).

For \(N, M \le 500\): Maintain the coefficient array of \(\prod_{m=1}^k \widehat{E}_m(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) and multiply by \(\widehat{E}_m(x)\) in \(O(N \cdot \min(m, N))\) time, taking \(O(M N^2)\) total operations (\(\le 1.25 \times 10^8\) ops, or \(O(M N \log N)\) with NTT).
If \(M\) and \(N\) are up to \(10^5\): Notice that \(\widehat{E}_m(x) \equiv e^x \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) for all \(m \ge N\), and for the remaining \(m < N\) you can either multiply the polynomials or group identical factors. Finally, multiply \([x^N]\) by \(N! \bmod 998244353\).








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Combinatorial-to-EGF Translation
A sequence \(A = (A_1, \dots, A_N) \in \{1, \dots, M\}^N\) is uniquely determined by partitioning the set of \(N\) position indices \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) into \(M\) labeled subsets \((U_1, U_2, \dots, U_M)\), where \(U_m = \{i \in [N] \mid A_i = m\}\) is the set of positions holding value \(m\).
Condition 2 requires \(\lvert U_m \rvert = c_m \in \{0, 1, \dots, m\}\) for each \(m = 1, \dots, M\). For a fixed tuple of sizes \((c_1, \dots, c_M)\) summing to \(N\), the number of ways to partition \([N]\) into \((U_1, \dots, U_M)\) is \(\frac{N!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_M!}\). Summing over all valid tuples \((c_1, \dots, c_M)\): \[\begin{aligned}
\text{Ans} &= \sum_{\substack{c_1 + \dots + c_M = N \\ 0 \le c_m \le m}} \frac{N!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_M!} \\
&= N! [x^N] \prod_{m=1}^{M} \left( \sum_{c_m=0}^{m} \frac{x^{c_m}}{c_m!} \right)
\end{aligned}\]


2. Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 3, M = 2\))
For \(N = 3, M = 2\):

\(\widehat{E}_1(x) = 1 + x\)
\(\widehat{E}_2(x) = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\) Multiplying \(\widehat{E}_1(x) \widehat{E}_2(x) = (1 + x)\left(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\right) = 1 + 2x + \frac{3}{2}x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x^3\). Extracting \(3! [x^3] = 6 \times \frac{1}{2} = 3\). Indeed, a sequence of length \(3\) over \(\{1, 2\}\) with at most one \(1\) and at most two \(2\)’s must have \(c_1 = 1\) and \(c_2 = 2\), giving the \(\binom{3}{1, 2} = 3\) permutations of \((1, 2, 2)\).



3. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(N, M \ge 1\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\) so \(0!, 1!, \dots, N! \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(N! [x^N] \prod_{m=1}^M \left(\sum_{j=0}^m \frac{x^j}{j!}\right) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \min(M, N)^2)\) time via bounded-degree polynomial multiplication (or \(O(\min(M, N) N \log N)\) via NTT) and \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: After processing symbol \(m \in \{1, \dots, K\}\) (with all \(M - K\) unconstrained symbols \(m \ge N\) absorbed into \(e^{(M-K)x} \bmod x^{N+1}\)), \(k! [x^k] P(x)\) equals the number of valid sequences of length \(k \le N\) over \(\{1, \dots, m\} \cup \{K+1, \dots, M\}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Total Capacity Shortage (\(\frac{M(M+1)}{2} < N\)): When \(M(M+1)/2 < N\), \(\deg \prod_{m=1}^M \widehat{E}_m(x) < N\), so \([x^N] P(x) = 0\).
Large \(M \ge N\): Any factor with \(m \ge N\) agrees with \(e^x\) modulo \(x^{N+1}\); grouping all \(M - K\) such factors into \(e^{(M-K)x}\) avoids \(O(M)\) redundant degree-\(N\) multiplications.

Algorithm Steps:

Precompute factorials \(j!\) and inverse factorials \((j!)^{-1} \bmod p\) for \(0 \le j \le N\) in \(O(N)\) time.
Set \(K = \min(M, N - 1)\). Since \(\widehat{E}_m(x) \equiv e^x \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) for all \(m \ge N\), combine all \(M - K\) unconstrained symbols into a single initial polynomial: \[P(x) \equiv e^{(M - K)x} \equiv \sum_{j=0}^{N} \frac{(M - K)^j}{j!} x^j \pmod{x^{N+1}}\]
For \(m = 1, 2, \dots, K\), update \(P(x) \gets P(x) \cdot \left(\sum_{j=0}^m \frac{x^j}{j!}\right) \pmod{x^{N+1}}\).
Return \(N! [x^N] P(x) \bmod p\).










Stepping Stone 2 (#007) — AtCoder fps_24_m: Value of Permutation (Cycle-Weight EGF Decomposition)

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_m (Value of Permutation / Cycle Decomposition)
Prerequisite Tags: Permutation Cycle Decomposition \(\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{Z}))\), Weighted Cycle EGF \(\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\), Catalytic Variable Differentiation.


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given an integer \(N\) and a cycle-length weight sequence \((w_1, w_2, \dots, w_N)\), every permutation \(\pi \in S_N\) of \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) decomposes uniquely into a set of disjoint directed cycles \(\{C_1, C_2, \dots, C_r\}\). Find, modulo \(998244353\), the sum over all \(N!\) permutations \(\pi \in S_N\) of the multiplicative cycle weight: \[V(\pi) = \prod_{j=1}^{r} w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\]

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(0 \le w_k < 998244353\), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space (and \(O(N)\) time for the companion additive cycle-weight variant derived in the solution).
Sample Trace (\(N = 3\)): The \(6\) permutations in \(S_3\) consist of \(1\) identity (three \(1\)-cycles, weight \(w_1^3\)), \(3\) transpositions (one \(1\)-cycle and one \(2\)-cycle, weight \(3 w_1 w_2\)), and \(2\) three-cycles (weight \(2 w_3\)), totaling \(w_1^3 + 3 w_1 w_2 + 2 w_3 = 3! [x^3] \exp\bigl(w_1 x + \frac{w_2}{2}x^2 + \frac{w_3}{3}x^3\bigr)\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Every permutation \(\pi \in S_N\) is uniquely an unordered \(\operatorname{SET}\) of directed cycles (\(\operatorname{CYC}\)). On a label subset of size \(k\), how many distinct directed cycles exist? There are \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles! When each cycle of length \(k\) carries weight \(w_k\), what is the EGF of a single weighted directed cycle?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Because there are \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles on \(k\) labeled elements, a single cycle of length \(k\) weighted by \(w_k\) has EGF term: \[w_k (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \frac{w_k}{k} x^k \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{N} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\]

For the multiplicative weight \(\prod_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\), the \(\operatorname{SET}\) construction multiplies the weights of the constituent cycles, so the EGF is \(\exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr)\).
What if a companion problem asks for the additive weight \(\sum_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\)? Then a permutation with one distinguished weighted cycle consists of one chosen cycle from \(\widehat{W}(x)\) paired with an arbitrary permutation on the remaining elements (counted by \(\exp(\ln\frac{1}{1-x}) = \frac{1}{1 - x}\))!




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Multiplicative: Call poly_exp on \(\widehat{W}(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time and return \(N! [x^N] \exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr) \bmod 998244353\).
Additive Companion: The EGF is \(\widehat{W}(x) \cdot \frac{1}{1 - x}\), so extracting \(N! [x^N] \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 - x}\) gives \(N! \sum_{k=1}^N \frac{w_k}{k}\) in \(O(N)\) linear time!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Weighted Cycle EGF & Bivariate Catalytic Generating Function
Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be the class of directed cycles. Since \(k\) labeled elements form \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles, the unweighted cycle EGF is \(\widehat{C}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^\infty (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{x^k}{k} = \ln\frac{1}{1 - x}\), and the weighted cycle EGF is: \[\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} w_k (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\]

Multiplicative Cycle Weight \(V_{\text{mul}}(\pi) = \prod_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\): Under \(\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\), the weight of a set of cycles \(\{C_1, \dots, C_r\}\) is the product of the individual cycle weights. By the Exponential Formula: \[\sum_{\pi \in S_N} \prod_{j=1}^{r} w_{\lvert C_j \rvert} = N! [x^N] \exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr) = N! [x^N] \exp\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{N} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\right)\]
Companion Variant — Additive Cycle Weight \(V_{\text{add}}(\pi) = \sum_{j=1}^r w_{\lvert C_j \rvert}\): Introduce a catalytic variable \(y\) where a cycle of length \(k\) carries weight \(e^{y w_k}\) (or \(1 + (y - 1)w_k\)). The bivariate EGF over all permutations is: \[\widehat{F}(x, y) = \exp\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \bigl(1 + (y - 1) w_k\bigr) \frac{x^k}{k}\right) = \exp\Bigl(\ln\frac{1}{1 - x} + (y - 1)\widehat{W}(x)\Bigr) = \frac{\exp\bigl((y - 1)\widehat{W}(x)\bigr)}{1 - x}\] Differentiating with respect to \(y\) and setting \(y = 1\) isolates the sum of cycle weights across all cycles of \(\pi\): \[\left.\frac{\partial \widehat{F}(x, y)}{\partial y}\right|_{y=1} = \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 - x} = \left(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{w_k}{k} x^k\right) \left(\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} x^m\right)\] Extracting \(N! [x^N]\) yields the exact \(O(N)\) closed form: \[\sum_{\pi \in S_N} \sum_{j=1}^{r} w_{\lvert C_j \rvert} = N! [x^N] \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 - x} = N! \sum_{k=1}^{N} \frac{w_k}{k}\]



2. Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 3\))
The \(3! = 6\) permutations in \(S_3\) decompose into cycles as follows:

\(1\) identity permutation \((1)(2)(3)\): three \(1\)-cycles (multiplicative weight \(w_1^3\), additive weight \(3 w_1\)).
\(3\) transpositions \((12)(3), (13)(2), (23)(1)\): one \(1\)-cycle and one \(2\)-cycle each (multiplicative weight \(3 w_1 w_2\), additive weight \(3(w_1 + w_2)\)).
\(2\) three-cycles \((123), (132)\): one \(3\)-cycle each (multiplicative weight \(2 w_3\), additive weight \(2 w_3\)). Total multiplicative weight: \(w_1^3 + 3 w_1 w_2 + 2 w_3 = 3! [x^3] \exp\left(w_1 x + \frac{w_2}{2}x^2 + \frac{w_3}{3}x^3\right)\). Total additive weight: \(6 w_1 + 3 w_2 + 2 w_3 = 3! \left(\frac{w_1}{1} + \frac{w_2}{2} + \frac{w_3}{3}\right)\). Both match our formulas identically!



3. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \ge 1\), cycle weights \(w_1, \dots, w_N \in \mathbb{F}_p\); prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\) so \(1, 2, \dots, N \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) and \([x^0]\widehat{W}(x) = 0\).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(\sum_{\pi \in S_N} V_{\text{mul}}(\pi) \bmod p\) (and \(\sum_{\pi \in S_N} V_{\text{add}}(\pi) \bmod p\) for the additive companion).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time for multiplicative cycle weights (\(O(N)\) time for additive weights) and \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: Because \(\mathcal{P} = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C})\), for every \(0 \le n \le N\), \(n! [x^n] \exp(\widehat{W}(x))\) equals \(\sum_{\pi \in S_n} \prod_{C \in \pi} w_{\lvert C \rvert}\) and \(n! [x^n] \frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1-x}\) equals \(\sum_{\pi \in S_n} \sum_{C \in \pi} w_{\lvert C \rvert}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Missing \(1/k\) Cycle Symmetry Factor: A directed cycle on \(k\) labeled vertices has \((k-1)!\) orientations, so its EGF coefficient is \(\frac{w_k (k-1)!}{k!} = \frac{w_k}{k}\), not \(\frac{w_k}{k!}\).
Zero Constant Term Requirement for \(\exp\): \(\widehat{W}(0) = 0\) must hold before invoking poly_exp.

Algorithm Steps:

Precompute modular inverses \(k^{-1} \bmod p\) for \(1 \le k \le N\) and \(N! \bmod p\) in \(O(N)\) time.
Form \(\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N (w_k \cdot k^{-1} \bmod p) x^k\).
Multiplicative Output: Compute \(E(x) \equiv \exp\bigl(\widehat{W}(x)\bigr) \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) via poly_exp in \(O(N \log N)\) time and output \(N! [x^N] E(x) \bmod p\).
Additive Companion Output: Compute \(N! \left(\sum_{k=1}^N w_k k^{-1}\right) \bmod p\) in \(O(N)\) time.










Intermediate 1 (#161) — Luogu P4841: [集训队作业2013] 城市规划 (Urban Planning)

Source: Luogu P4841 — [集训队作业2013] 城市规划
Prerequisite Tags: Connected Labeled Graphs \(\widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x)\), Boxed Product ODE \(\widehat{G}'(x) = \widehat{C}'(x)\widehat{G}(x)\), Non-Standard NTT Prime \(p = 1004535809\).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
A country consists of \(n\) labeled cities \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\). Between any pair of distinct cities, an undirected road may or may not be built. Count the number of road networks (simple undirected graphs on \(n\) labeled vertices) such that all \(n\) cities form a single connected component, modulo \(1004535809\).

Constraints: \(1 \le n \le 1.3 \times 10^5\), prime modulus \(p = 1004535809 = 479 \times 2^{21} + 1\) (primitive root \(g = 3\)), time limit \(1.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) space.
Sample Trace (\(n = 3\)): Of the \(2^{\binom{3}{2}} = 8\) simple labeled graphs on \(\{1, 2, 3\}\), the \(4\) connected graphs are the \(3\) spanning paths (\(3\) labeled trees) plus \(1\) triangle \(K_3\), matching \(3! [x^3] \ln\bigl(1 + x + x^2 + \frac{4}{3}x^3\bigr) = 4\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Notice that the modulus \(p = 1004535809 = 479 \times 2^{21} + 1\) is an NTT-friendly prime with \(2^{21} > 2.6 \times 10^5\) and primitive root \(g = 3\). We want to extract \(c_n = n! [x^n] \widehat{C}(x)\) where \(\widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr)\) and \(g_k = 2^{\binom{k}{2}}\).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Compare the two equivalent algebraic formulations for \(\widehat{C}(x)\):

Direct Logarithm: \(\widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x) = \int_0^x \widehat{G}'(t)\widehat{G}(t)^{-1}\,dt \pmod{x^{n+1}}\).
Boxed Product / Minimum-Label Pivot: Isolate the connected component of size \(k\) containing city \(1\): \[g_m = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \binom{m-1}{k-1} c_k g_{m-k} \iff \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \left(\frac{c_k}{(k-1)!}\right) \left(\frac{g_{m-k}}{(m-k)!}\right)\] Notice that \(\sum_{m \ge 1} \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} x^{m-1} = \widehat{G}'(x)\) and \(\sum_{k \ge 1} \frac{c_k}{(k-1)!} x^{k-1} = \widehat{C}'(x)\), so solving \(\widehat{C}'(x) = \widehat{G}'(x)\widehat{G}(x)^{-1} \pmod{x^n}\) is the exact same polynomial inversion + multiplication!




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

Watch out for integer overflow when computing \(\binom{k}{2} = \frac{k(k-1)}{2}\) for \(k = 1.3 \times 10^5\): \(\binom{k}{2} \approx 8.45 \times 10^9 > 2^{31}-1\). By Fermat’s Little Theorem, \(2^{\binom{k}{2}} \equiv 2^{\binom{k}{2} \bmod (p - 1)} \pmod p\)—reduce the exponent modulo \(p - 1 = 1004535808\) (not modulo \(p\)!).







NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Derivation via the Boxed Product & EGF Logarithm
Let \(g_k = 2^{\binom{k}{2}}\) be the total number of simple undirected graphs on \(k\) labeled cities, and let \(c_k\) be the number of connected simple undirected graphs on \(k\) labeled cities.
In any graph on \(m \ge 1\) labeled cities, consider the connected component containing city \(1\). If this component has size \(k \in \{1, 2, \dots, m\}\):

There are \(\binom{m-1}{k-1}\) ways to choose the remaining \(k - 1\) cities in city \(1\)’s connected component from \(\{2, 3, \dots, m\}\).
There are \(c_k\) ways to form a connected graph on those \(k\) cities.
There are \(g_{m-k}\) ways to form an arbitrary simple graph on the remaining \(m - k\) cities (with no edges between the two parts).

Summing over \(k = 1, \dots, m\) yields the Boxed Product identity: \[g_m = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \binom{m-1}{k-1} c_k g_{m-k} \quad (m \ge 1)\] Dividing both sides by \((m - 1)!\): \[\frac{g_m}{(m - 1)!} = \sum_{k=1}^{m} \left(\frac{c_k}{(k - 1)!}\right) \left(\frac{g_{m-k}}{(m - k)!}\right)\] Define the formal power series: \[\widehat{G}(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \frac{g_j}{j!} x^j, \qquad \widehat{G}'(x) = \sum_{m=1}^{\infty} \frac{g_m}{(m - 1)!} x^{m-1}, \qquad \widehat{C}'(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{c_k}{(k - 1)!} x^{k-1}\] Then the recurrence is equivalent to \(\widehat{G}'(x) = \widehat{C}'(x) \widehat{G}(x)\) in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]\). Since \([x^0]\widehat{G}(x) = g_0 = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\), \(\widehat{G}(x)\) is invertible in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]\), and: \[\widehat{C}'(x) \equiv \widehat{G}'(x) \widehat{G}(x)^{-1} \pmod{x^n}\] Extracting \([x^{n-1}]\widehat{C}'(x) = \frac{c_n}{(n - 1)!}\) and multiplying by \((n - 1)!\) directly yields \(c_n\) without even needing the final integration step!


2. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(1 \le n \le 1.3 \times 10^5\), prime modulus \(p = 1004535809 = 479 \times 2^{21} + 1 > n\) with primitive root \(g = 3\), and \([x^0]\widehat{G}(x) = 1\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(c_n = n! [x^n] \ln \widehat{G}(x) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(n \log n)\) time and \(O(n)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At each Newton doubling step \(L = 2^s\) of poly_inv, \(A_L(x) \cdot \widehat{G}(x) \equiv 1 \pmod{x^L}\), so \(\widehat{C}'(x) \equiv \widehat{G}'(x) A_n(x) \pmod{x^n}\) satisfies \((m-1)! [x^{m-1}] \widehat{C}'(x) \equiv c_m \pmod p\) for all \(1 \le m \le n\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Exponent Overflow in \(\binom{k}{2}\): For \(k = 1.3 \times 10^5\), \(\binom{k}{2} > 2^{31}-1\) overflows 32-bit signed integers; compute 1LL * k * (k - 1) / 2 % (p - 1) before modular exponentiation (reducing modulo \(p - 1\), not \(p\)).
Non-Standard NTT Prime: Must configure NTT with \(p = 1004535809\) (not \(998244353\)), primitive root \(g = 3\).

Algorithm Steps:

Configure NTT with prime \(p = 1004535809\) and primitive root \(g = 3\).
Precompute factorials, inverse factorials, and \(g_k = 2^{\binom{k}{2} \bmod (p - 1)} \bmod p\) for \(0 \le k \le n\).
Construct polynomial \(A(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \frac{g_j}{j!} x^j \bmod x^n\) and \(B(x) = \sum_{m=1}^{n} \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} x^{m-1} \bmod x^n\).
Compute \(A^{-1}(x) \equiv A(x)^{-1} \pmod{x^n}\) via Newton polynomial inversion in \(O(n \log n)\) time.
Output \(c_n = (n - 1)! [x^{n-1}]\bigl(B(x) A^{-1}(x)\bigr) = (n - 1)! \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{g_k}{(k-1)!} [x^{n-k}]A^{-1}(x) \bmod p\).








TipCross-Chapter Landmark Thread (“Revisited” Index #3)



We will revisit Luogu P4841 in Chapter 07 / Chapter 13 (where the quadratic exponent \(2^{\binom{k}{2}}\) is used inside Bluestein’s Chirp-\(Z\) Transform to evaluate graphical convolutions directly) and in Chapter 09 (where the recurrence \(\frac{c_m}{(m-1)!} = \frac{g_m}{(m-1)!} - \sum_{k=1}^{m-1} \frac{c_k}{(k-1)!} \frac{g_{m-k}}{(m-k)!}\) is solved online via CDQ Divide-and-Conquer NTT).










Intermediate 2 (#008) — AtCoder fps_24_n: Tree (Prüfer Sequence Degree-Distribution EGF)

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_n (Tree) & Luogu P2290 — [HNOI2004] 树的计数
Prerequisite Tags: Prüfer Sequence Bijection, Degree-Weighted EGF Product \((N-2)!\,[x^{N-2}]\prod_{i=1}^N \widehat{E}_i(x)\), Canonical Failure Mode #16 (\(N = 1\) Boundary Guard).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
You are given \(N\) labeled vertices \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\), where each vertex \(i \in \{1, \dots, N\}\) has a prescribed degree weight polynomial \(w_i(d)\) supported on \(1 \le d \le D_i\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^N D_i \le 2.5 \times 10^5\). Compute the total weight \(\sum_T \prod_{i=1}^N w_i(\deg_T(i))\) over all labeled trees \(T\) on \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(\sum_{i=1}^N D_i \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space (reducing to \(O(N)\) time in the Luogu P2290 special case where each vertex \(i\) has a single exact prescribed degree \(d_i\)).
Sample Trace (\(N = 4, D = (2, 2, 3, 1)\)): With \(w_i(d) = [1 \le d \le D_i]\), multiplying \(\widehat{E}_1(x) = 1+x\), \(\widehat{E}_2(x) = 1+x\), \(\widehat{E}_3(x) = 1+x+\frac{x^2}{2}\), \(\widehat{E}_4(x) = 1\) yields \((4-2)! [x^2] \prod_{i=1}^4 \widehat{E}_i(x) = 2 \times \frac{7}{2} = 7\) valid trees.



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Whenever an unrooted labeled tree problem constrains or weights the individual vertex degrees \(\deg_T(1), \dots, \deg_T(N)\), apply Prüfer’s Bijection: for \(N \ge 2\), a labeled tree \(T\) on \(\{1, \dots, N\}\) corresponds bijectively to a Prüfer word \(P \in \{1, \dots, N\}^{N-2}\) of length \(N - 2\) in which each vertex \(i\) appears \(c_i = \deg_T(i) - 1\) times! Don’t forget Canonical Failure Mode #16: what happens when \(N = 1\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

For \(N \ge 2\), a fixed multiplicity tuple \((c_1, \dots, c_N) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^N\) with \(c_1 + \dots + c_N = N - 2\) corresponds to \(\frac{(N - 2)!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_N!}\) Prüfer words, and vertex \(i\) has degree \(d_i = c_i + 1\). Therefore, associating the truncated EGF factor \[\widehat{E}_i(x) = \sum_{c_i = 0}^{D_i - 1} w_i(c_i + 1) \frac{x^{c_i}}{c_i!} = \sum_{d=1}^{D_i} w_i(d) \frac{x^{d-1}}{(d - 1)!}\] to each vertex \(i \in \{1, \dots, N\}\) reduces the tree sum to: \[\text{Ans} = (N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \prod_{i=1}^{N} \widehat{E}_i(x)\]



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Guard \(N = 1\) first: At \(N = 1\), the unique tree on \(\{1\}\) has \(0\) edges, so \(\deg_T(1) = 0\). Output \(w_1(0) \bmod 998244353\) immediately.
Heterogeneous Degree Polynomials (fps_24_n): Multiply \(\widehat{E}_1(x), \dots, \widehat{E}_N(x)\) modulo \(x^{N-1}\) via a balanced Divide-and-Conquer product tree in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time and multiply \([x^{N-2}]\) by \((N - 2)! \bmod 998244353\).
Exact Prescribed Degrees (Luogu P2290 Special Case): If each vertex \(i\) must have exact degree \(d_i\), then \(\widehat{E}_i(x) = \frac{x^{d_i - 1}}{(d_i - 1)!}\) is a monomial! Verify \(d_i \ge 1\) for all \(i\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^N (d_i - 1) = N - 2\), then return \(\frac{(N - 2)!}{\prod_{i=1}^N (d_i - 1)!}\) in \(O(N)\) time.








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Labeled Tree Degree Distribution via Prüfer EGF
By Prüfer’s Bijection (§4.4), for \(N \ge 2\), the map sending a tree \(T\) on \(\{1, \dots, N\}\) to its Prüfer sequence \(P \in \{1, \dots, N\}^{N-2}\) is a bijection under which the multiplicity of label \(i\) in \(P\) is \(c_i = \deg_T(i) - 1 \ge 0\). Consequently: \[\begin{aligned}
\sum_{T \text{ on } [N]} \prod_{i=1}^{N} w_i\bigl(\deg_T(i)\bigr) &= \sum_{c_1 + \dots + c_N = N - 2} \frac{(N - 2)!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_N!} \prod_{i=1}^{N} w_i(c_i + 1) \\
&= (N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \prod_{i=1}^{N} \left(\sum_{c=0}^{D_i - 1} w_i(c + 1) \frac{x^c}{c!}\right)
\end{aligned}\]

General Case — Heterogeneous Degree Bounds (fps_24_n): When vertex \(i\) has degree bound \(1 \le \deg_T(i) \le D_i\), \(\widehat{E}_i(x) = \sum_{c=0}^{D_i - 1} \frac{x^c}{c!}\) has degree \(D_i - 1\). Since \(\sum_{i=1}^N \deg \widehat{E}_i \le \sum_{i=1}^N D_i = O(N)\), a recursive binary product tree multiplies all \(N\) polynomials in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time.
Special Case — Exact Prescribed Degrees (Luogu P2290): When \(w_i(d) = [d = d_i]\), each factor is the monomial \(\widehat{E}_i(x) = \frac{x^{d_i - 1}}{(d_i - 1)!}\) (provided \(d_i \ge 1\)). Their product is a single monomial \(\frac{x^{\sum (d_i - 1)}}{\prod (d_i - 1)!}\), so a valid tree exists for \(N \ge 2\) if and only if \(d_i \ge 1\) for all \(1 \le i \le N\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^N d_i = 2N - 2\), in which case the count is \(\frac{(N - 2)!}{(d_1 - 1)! \cdots (d_N - 1)!}\).



2. Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 4\), Upper Bounds \(D = (2, 2, 3, 1)\))
Suppose \(N = 4\) and vertex degrees must satisfy \(1 \le \deg_T(i) \le D_i\) with \((D_1, D_2, D_3, D_4) = (2, 2, 3, 1)\):

\(\widehat{E}_1(x) = 1 + x\), \(\widehat{E}_2(x) = 1 + x\), \(\widehat{E}_3(x) = 1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\), \(\widehat{E}_4(x) = 1\).
Product modulo \(x^3\): \((1 + x)^2 \left(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\right) = (1 + 2x + x^2)\left(1 + x + \frac{x^2}{2}\right) \equiv 1 + 3x + \frac{7}{2}x^2 \pmod{x^3}\).
Extracting \((4 - 2)! [x^2] = 2! \times \frac{7}{2} = 7\) valid trees on \(4\) vertices (specifically, the \(1\) star centered at vertex \(3\), plus the \(6\) paths in which vertex \(4\) is a leaf).



3. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \ge 1\), degree weight polynomials \(\widehat{E}_i(x)\) with \(\sum_{i=1}^N D_i \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\) so \((N - 2)!\) and \(c!\) are units in \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(\sum_{T \text{ on } [N]} \prod_{i=1}^N w_i(\deg_T(i)) \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time for heterogeneous degree polynomials (\(O(N)\) time for exact prescribed degrees) and \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: At each node \([L, R]\) of daq_prod(L, R), the returned polynomial \(P_{L, R}(x) \equiv \prod_{i=L}^R \widehat{E}_i(x) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) satisfies \(k! [x^k] P_{L, R}(x) = \sum_{c_L + \dots + c_R = k} \frac{k!}{c_L! \cdots c_R!} \prod_{i=L}^R w_i(c_i + 1)\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Failure Mode #16 (\(N = 1\) Boundary Trap): At \(N = 1\), \(N - 2 = -1\) and the unique \(1\)-vertex tree has \(\deg_T(1) = 0\); must guard \(N = 1\) first and return \(w_1(0) \bmod p\).
Degree-\(0\) Vertex in \(N \ge 2\): In any tree on \(N \ge 2\) vertices, \(\deg_T(i) \ge 1\) for all \(i\); if any vertex has \(D_i = 0\) (or \(d_i = 0\) in Luogu P2290), the answer is \(0\).

Algorithm Steps:

Failure Mode #16 Guard (\(N = 1\)): If \(N = 1\), return \(w_1(0) \bmod p\) immediately (for Luogu P2290, return \(1\) if \(d_1 = 0\) and \(0\) otherwise).
Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to \(N\) in \(O(N)\) time.
Construct \(\widehat{E}_i(x) = \sum_{c=0}^{\min(D_i - 1, N - 2)} w_i(c + 1) \frac{x^c}{c!}\) for \(1 \le i \le N\).
Multiply \(\prod_{i=1}^N \widehat{E}_i(x) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) via a recursive binary product tree daq_prod(1, N) where each node truncates modulo \(x^{N-1}\).
Return \((N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] P(x) \bmod p\).










Advanced 1 (#083) — Codeforces 407E / Gym & AtCoder fps_24_l: Constrained Cycle-Length Permutations

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_l (Permutation 2) & CF Gym Constrained \(k\)-Cycle Permutation Enumerations
Prerequisite Tags: Composite Operator \(\operatorname{SET} \circ \operatorname{CYC}_S\), Cycle-Length EGF \(\exp\bigl(\sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\bigr)\), D-Finite Logarithmic-Derivative ODE Recurrence.


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
Given an integer \(N\) and a subset \(S \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) of allowed cycle lengths, count for all \(1 \le n \le N\) the number of permutations \(P = (P_1, P_2, \dots, P_n)\) of \(\{1, 2, \dots, n\}\) modulo \(998244353\) whose disjoint cycle decomposition consists exclusively of cycles with lengths in \(S\) (in fps_24_l, \(S = \{3, 4, \dots, N\}\), i.e., \(P_{P_i} \neq i\) for all \(1 \le i \le n\)).

Constraints: \(1 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) for general \(S\); \(O(N)\) time and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space for \(S = \{3, 4, 5, \dots, N\}\).
Sample Trace (\(n = 4, S = \{3, 4\}\)): With cycles of length \(1\) and \(2\) forbidden (\(P_{P_i} \neq i\)), a valid permutation of \(\{1, 2, 3, 4\}\) must be a single \(4\)-cycle; there are \((4 - 1)! = 6\) such permutations, matching \(a_4 = 3 a_3 + 3(2) a_1 = 6\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Every permutation \(\pi \in S_N\) decomposes uniquely into an unordered \(\operatorname{SET}\) of directed cycles (\(\operatorname{CYC}\)). In the concrete regime \(P_{P_i} \neq i\), what does \(P_{P_i} = i\) mean in terms of the cycle containing \(i\)? It means \(i\) belongs either to a cycle of length \(1\) (\(P_i = i\), a fixed point) or to a cycle of length \(2\) (\(P_i = j \neq i\) and \(P_j = i\), a transposition)! Thus \(P_{P_i} \neq i\) for all \(i\) if and only if \(S = \{3, 4, 5, \dots\}\).



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

A single directed cycle of length \(k\) has \((k - 1)!\) ways to orient \(k\) labeled elements, so its EGF term is \((k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \frac{x^k}{k}\).

For general \(S\): \(\widehat{A}_S(x) = \exp\!\left(\sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\right)\).
For \(S = \{3, 4, 5, \dots\}\): Since \(\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{x^k}{k} = \ln\frac{1}{1 - x}\), removing \(k = 1\) and \(k = 2\) gives: \[\widehat{C}_{\ge 3}(x) = \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - x}\right) - x - \frac{x^2}{2} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \widehat{A}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}_{\ge 3}(x)\bigr) = \frac{\exp\bigl(-x - \frac{x^2}{2}\bigr)}{1 - x}\]




Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


For general \(S\): Form \(C_S(x) = \sum_{k \in S, k \le N} k^{-1} x^k \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) and call poly_exp in \(O(N \log N)\) time.
For \(S = \{3, 4, \dots\}\): Differentiate \(\ln \widehat{A}(x) = -\ln(1 - x) - x - \frac{x^2}{2}\) to get \(\frac{\widehat{A}'(x)}{\widehat{A}(x)} = \frac{1}{1 - x} - 1 - x = \frac{x^2}{1 - x}\), cross-multiply to \((1 - x)\widehat{A}'(x) = x^2 \widehat{A}(x)\), and extract the \(O(N)\) 3-term recurrence!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. General Cycle-Length Set \(S \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) in \(O(N \log N)\)
Let \(\mathcal{C}_S\) be the class of directed cycles whose length belongs to \(S\). Since there are \((k - 1)!\) directed cycles on \(k\) labeled vertices, the EGF of \(\mathcal{C}_S\) is: \[\widehat{C}_S(x) = \sum_{k \in S} (k - 1)! \frac{x^k}{k!} = \sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\] A permutation whose cycle lengths all lie in \(S\) is an unordered set \(\mathcal{A}_S = \operatorname{SET}(\mathcal{C}_S)\) of such cycles. By the Exponential Formula: \[\widehat{A}_S(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}_S(x)\bigr) = \exp\!\left(\sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\right)\] Since \([x^0]\widehat{C}_S(x) = 0\) and \(p = 998244353 > N\), computing \(\widehat{A}_S(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) via a single \(O(N \log N)\) polynomial exponential (poly_exp) and multiplying \([x^n]\widehat{A}_S(x)\) by \(n!\) gives \(a_n\) for all \(1 \le n \le N\).


2. Optimal \(O(N)\) ODE Recurrence for \(P_{P_i} \neq i\) (fps_24_l)
When the condition is \(P_{P_i} \neq i\) for all \(i\), every cycle must have length \(\ge 3\), so \(S = \{3, 4, 5, \dots\}\). Using \(\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{x^k}{k} = \ln\frac{1}{1 - x}\): \[\widehat{C}_{\ge 3}(x) = \sum_{k=3}^{\infty} \frac{x^k}{k} = \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - x}\right) - x - \frac{x^2}{2}\] Instead of calling poly_exp, differentiate \(\ln \widehat{A}(x) = \widehat{C}_{\ge 3}(x)\) with respect to \(x\): \[\frac{\widehat{A}'(x)}{\widehat{A}(x)} = \widehat{C}_{\ge 3}'(x) = \frac{1}{1 - x} - 1 - x = \frac{1 - (1 - x^2)}{1 - x} = \frac{x^2}{1 - x}\] Clear the denominator \((1 - x)\): \[(1 - x) \widehat{A}'(x) = x^2 \widehat{A}(x)\] Now substitute \(\widehat{A}(x) = \sum_{m=0}^\infty a_m \frac{x^m}{m!}\) and \(\widehat{A}'(x) = \sum_{m=0}^\infty a_{m+1} \frac{x^m}{m!}\), and extract the coefficient of \(\frac{x^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\) on both sides (for \(n \ge 3\)):

On the left-hand side: \(\left[\frac{x^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\right] \widehat{A}'(x) = a_n\), and \(\left[\frac{x^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\right] x \widehat{A}'(x) = (n - 1) a_{n-1}\).
On the right-hand side: \(\left[\frac{x^{n-1}}{(n-1)!}\right] x^2 \widehat{A}(x) = (n - 1)(n - 2) a_{n-3}\).

Equating both sides yields the exact \(O(N)\) recurrence: \[a_n - (n - 1) a_{n-1} = (n - 1)(n - 2) a_{n-3} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad a_n = (n - 1) a_{n-1} + (n - 1)(n - 2) a_{n-3} \quad (n \ge 3)\] with base cases \(a_0 = 1, a_1 = 0, a_2 = 0\).


3. Combinatorial Verification of the Recurrence (\(n = 3, 4\))
Why does \(a_n = (n - 1) a_{n-1} + (n - 1)(n - 2) a_{n-3}\) hold combinatorially (via the Boxed Product / vertex \(n\) insertion)? Consider the cycle containing label \(n\) in a valid permutation of \([n]\):

If label \(n\)’s cycle has length \(\ge 4\), deleting \(n\) from its cycle leaves a valid permutation of \([n - 1]\) where all cycles have length \(\ge 3\); reversely, \(n\) can be inserted immediately after any of the \(n - 1\) elements in a valid permutation of \([n - 1]\) in \((n - 1) a_{n-1}\) ways.
If label \(n\)’s cycle has length exactly \(3\), we choose the other \(2\) elements of this \(3\)-cycle from \([n - 1]\) and orient them in \((n - 1)(n - 2)\) ways, leaving a valid permutation of the remaining \(n - 3\) elements in \(a_{n-3}\) ways!
Trace: \(a_3 = 2 a_2 + 2(1) a_0 = 2\) (the two \(3\)-cycles); \(a_4 = 3 a_3 + 3(2) a_1 = 6\) (the six \(4\)-cycles).



4. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \ge 1\), allowed cycle-length set \(S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}\), prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\) so \([x^0]\widehat{C}_S(x) = 0\) and \(1, 2, \dots, N \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(a_n = n! [x^n] \exp\bigl(\sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\bigr) \bmod p\) for \(1 \le n \le N\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space for general \(S\); \(O(N)\) time and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space for \(S = \{3, 4, \dots, N\}\) (fps_24_l).
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: Because \(\widehat{A}'(x) = \widehat{C}_S'(x) \widehat{A}(x)\), for \(S = \{3, 4, \dots\}\) the polynomial ODE \((1 - x)\widehat{A}'(x) = x^2 \widehat{A}(x)\) guarantees that \(a_n = (n-1)a_{n-1} + (n-1)(n-2)a_{n-3}\) counts permutations of \([n]\) with all cycle lengths \(\ge 3\) for every \(n \ge 3\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Base Cases \(n \in \{1, 2\}\) for \(S = \{3, 4, \dots\}\): Must initialize \(a_0 = 1, a_1 = 0, a_2 = 0\); starting the recurrence at \(n = 2\) accesses \(a_{-1}\) and miscounts \(2\)-cycles.
Missing \(1/k\) vs. \(1/k!\) in \(\widehat{C}_S(x)\): The cycle EGF uses \(k^{-1} x^k\), whereas the final extraction multiplies \([x^n]\widehat{A}_S(x)\) by \(n!\).

Algorithm Steps:

General \(S\) (\(O(N \log N)\)): Form \(\widehat{C}_S(x) = \sum_{k \in S} k^{-1} x^k \bmod x^{N+1}\), compute \(\widehat{A}_S(x) \equiv \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}_S(x)\bigr) \pmod{x^{N+1}}\) via poly_exp, and output \(n! [x^n] \widehat{A}_S(x) \bmod p\).
Cofinite \(S = \{3, 4, \dots, N\}\) (\(O(N)\)): Initialize \(a_0 = 1, a_1 = 0, a_2 = 0\), and iterate \(a_n = (n - 1)\bigl(a_{n-1} + (n - 2)a_{n-3}\bigr) \bmod p\) for \(3 \le n \le N\).










Advanced 2 (#011) — AtCoder fps_24_q: Dice (Power Sums & EGF Moment Expansion)

Source: AtCoder — fps_24_q (Dice)
Prerequisite Tags: EGF Binomial Convolution of Moments \(\sum_{r=0}^k \binom{k}{r} a^r b^{k-r}\), Newton–Girard Power-Sum Generating Function \(-\ln \prod_{i=1}^N (1 - A_i x)\), D&C Product Tree.


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
You are given an \(N\)-sided die with face values \(A = (A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N)\) and an integer \(M\) representing \(M\) independent rolls of the die. Compute for every exponent \(k = 1, 2, \dots, K\) the sum of \(k\)-th powers of the \(M\)-roll sum across all \(N^M\) outcomes modulo \(998244353\): \[R_k = \sum_{1 \le i_1, \dots, i_M \le N} \bigl(A_{i_1} + A_{i_2} + \dots + A_{i_M}\bigr)^k \pmod{998244353}\]

Constraints: \(1 \le N, K \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(1 \le M \le 10^9\), \(0 \le A_i < 998244353\), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(2.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N + K \log K)\) time and \(O(N + K)\) space.
Sample Trace (\(N = 2, A = (1, 2), M = 2, K = 2\)): The \(2^2 = 4\) roll sums \(A_{i_1} + A_{i_2}\) are \(1+1=2, 1+2=3, 2+1=3, 2+2=4\), giving \(R_1 = 2+3+3+4 = 12\) and \(R_2 = 2^2+3^2+3^2+4^2 = 38\), matching \(\widehat{P}_A(x)^2 = (e^x + e^{2x})^2 \equiv 4 + 12x + 19x^2 \pmod{x^3}\) with \(1!\,[x^1] = 12\) and \(2!\,[x^2] = 38\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Look at the expression \(\bigl(A_{i_1} + A_{i_2} + \dots + A_{i_M}\bigr)^k\). Expanding a \(k\)-th power of a sum via the multinomial theorem gives: \[\bigl(A_{i_1} + \dots + A_{i_M}\bigr)^k = \sum_{r_1 + \dots + r_M = k} \frac{k!}{r_1! \cdots r_M!} A_{i_1}^{r_1} \cdots A_{i_M}^{r_M}\] That \(\frac{k!}{r_1! \cdots r_M!}\) is an EGF binomial/multinomial convolution of the power sums \(p_r = \sum_{i=1}^N A_i^r\)!



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Define the Moment Exponential Generating Function of the die \(A\): \[\widehat{P}_A(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} e^{A_i x} = \sum_{r=0}^{\infty} \left(\sum_{i=1}^{N} A_i^r\right) \frac{x^r}{r!} = \sum_{r=0}^{\infty} p_r(A) \frac{x^r}{r!}\] Because \(e^{(A_{i_1} + \dots + A_{i_M})x} = e^{A_{i_1} x} \cdots e^{A_{i_M} x}\), summing over all \(N^M\) outcomes of \(M\) independent rolls simply raises \(\widehat{P}_A(x)\) to the \(M\)-th power: \[\sum_{i_1, \dots, i_M} e^{(A_{i_1} + \dots + A_{i_M})x} = \bigl(\widehat{P}_A(x)\bigr)^M \quad \Longrightarrow \quad R_k = k! [x^k] \bigl(\widehat{P}_A(x)\bigr)^M\] (And for a companion two-array sum \(S_k = \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^M (A_i + B_j)^k\), \(S_k = k! [x^k]\bigl(\widehat{P}_A(x) \widehat{P}_B(x)\bigr)\)!) Now, how do we compute the power sums \(p_r(A) = \sum_{i=1}^N A_i^r\) for all \(0 \le r \le K\) in \(O(N \log^2 N + K \log K)\) time instead of \(O(N K)\)?



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract

To find \(p_r(A) = \sum_{i=1}^N A_i^r\) for \(1 \le r \le K\), switch temporarily from the EGF \(\sum p_r \frac{x^r}{r!}\) to the OGF of \(p_r\): \[\sum_{r=1}^{\infty} p_r(A) \frac{x^r}{r} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{r=1}^{\infty} \frac{(A_i x)^r}{r} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - A_i x}\right) = -\ln \prod_{i=1}^{N} (1 - A_i x)\]

Compute \(Q_A(x) = \prod_{i=1}^N (1 - A_i x)\) via a Divide-and-Conquer NTT product tree in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time.
Compute \(L_A(x) = -\ln Q_A(x) \bmod x^{K+1}\) in \(O(K \log K)\) time, so \(p_r(A) = r [x^r] L_A(x)\) for \(r \ge 1\) (and \(p_0(A) = N\)).
Convert \(p_r(A) \mapsto \frac{p_r(A)}{r!}\) to get \(\widehat{P}_A(x) \bmod x^{K+1}\), and compute \(\bigl(\widehat{P}_A(x)\bigr)^M \bmod x^{K+1}\) via poly_pow!








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. The OGF-to-EGF Dual Transform Bridge (Newton–Girard \(\to\) Binomial Moments)
This problem showcases one of the most important algebraic pipelines in competitive programming: computing power sums via an OGF logarithm, then switching to an EGF by dividing by \(r!\) to convolve additive moments.
Let \(X_1, X_2, \dots, X_M\) be the outcomes of \(M\) independent rolls, where each \(X_j\) takes values in \(\{A_1, \dots, A_N\}\). Consider the exponential generating function of the sum \(X_1 + \dots + X_M\): \[\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} R_k \frac{x^k}{k!} &= \sum_{1 \le i_1, \dots, i_M \le N} \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{(A_{i_1} + \dots + A_{i_M})^k}{k!} x^k \\
&= \sum_{1 \le i_1, \dots, i_M \le N} \exp\bigl((A_{i_1} + \dots + A_{i_M})x\bigr) \\
&= \sum_{1 \le i_1, \dots, i_M \le N} e^{A_{i_1} x} e^{A_{i_2} x} \cdots e^{A_{i_M} x} \\
&= \left( \sum_{i=1}^{N} e^{A_i x} \right)^M = \bigl(\widehat{P}_A(x)\bigr)^M
\end{aligned}\] where the single-die moment EGF is: \[\widehat{P}_A(x) = \sum_{i=1}^{N} e^{A_i x} = N + \sum_{r=1}^{\infty} \left(\sum_{i=1}^{N} A_i^r\right) \frac{x^r}{r!} = N + \sum_{r=1}^{\infty} p_r(A) \frac{x^r}{r!}\] Similarly, for the companion two-array sum \(S_k = \sum_{i=1}^N \sum_{j=1}^M (A_i + B_j)^k\) over two arrays \(A\) and \(B\): \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} S_k \frac{x^k}{k!} = \left(\sum_{i=1}^{N} e^{A_i x}\right) \left(\sum_{j=1}^{M} e^{B_j x}\right) = \widehat{P}_A(x) \widehat{P}_B(x)\]


2. Fast Evaluation of Power Sums \(p_r(A) = \sum_{i=1}^N A_i^r\) via D&C Product Tree
Evaluating \(p_r(A)\) naively for \(1 \le r \le K\) takes \(O(N K)\) time, which TLEs for \(N, K = 2.5 \times 10^5\). Instead, form the ordinary generating function of \(\frac{p_r(A)}{r}\): \[\sum_{r=1}^{\infty} \frac{p_r(A)}{r} x^r = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{r=1}^{\infty} \frac{(A_i x)^r}{r} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 - A_i x}\right) = -\ln \left(\prod_{i=1}^{N} (1 - A_i x)\right)\] To evaluate \(Q_A(x) = \prod_{i=1}^N (1 - A_i x)\) in \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time (a paradigm we will study systematically under Divide-and-Conquer Product Trees in Chapter 09, §9.1), we recursively multiply the left and right halves of the degree-\(1\) factors:
// Self-contained D&C Product Tree core: returns prod_{i=l}^{r-1} (1 - A[i]*x) in O(N log^2 N)
Poly daq_prod(int l, int r, const vector<long long>& A) {
    if (r - l == 1) return {1, (MOD - A[l] % MOD) % MOD};
    int mid = l + (r - l) / 2;
    return poly_mul(daq_prod(l, mid, A), daq_prod(mid, r, A));
}
At recursion depth \(d \in \{0, 1, \dots, \lceil \log_2 N \rceil\}\), the polynomial degrees sum to \(N\), so the NTT work at depth \(d\) is \(O(N \log N)\), yielding \(O(N \log^2 N)\) total time.


3. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(1 \le N, K \le 2.5 \times 10^5 < p = 998244353\) (so \([x^0]\widehat{P}_A(x) = N \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) and \(0!, \dots, K! \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\)), roll count \(M \ge 1\), face values \(A_1, \dots, A_N \in \mathbb{F}_p\).
Postconditions (Output): Outputs \(R_k = k! [x^k] (\widehat{P}_A(x))^M \bmod p\) (and \(S_k = k! [x^k] (\widehat{P}_A(x)\widehat{P}_B(x)) \bmod p\) for the two-array companion) for \(1 \le k \le K\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log^2 N + K \log K)\) time and \(O(N + K)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: In daq_prod(l, r, A), the returned polynomial equals \(\prod_{i=l}^{r-1} (1 - A_i x)\), so \(r [x^r] (-\ln Q_A(x)) = \sum_{i=1}^N A_i^r = p_r(A)\) for all \(1 \le r \le K\), and \([x^k]\widehat{P}_A(x)^M = \frac{R_k}{k!}\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Zero Face Values \(A_i = 0\) at \(r = 0\): The logarithmic derivative extracts \(p_r(A)\) only for \(r \ge 1\); the constant term \(p_0(A) = \sum_{i=1}^N A_i^0 = N\) must be set explicitly to \(N\) (even if some \(A_i = 0\)).
3-Way Modular Reduction of \(M \le 10^9\): Because \([x^0]\widehat{P}_A(x) = N \not\equiv 0 \pmod p\), reduce \(M \bmod (p - 1)\) in \(N^{M \bmod (p - 1)}\) (Fermat’s Little Theorem) and \(M \bmod p\) in \((M \bmod p) \ln(N^{-1}\widehat{P}_A(x))\).

Algorithm Steps:

Product Tree (\(O(N \log^2 N)\)): Compute \(Q_A(x) = \prod_{i=1}^N (1 - A_i x)\) via daq_prod(0, N, A).
Logarithm (\(O(K \log K)\)): Resize \(Q_A(x)\) to length \(K + 1\) (since \([x^0]Q_A(x) = 1\)) and compute \(L_A(x) \equiv -\ln Q_A(x) \pmod{x^{K+1}}\).
OGF-to-EGF Conversion (\(O(K)\)): Extract \(p_0(A) = N\) and \(p_r(A) = r [x^r] L_A(x) \bmod p\) for \(1 \le r \le K\). Form the truncated EGF: \[\widehat{P}_A(x) = \sum_{r=0}^{K} \frac{p_r(A)}{r!} x^r \pmod{x^{K+1}}\]
EGF Power / Product (\(O(K \log K)\)):

For the \(M\)-die sum \(R_k\): Since \([x^0]\widehat{P}_A(x) = N \not\equiv 0 \pmod p\) and \(M \le 10^9\) can exceed \(p\), apply Chapter 02’s 3-way modular reduction law (\(M \bmod (p - 1)\) in the constant-term scalar exponent by Fermat’s Little Theorem, and \(M \bmod p\) inside the formal logarithm multiplier): \[\widehat{R}(x) \equiv \bigl(\widehat{P}_A(x)\bigr)^M \equiv N^{M \bmod (p - 1)} \exp\!\Bigl((M \bmod p) \ln\bigl(N^{-1}\widehat{P}_A(x)\bigr)\Bigr) \pmod{x^{K+1}}\] and output \(R_k = k! [x^k] \widehat{R}(x) \bmod p\) for \(1 \le k \le K\).
For the two-array companion \(S_k\): Multiply \(\widehat{S}(x) \equiv \widehat{P}_A(x)\widehat{P}_B(x) \pmod{x^{K+1}}\) via one NTT and output \(S_k = k! [x^k]\widehat{S}(x) \bmod p\).











Mastery 1 (#041) — AtCoder ABC 303 Ex: Constrained Tree Degree

Source: AtCoder ABC 303 Ex — Constrained Tree Degree
Prerequisite Tags: Prüfer Sequence Bijection, EGF Polynomial Power \((N-2)!\,[x^{N-2}] E(x)^N\), Canonical Failure Mode #16 (\(N = 1\) Guard).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
You are given an integer \(N\) and a subset \(S \subseteq \{1, 2, \dots, N - 1\}\) of \(K = \lvert S \rvert\) allowed vertex degrees. Count the number of trees on \(N\) labeled vertices \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) such that the degree of every vertex in the tree belongs to \(S\), modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(2 \le N \le 2.5 \times 10^5\), \(1 \le K \le N - 1\), \(1 \le s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_K \le N - 1\), modulus \(998244353\), time limit \(3.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time and \(O(N)\) space.
Sample Trace (\(N = 4, S = \{1, 3\}\)): With degree-\(2\) vertices forbidden, the \(12\) path trees on \(4\) vertices are excluded and only the \(4\) star trees remain, matching \((4 - 2)! [x^2] \bigl(1 + \frac{x^2}{2!}\bigr)^4 = 2! \times 2 = 4\).



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

Every vertex \(i \in \{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) is required to have degree \(d_i \in S\). By Prüfer’s bijection (for \(N \ge 2\)), labeled trees on \(N\) vertices with degree sequence \((d_1, \dots, d_N)\) are in \(1\)-to-\(1\) correspondence with Prüfer words of length \(N - 2\) over \(\{1, \dots, N\}\) in which vertex \(i\) appears \(c_i = d_i - 1\) times! Notice a necessary feasibility condition immediately: every tree with \(N \ge 2\) vertices has at least two leaves (vertices of degree \(1\)). What if \(1 \notin S\)?



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Since \(d_i \in S \iff c_i = d_i - 1 \in \{s - 1 \mid s \in S\}\), every vertex \(i \in \{1, \dots, N\}\) has the exact same allowed Prüfer-multiplicity EGF: \[\widehat{E}(x) = \sum_{s \in S} \frac{x^{s-1}}{(s - 1)!}\] By Algorithm Contract 4.2, the number of valid trees on \(N\) labeled vertices is: \[\text{Ans} = (N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \bigl(\widehat{E}(x)\bigr)^N\]



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


If \(N = 1\) (Failure Mode #16 guard, if general \(N \ge 1\) is tested): \(\deg_T(1) = 0 \notin S \implies 0\).
For \(N \ge 2\): If \(1 \notin S\), then \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = 0\), so \(\operatorname{val}(\widehat{E}) \ge 1 \implies \operatorname{val}(\widehat{E}^N) \ge N > N - 2\), meaning \([x^{N-2}]\widehat{E}(x)^N = 0\)! Thus if \(1 \notin S\), we can return \(0\) immediately.
Otherwise \(1 \in S\), so \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = \frac{1}{0!} = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\). Compute \(\widehat{E}(x)^N = \exp\bigl(N \ln \widehat{E}(x)\bigr) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time and multiply \([x^{N-2}]\) by \((N - 2)! \bmod 998244353\).








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Reduction via Prüfer’s Bijection
For \(N \ge 2\), Prüfer’s theorem establishes a bijection between labeled trees \(T\) on \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) and words \(P \in \{1, 2, \dots, N\}^{N-2}\) such that each vertex \(i\) appears \(c_i = \deg_T(i) - 1\) times in \(P\).
Therefore, \(\deg_T(i) \in S\) for all \(1 \le i \le N\) if and only if the multiplicity \(c_i\) of every symbol \(i \in \{1, \dots, N\}\) in the word \(P\) belongs to \(S - 1 = \{s - 1 \mid s \in S\}\). For a fixed tuple of valid multiplicities \((c_1, \dots, c_N) \in (S - 1)^N\) with \(c_1 + \dots + c_N = N - 2\), there are \(\frac{(N - 2)!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_N!}\) such Prüfer words. Summing over all valid tuples: \[\begin{aligned}
\text{Ans} &= \sum_{\substack{c_1 + \dots + c_N = N - 2 \\ c_i \in S - 1}} \frac{(N - 2)!}{c_1! c_2! \cdots c_N!} \\
&= (N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \left( \sum_{s \in S} \frac{x^{s-1}}{(s - 1)!} \right)^N
\end{aligned}\]


2. Valuation & Boundary Analysis
Let \(\widehat{E}(x) = \sum_{s \in S} \frac{x^{s-1}}{(s - 1)!} \in \mathbb{F}_p[x]/(x^{N-1})\).

Boundary Case \(N = 1\) (Failure Mode #16): A \(1\)-vertex tree has degree \(0\); since \(S \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\), \(0 \notin S\), so the answer is \(0\).
Boundary Case \(N = 2\): \(N - 2 = 0\). The answer is \(0! [x^0] \widehat{E}(x)^2 = ([x^0]\widehat{E}(x))^2\), which is \(1\) if \(1 \in S\) and \(0\) otherwise.
Leaf Feasibility (\(1 \in S\) vs. \(1 \notin S\)):

If \(1 \notin S\), then every term \(x^{s-1}\) in \(\widehat{E}(x)\) has exponent \(s - 1 \ge 1\), so \(\operatorname{val}(\widehat{E}) \ge 1\). Raising \(\widehat{E}(x)\) to the \(N\)-th power gives \(\operatorname{val}(\widehat{E}^N) = N \operatorname{val}(\widehat{E}) \ge N > N - 2\), which algebraically proves that \([x^{N-2}]\widehat{E}(x)^N = 0\) (combinatorially: every tree with \(N \ge 2\) vertices has average degree \(\frac{2N - 2}{N} < 2\), so at least two vertices must have degree \(1\)).
If \(1 \in S\), then \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = \frac{1}{(1 - 1)!} = 1\). Since \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = 1\) and \(p = 998244353 > N\), the formal logarithm \(\ln \widehat{E}(x) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) and formal exponential \(\exp\bigl(N \ln \widehat{E}(x)\bigr) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) are both well-defined without any valuation shift!




3. Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 4, S = \{1, 3\}\))
When \(N = 4\) and \(S = \{1, 3\}\), trees cannot have degree-\(2\) vertices (so the \(12\) path trees are forbidden, leaving only the \(4\) star trees). Here \(\widehat{E}(x) = 1 + \frac{x^2}{2!} = 1 + \frac{1}{2}x^2\). Raising to the \(4\)-th power modulo \(x^3\): \[\widehat{E}(x)^4 = \left(1 + \frac{1}{2}x^2\right)^4 \equiv 1 + 4\left(\frac{1}{2}x^2\right) = 1 + 2x^2 \pmod{x^3}\] Extracting \((4 - 2)! [x^{4-2}] \widehat{E}(x)^4 = 2! \times 2 = 4\), matching the \(4\) star trees!


4. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integer \(N \ge 2\), subset \(S \subseteq \{1, \dots, N - 1\}\), prime modulus \(p = 998244353 > N\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \((N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] (\widehat{E}(x))^N \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(N \log N)\) time via one poly_ln and one poly_exp of length \(N - 1\), and \(O(N)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: When \(1 \in S\), \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = 1\), so \(P(x) \equiv \exp(N \ln \widehat{E}(x)) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) satisfies \(k! [x^k] P(x) = \sum_{\substack{c_1 + \dots + c_N = k \\ c_i \in S - 1}} \frac{k!}{c_1! \cdots c_N!}\) for all \(0 \le k \le N - 2\).
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Missing Leaf Degree (\(1 \notin S\)): When \(1 \notin S\), \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = 0\), so calling poly_ln directly crashes on division by \(0\); guard \(1 \notin S \implies \text{return } 0\) before poly_ln.
Failure Mode #16 (\(N = 1, 2\) Bounds): At \(N = 1\), \(N - 2 = -1\) (return \(0\)); at \(N = 2\), \(N - 2 = 0\) and \((2-2)! [x^0] \widehat{E}(x)^2 = 1\) when \(1 \in S\).

Algorithm Steps:

If \(N = 1\) or \(1 \notin S\), return \(0\) immediately.
Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to \(N - 2\) in \(O(N)\) time.
Form \(\widehat{E}(x) = \sum_{s \in S} \frac{x^{s-1}}{(s - 1)!} \bmod x^{N-1}\) (which satisfies \([x^0]\widehat{E}(x) = 1\)).
Compute \(P(x) \equiv \exp\bigl(N \ln \widehat{E}(x)\bigr) \pmod{x^{N-1}}\) in \(O(N \log N)\) time.
Return \((N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] P(x) \bmod p\).










Mastery 2 (#174) — Luogu P5401 / UOJ #450: [CTS2019] 珍珠 (Pearls)

Source: Luogu P5401 — [CTS2019] 珍珠 / UOJ #450
Prerequisite Tags: Hyperbolic Parity EGF \(\sinh x = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\), Binomial Expansion of Exponential Sums, Binomial Inversion (Reversed Binomial Convolution via NTT).


Problem Statement & Exact Constraints
There are \(D\) distinct colors of pearls \(\{1, 2, \dots, D\}\). An artisan strings a sequence of \(n\) pearls \(a = (a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n) \in \{1, 2, \dots, D\}^n\). Two pearls of the same color can be paired up to form a matching ornament. We say a sequence \(a\) is good if at least \(m\) disjoint pairs of identical-color pearls can be formed from the \(n\) pearls in \(a\).
Compute the number of good pearl sequences of length \(n\) modulo \(998244353\).

Constraints: \(1 \le D \le 10^5\), \(1 \le n \le 10^9\), \(0 \le m \le 10^9\), modulus \(p = 998244353\), time limit \(1.0\text{ s}\).
Required Complexity: \(O(D \log D)\) time and \(O(D)\) space (independent of \(n, m \le 10^9\)!).
Sample Trace (\(D = 2, n = 3, m = 1\)): We need at least \(m = 1\) pair among \(3\) pearls of \(2\) colors, i.e., \(c_{\text{odd}} \le 3 - 2(1) = 1\); since \(c_1 + c_2 = 3\) is odd, every sequence has one odd and one even color count (\(c_{\text{odd}} = 1 \le 1\)), so all \(2^3 = 8\) sequences are good.



Hint 1 — Diagnostic Signal & Combinatorial Model

In a pearl sequence \(a\) of length \(n\), suppose color \(i\) appears \(c_i\) times (\(c_1 + \dots + c_D = n\)). Color \(i\) contributes \(\lfloor c_i / 2 \rfloor = \frac{c_i - (c_i \bmod 2)}{2}\) pairs! Summing over all \(D\) colors, if \(c_{\text{odd}}\) denotes the number of colors that appear an odd number of times in \(a\), the maximum number of pairs we can form is: \[\sum_{i=1}^{D} \frac{c_i - (c_i \bmod 2)}{2} = \frac{n - c_{\text{odd}}}{2}\] Thus the condition \(\frac{n - c_{\text{odd}}}{2} \ge m\) is equivalent to \(c_{\text{odd}} \le n - 2m\)!



Hint 2 — Algebraic Setup & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad

Notice that \(n \le 10^9\) is huge, while \(D \le 10^5\) is small! We cannot compute polynomials up to degree \(n\). Instead, we must extract \(\left[\frac{x^n}{n!}\right]\) analytically by expanding products of \(e^{\lambda x}\)! Tag each color that appears an odd number of times with a formal marker \(y\). Since a single color has even-frequency EGF \(\cosh x\) and odd-frequency EGF \(\sinh x = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\), its \(y\)-tagged EGF is: \[\cosh x + y \sinh x = (\cosh x + \sinh x) + (y - 1)\sinh x = e^x + (y - 1)\left(\frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\right)\] Raising this to the \(D\)-th power and expanding in powers of \((y - 1)^k\) directly gives both the binomial-sieve coefficients \(f_k\) and the exact inversion formula for \(g_c = [y^c]\)!



Hint 3 — Coefficient Extraction & Complexity Contract


Expanding \(f_k = \binom{D}{k} n! [x^n] (\sinh x)^k e^{(D - k)x}\) via the Binomial Theorem gives: \[f_k = \frac{D!}{(D - k)! 2^k} \sum_{r=0}^{k} \left(\frac{(-1)^r (D - 2r)^n}{r!}\right) \left(\frac{1}{(k - r)!}\right)\] Because \((D - 2r)^n\) depends only on \(r\), one standard NTT of length \(2D\) computes \(f_0, f_1, \dots, f_D\) in \(O(D \log D)\) time!
Extracting \([y^c]\) from \(\sum_{k=0}^D f_k (y - 1)^k\) gives \(g_c = \sum_{k=c}^D (-1)^{k-c} \binom{k}{c} f_k\), which reduces via Chapter 01 §1.2’s Reversed Convolution (Difference Index Shift) to a second NTT of length \(2D\). Finally, sum \(\sum_{c=0}^{n - 2m} g_c\).








NoteComplete Derivation & Solution






1. Parity Reduction of the Pair Count
Let \(c_i\) be the number of occurrences of color \(i\) in the sequence \(a \in \{1, \dots, D\}^n\), and let \(c_{\text{odd}} = \lvert \{i \in \{1, \dots, D\} \mid c_i \equiv 1 \pmod 2\} \rvert\). Since each odd \(c_i\) leaves exactly \(1\) pearl unpaired and each even \(c_i\) leaves \(0\) pearls unpaired, the total number of pairs formed is \(\frac{n - c_{\text{odd}}}{2}\). Therefore: \[\frac{n - c_{\text{odd}}}{2} \ge m \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad c_{\text{odd}} \le n - 2m\] Define \(K = n - 2m\):

Boundary Case 1 (\(K < 0\)): Since \(c_{\text{odd}} \ge 0 > K\), no valid sequence exists; return \(0\) immediately.
Boundary Case 2 (\(K \ge D\)): Since there are only \(D\) colors in total, every sequence has \(c_{\text{odd}} \le D \le K\); return \(D^n \bmod 998244353\) immediately.

Now assume \(0 \le K < D\).


2. Self-Contained Derivation of Binomial Inversion via Bivariate Hyperbolic EGF
Let \(g_c\) be the number of sequences of length \(n\) in which exactly \(c\) colors appear an odd number of times. By §4.2, a single color has even-frequency EGF \(\cosh x = \frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}\) and odd-frequency EGF \(\sinh x = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\). If we mark each odd-frequency color with a catalytic variable \(y\), a single color has bivariate EGF: \[\cosh x + y \sinh x = \underbrace{(\cosh x + \sinh x)}_{e^x} + (y - 1)\sinh x = e^x + (y - 1)\sinh x\] Because the \(D\) colors are independent, the generating polynomial \(\sum_{c=0}^D g_c y^c\) is obtained by raising \(e^x + (y - 1)\sinh x\) to the \(D\)-th power and applying the Binomial Theorem: \[\sum_{c=0}^{D} g_c y^c = n! [x^n] \bigl(e^x + (y - 1)\sinh x\bigr)^D = \sum_{k=0}^{D} (y - 1)^k \underbrace{\binom{D}{k} n! [x^n] (\sinh x)^k e^{(D - k)x}}_{f_k}\] Now expand \((y - 1)^k = \sum_{c=0}^k \binom{k}{c} y^c (-1)^{k - c}\) on the right-hand side and extract \([y^c]\): \[g_c = [y^c] \sum_{k=0}^{D} f_k (y - 1)^k = \sum_{k=c}^{D} (-1)^{k - c} \binom{k}{c} f_k \quad (0 \le c \le D)\] Notice how shifting the basis from \((\cosh x, \sinh x)\) to \((e^x, \sinh x)\) proves the Binomial Inversion relation between \(f_k\) and \(g_c\) in three lines using purely the Binomial Theorem! (We will develop the general theory of Binomial Inversion and subset sieves systematically in Chapter 08, §8.1.)


3. Hyperbolic EGF Expansion for \(f_k\) (First Convolution)
Let us expand the exponential product inside \(f_k = \binom{D}{k} n! [x^n] \left(\frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\right)^k e^{(D - k)x}\) using the Binomial Theorem on \((e^x - e^{-x})^k\), indexing by \(r = k - j\) (the number of \(-e^{-x}\) terms chosen): \[\begin{aligned}
\left(\frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\right)^k e^{(D - k)x} &= \frac{1}{2^k} \sum_{r=0}^{k} (-1)^r \binom{k}{r} \bigl(e^{-x}\bigr)^r \bigl(e^x\bigr)^{k - r} e^{(D - k)x} \\
&= \frac{1}{2^k} \sum_{r=0}^{k} (-1)^r \binom{k}{r} e^{(D - 2r)x}
\end{aligned}\] Notice the crucial cancellation: the exponent of \(e\) is \((k - r) - r + (D - k) = D - 2r\), which depends only on \(r\) and not on \(k\)! Since \(n! [x^n] e^{(D - 2r)x} = (D - 2r)^n\), extracting \(n! [x^n]\) and expanding \(\binom{k}{r} = \frac{k!}{r!(k - r)!}\) with \(\binom{D}{k} \cdot \frac{k!}{2^k} = \frac{D!}{k!(D - k)!} \cdot \frac{k!}{2^k} = \frac{D!}{(D - k)! 2^k}\) yields: \[\begin{aligned}
f_k &= \binom{D}{k} \frac{k!}{2^k} \sum_{r=0}^{k} \left(\frac{(-1)^r (D - 2r)^n}{r!}\right) \left(\frac{1}{(k - r)!}\right) \\
&= \frac{D!}{(D - k)! 2^k} \sum_{r=0}^{k} \left(\frac{(-1)^r (D - 2r)^n}{r!}\right) \left(\frac{1}{(k - r)!}\right)
\end{aligned}\] This is a standard Cauchy convolution of the two degree-\(D\) polynomials: \[U(x) = \sum_{r=0}^{D} \frac{(-1)^r (D - 2r)^n}{r!} x^r, \qquad V(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{D} \frac{1}{j!} x^j\] Computing \(U(x) V(x) \bmod x^{D+1}\) via a single NTT gives \(f_0, f_1, \dots, f_D\) in \(O(D \log D)\) time!


4. Reversed Convolution to Recover \(g_c\) (Second Convolution)
To evaluate the upper-triangular sum \[g_c = \sum_{k=c}^{D} (-1)^{k - c} \binom{k}{c} f_k = \frac{1}{c!} \sum_{k=c}^{D} \bigl(k! f_k\bigr) \frac{(-1)^{k - c}}{(k - c)!}\] for all \(0 \le c \le D\) simultaneously, notice that the indices \(k\) and \(k - c\) have a fixed difference \(k - (k - c) = c\). By Chapter 01 (§1.2, Reversed Convolution / Difference Index Shift), reversing the array \(k! f_k\) by setting \(i = D - k\) and \(d = k - c\) turns the difference \(c = k - d\) into the sum \((D - c) = (D - k) + d = i + d\)! Specifically, define the two degree-\(D\) polynomials: \[A(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{D} \bigl((D - i)! f_{D - i}\bigr) x^i, \qquad B(x) = \sum_{d=0}^{D} \frac{(-1)^d}{d!} x^d\] Then the Cauchy product coefficient \([x^{D - c}]\bigl(A(x)B(x)\bigr)\) is \(\sum_{i + d = D - c} A_i B_d = \sum_{k=c}^D (k! f_k) \frac{(-1)^{k - c}}{(k - c)!}\), so one NTT yields: \[g_c = \frac{1}{c!} [x^{D - c}] \bigl(A(x) B(x)\bigr) \quad (0 \le c \le D)\] (We will formalize this reversed Cauchy convolution operator as the transposed multiplication / middle product mulT in Chapter 05, §5.1–§5.2.) Finally, sum \(\text{Ans} = \sum_{c=0}^K g_c \pmod{998244353}\).


5. Small Hand-Checkable Trace (\(D = 2, n = 3, m = 1\))
For \(D = 2, n = 3, m = 1\), we need at most \(K = n - 2m = 3 - 2 = 1\) odd-frequency color:

Using \(f_k = \binom{2}{k} 2^{-k} \sum_{r=0}^k (-1)^r \binom{k}{r} (2 - 2r)^3\):

\(k = 0\): \(f_0 = 1 \cdot 2^3 = 8\).
\(k = 1\): \(f_1 = \frac{2}{2} \bigl(2^3 - 0^3\bigr) = 8\).
\(k = 2\): \(f_2 = \frac{1}{4} \bigl(2^3 - 2(0^3) + (-2)^3\bigr) = 0\).

Recovering \(g_c = \sum_{k=c}^2 (-1)^{k-c}\binom{k}{c} f_k\):

\(g_0 = f_0 - f_1 + f_2 = 8 - 8 + 0 = 0\) (indeed, \(c_1 + c_2 = 3\) is odd, so \(c_1, c_2\) cannot both be even).
\(g_1 = f_1 - 2 f_2 = 8 - 0 = 8\) (all \(2^3 = 8\) sequences have one odd count and one even count, forming \(1 \ge m\) pair).
Total \(\sum_{c=0}^1 g_c = 0 + 8 = 8\).




6. Algorithm Contract

Input & Preconditions: Integers \(1 \le D \le 10^5 < p = 998244353\) (so \(2\) and \(0!, \dots, D!\) are invertible in \(\mathbb{F}_p\)), \(n \ge 1, m \ge 0\).
Postconditions (Output): Returns \(\sum_{c=0}^{n - 2m} g_c \bmod p\).
Time & Space Complexity: \(O(D \log D + D \log p)\) time (two NTTs of size \(2D\) and \(D + 1\) modular exponentiations) and \(O(D)\) auxiliary space.
Loop / Algebraic Invariant: After the first NTT, \(f_k = \binom{D}{k} n! [x^n] (\sinh x)^k e^{(D-k)x}\) equals \(\sum_{c=k}^D \binom{c}{k} g_c\); after the second (reversed) NTT, \(g_c = \frac{1}{c!}[x^{D-c}](A(x)B(x))\) equals the exact number of pearl sequences with \(c\) odd-frequency colors.
Failure Modes & Edge Cases:

Out-of-Range \(K = n - 2m\): If \(K < 0\), return \(0\) immediately; if \(K \ge D\), every sequence has \(c_{\text{odd}} \le D \le K\), so return \(D^{n \bmod (p - 1)} \bmod p\) without indexing past \(D\).
Negative Base \(D - 2r < 0\) in \((D - 2r)^n \bmod p\): When \(2r > D\), reduce \((D - 2r \bmod p + p) \bmod p\) before modular exponentiation, and at \(D - 2r = 0\), \(0^n = 0\) since \(n \ge 1\).

Algorithm Steps:

Set \(K = n - 2m\). If \(K < 0\), return \(0\); if \(K \ge D\), return \(D^{n \bmod (p - 1)} \bmod p\).
Precompute factorials, inverse factorials, powers of \(2^{-1}\), and \((D - 2r)^{n \bmod (p - 1)} \bmod p\) for \(0 \le r \le D\) in \(O(D \log p)\) time.
Convolve \(U(x)\) and \(V(x)\) via NTT to obtain \(f_0, \dots, f_D\).
Form \(A_i = (D - i)! f_{D - i} \bmod p\) and \(B_d = (-1)^d (d!)^{-1} \bmod p\), convolve \(A(x)\) and \(B(x)\) via NTT to obtain \(g_0, \dots, g_D\), and return \(\sum_{c=0}^K g_c \bmod p\).

4.6 Chapter Summary, Diagnostic Checklist & Library Verification Footnotes

Quick-Reference Diagnostic Checklist for Labeled Enumeration
When faced with a counting problem on \(N\) elements, run through this 5-point checklist:

Are atoms distinguishable?

If elements are indistinguishable (coins, integer partitions, unlabeled trees), stay in Chapter 03 (OGFs).
If elements carry labels \(\{1, 2, \dots, N\}\) and can be partitioned into arbitrary disjoint subsets in \(\binom{N}{k}\) ways, switch to EGFs \(\widehat{A}(x) = \sum a_n \frac{x^n}{n!}\).
Exception: If elements are labeled \(\{1, \dots, N\}\) but components are forced to occupy contiguous intervals \(\{1, \dots, k\}\) and \(\{k+1, \dots, N\}\) (as in indecomposable permutations, treated in Synthesis Reserve Syn-01 (#006 — fps_24_k)), there is only \(1\) way to split the labels—use an OGF on the factorial series!

Are you combining components or extracting connected components?

General = \(\operatorname{SET}(\text{Connected}) \iff \widehat{G}(x) = \exp\bigl(\widehat{C}(x)\bigr)\).
Connected = \(\ln(\text{General}) \iff \widehat{C}(x) = \ln \widehat{G}(x)\).
Permutations = \(\operatorname{SET}\bigl(\operatorname{CYC}(\mathcal{Z})\bigr) \iff \exp\!\left(\sum_{k \in S} \frac{x^k}{k}\right)\).

Does the recurrence have a \(\binom{n-1}{k-1}\) binomial factor or is the modulus \(p \le N\)?

Use the Greene–Wilf Boxed Product \(\mathcal{C} = \mathcal{A}^{\square} \star \mathcal{B} \iff \widehat{C}'(x) = \widehat{A}'(x)\widehat{B}(x)\)!
When \(p \le N\) or working over a non-field ring \(R\), use the division-free Boxed Product recurrence \(c_n = g_n - \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \binom{n-1}{k-1} c_k g_{n-k}\) in \(O(N^2)\) time.

Are you counting words of length \(n \le 10^9\) over \(D \le 10^5\) symbols with frequency parity constraints?

Use the hyperbolic EGF filters \(\cosh x = \frac{e^x + e^{-x}}{2}\) and \(\sinh x = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{2}\), expand into linear combinations of \(e^{\lambda x}\) to extract \(n!\,[x^n]e^{\lambda x} = \lambda^n\), and apply Binomial Inversion via NTT.

Are you counting unrooted labeled trees on \(N\) vertices with degree constraints?

Apply the Prüfer Sequence Engine: \((N - 2)! [x^{N-2}] \prod_{i=1}^N \left(\sum_{d \ge 1} w_i(d) \frac{x^{d-1}}{(d-1)!}\right)\).
Always write the \(N = 1\) boundary guard first (Failure Mode #16: at \(N = 1\), \(\deg_T(1) = 0\) and \(N - 2 = -1\))!





Quarantined Library Verification Footnotes (R-24, R-37)
Before tackling the contest problems in §4.5, you may unit-test your EGF \(\exp\) and constructive Prüfer sequence primitives against these two bare template problems (quarantined from the main problem ladder under the textbook’s anti-template policy):

R-24 — Bell Numbers (\(\exp(e^x - 1) \pmod{x^{N+1}}\)):

Luogu P5748 — 集合划分计数 / Library Checker — bell_number: Given \(N \le 10^5\) (or \(5 \times 10^5\)), output the Bell numbers \(B_n = n! [x^n] \exp(e^x - 1) \bmod 998244353\) for \(0 \le n \le N\).

R-37 — Constructive \(O(N)\) Prüfer Sequence Bijection:

Luogu P6086 — 【模板】Prufer 序列: Given \(N \le 5 \times 10^6\), convert in \(O(N)\) linear time using a monotonic leaf pointer between a tree parent array and its Prüfer sequence \(P \in \{1, \dots, N\}^{N-2}\).

NoteChapter Metadata & Curriculum Contract




Part II — Rational Recurrences, Binomial Sums, Sieves & Pattern Inclusion-Exclusion
Prerequisites:

Ch 01: The formal power series ring \(K[[x]]\), valuation \(\operatorname{val}(F)\), Cauchy convolution (mul), reverse-indexed cross-correlation, divide-and-conquer product trees, and Newton inversion (inv).
Ch 02: Formal calculus (\(D, \vartheta = xD, \int\)), characteristic-\(p\) Frobenius endomorphism, and 1D Newton transcendental primitives (\(\ln, \exp, \sqrt{\cdot}, P^\alpha\)).
Ch 03: Unlabeled combinatorial operators (SEQ, PSET, MSET) and harmonic \(\ln/\exp\) compression.
Ch 04: Exponential generating functions (\(K_{\text{EGF}}[[x]]\)), binomial convolution, and labeled SET/CYC assemblies.

Core Algebraic Objects & Operators Introduced:

Upper-index negation \((1-x)^{-r} = \sum_{k \ge 0} \binom{r+k-1}{k} x^k\), Chu–Vandermonde convolution, and parallel summation.
Binomial Sum Engine 1 (Wilf’s Snake Oil): Interchanging \(\sum_n x^n\) with \(\sum_k\) to collapse sums where the free parameter \(n\) appears in a single binomial factor.
Binomial Sum Engine 2 (Egorychev Coefficient Extraction): Encoding \(\binom{A}{B} = [u^B](1+u)^A = [u^{A-B}](1-u)^{-B-1}\) in \(K[[u]]\) to sum multi-factor binomial products via geometric series in \(K[[u]][[x]]\).
Polynomial Taylor Shift \(\mathcal{T}_c: F(x) \mapsto F(x+c)\), Projective Möbius Action \((cx+e)^d F\!\left(\frac{ax+b}{cx+e}\right)\) via Bruhat decomposition, and the Generalized \(\alpha\)-Euler Transform \((1-cx)^{-\alpha}F\!\left(\frac{ax}{1-cx}\right)\) (including Failure Mode #14: Negative-Integer \(\alpha = -d\) Pole Trap).
Unsigned Stirling Numbers of the First Kind \(\left[\begin{smallmatrix} n \\ k \end{smallmatrix}\right]\), Stirling Numbers of the Second Kind \(\left\{\begin{smallmatrix} n \\ k \end{smallmatrix}\right\}\), Eulerian Numbers \(\left\langle\begin{smallmatrix} n \\ k \end{smallmatrix}\right\rangle\), Falling-Factorial Polynomials (FFP) \(x^{\underline{k}}\) with point-value EGF \(\widehat{P}(t) = C(t)e^t\), and \(O(d)\) Consecutive-Grid Lagrange Interpolation.

Complexity Targets:

Closed-form / \(O(1)\)-per-query binomial sum evaluation via Vandermonde, Snake Oil, or Egorychev extraction.
\(O(d \log d)\) Polynomial Taylor Shift, Projective Möbius Transform, and Generalized \(\alpha\)-Euler Transform via a single reverse-indexed NTT.
\(O(N \log N)\) generation of full rows and columns of \(\left[\begin{smallmatrix} n \\ k \end{smallmatrix}\right]\), \(\left\{\begin{smallmatrix} n \\ k \end{smallmatrix}\right\}\), and \(\left\langle\begin{smallmatrix} n \\ k \end{smallmatrix}\right\rangle\).
\(O(m \log m)\) or \(O(m^2)\) evaluation of polynomial-weighted binomial sums \(\sum_{k=0}^n P(k)\binom{n}{k} a^k b^{n-k}\) for huge \(n \le 10^{18}\) and \(\deg P = m\) (including arbitrary non-prime moduli \(M\)).
\(O(d)\) evaluation of a degree-\(d\) polynomial \(P(T)\) at \(T \le 10^{18}\) from consecutive sample values \(P(0), P(1), \dots, P(d)\).
