section: 8.2 Universal Run-Length Inclusion–Exclusion (连续段容斥) & ez_lcw Sparsity
text:
8.2 Universal Run-Length Inclusion–Exclusion (连续段容斥) & ez_lcw Sparsity

Why Maximal Monochromatic Runs Couple Adjacent Choices
Suppose we are counting sequences \(a = (a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n)\) over a color alphabet \(\Sigma\), where every maximal monochromatic contiguous segment (a run of identical adjacent elements \(a_l = a_{l+1} = \dots = a_r\) bounded by \(a_{l-1} \neq a_l\) and \(a_r \neq a_{r+1}\)) of length \(L = r - l + 1\) carries a prescribed weight \(w_L\). Examples include:

Smirnov Words (\(a_i \neq a_{i+1}\)): Every maximal run must have length \(L = 1\), so \(w_1 = 1\) and \(w_L = 0\) for all \(L \ge 2\).
Bounded Run Lengths (\(1 \le L \le k\)): No \(k + 1\) consecutive elements may be equal, so \(w_L = 1\) for \(1 \le L \le k\) and \(w_L = 0\) for \(L > k\).
Forbidden Exact Run (\(L \neq k\)): Runs of length exactly \(k\) are banned, so \(w_k = 0\) and \(w_L = 1\) for \(L \neq k\).
Arbitrary Run Weight \(w_L\): A maximal run of length \(L\) contributes a factor of \(w_L\) (such as \(L^2\), \([2 \nmid L]\), or a bivariate marker \(y\)) to the weight of the sequence.

Why can we not simply write \(\operatorname{SEQ}\!\left(\sum_{c \in \Sigma} W_c(x)\right)\) where \(W_c(x) = \sum_{L \ge 1} w_L x^L\)? Because in an unrestricted sequence of blocks, two blocks of the same color \(c\) can be placed adjacent to each other, fusing into a single longer run whose true length is \(L_1 + L_2\), whereas \(\operatorname{SEQ}\) would mistakenly give it weight \(w_{L_1} w_{L_2}\) instead of \(w_{L_1 + L_2}\)!



Deriving the Universal Run-Length Transfer Identity (\(F = \frac{W}{1 + W}\))
How do we eliminate the requirement that adjacent blocks have different colors? We reverse-engineer a signed formal sub-block weight \(f_s\) (\(s \ge 1\)) so that even when we allow sub-blocks of the same color to be concatenated freely, the sum of signed products over all ways to split a maximal run of true length \(L\) into formal sub-blocks equals the desired weight \(w_L\)!






TipDiagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Run-Length Transfer (连续段容斥)




The Diagnostic Signal: A problem constrains or weights maximal contiguous monochromatic blocks (or maximal contiguous intervals satisfying a transitive/equivalence bond) by their length \(L\), with target OGF \(W(x) = \sum_{L \ge 1} w_L x^L\) (\([x^0]W(x) = 0\)).
The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Two Dual Routes):

Route 1 (Formal Sub-Block Synthesis / Cluster Splitting): Replace the true run OGF \(W(x) = \sum_{L \ge 1} w_L x^L\) of a single color by a formal sub-block OGF \(F(x) = \sum_{s \ge 1} f_s x^s\), and allow sub-blocks of the same color to sit next to each other without restriction! Now consider a maximal contiguous run of color \(c\) of true length \(L \ge 1\) in the final sequence. Because adjacent runs of different colors cannot merge, this length-\(L\) run of color \(c\) is formed by concatenating some number \(r \ge 1\) of formal sub-blocks of color \(c\) of lengths \(s_1 + s_2 + \dots + s_r = L\). Summing the product of formal weights \(f_{s_1} \cdots f_{s_r}\) over all compositions of \(L\) gives: \[\sum_{r \ge 1} \sum_{\substack{s_1 + \dots + s_r = L \\ s_i \ge 1}} f_{s_1} f_{s_2} \cdots f_{s_r} = [x^L] \sum_{r \ge 1} F(x)^r = [x^L] \frac{F(x)}{1 - F(x)}\] We want this net weight to equal \(w_L = [x^L] W(x)\) for every \(L \ge 1\)! Matching generating functions gives: \[\frac{F(x)}{1 - F(x)} = W(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad F(x) = W(x) - F(x) W(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad F(x) = \frac{W(x)}{1 + W(x)}\]
Route 2 (Automaton Last-Color Isolation): Let \(S(x)\) be the OGF of all valid sequences (including the empty sequence \(1\)), and let \(A_c(x)\) be the OGF of valid non-empty sequences whose last maximal run has color \(c\). Every valid sequence ending in color \(c\) is uniquely obtained by taking a valid sequence that does not end in color \(c\)—whose OGF is \(S(x) - A_c(x)\)—and appending a single maximal run of color \(c\) with OGF \(W_c(x)\): \[A_c(x) = \bigl(S(x) - A_c(x)\bigr) W_c(x)\] Move \(-A_c(x) W_c(x)\) to the left-hand side to isolate \(A_c(x)\): \[\bigl(1 + W_c(x)\bigr) A_c(x) = W_c(x) S(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad A_c(x) = \frac{W_c(x)}{1 + W_c(x)} S(x) = F_c(x) S(x)\] Now sum over all colors \(c \in \Sigma\) using \(S(x) = 1 + \sum_{c \in \Sigma} A_c(x)\): \[S(x) = 1 + \left(\sum_{c \in \Sigma} F_c(x)\right) S(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad S(x) = \frac{1}{1 - \sum_{c \in \Sigma} F_c(x)}\]





Theorem 8.2 (Universal Run-Length Inclusion–Exclusion Transfer)
Let \(K\) be a commutative ring, and for each color \(c \in \Sigma\), let \(W_c(x) = \sum_{L \ge 1} w_{c, L} x^L \in x K[[x]]\) be the target OGF of a maximal monochromatic run of color \(c\) (\(\operatorname{val}(W_c) \ge 1\), so \(1 + W_c(x)\) has constant term \(1 \in K^\times\) and is invertible in \(K[[x]]\)). Define the Run-Length Transfer Series: \[F_c(x) = \frac{W_c(x)}{1 + W_c(x)} = 1 - \frac{1}{1 + W_c(x)} \in x K[[x]]\] Then:

Unconstrained Alphabet Sequence OGF: The OGF of sequences over \(\Sigma\) where every maximal monochromatic run of color \(c\) of length \(L\) carries multiplicative weight \(w_{c, L}\) is the free sequence of \(F_c(x)\): \[S(x) = \operatorname{SEQ}\!\left(\sum_{c \in \Sigma} F_c(x)\right) = \frac{1}{1 - \sum_{c \in \Sigma} \frac{W_c(x)}{1 + W_c(x)}}\]
Inversion Symmetry: The map \(W \mapsto F = \frac{W}{1 + W}\) is conjugated to the negation involution via the Möbius transformation \(W = \frac{F}{1 - F}\).





Master Dictionary of Canonical Run-Length Transfer Functions
The five rows below catalog the most frequent target weight functions \(W(x)\) in competitive programming and their exact transfer series \(F(x) = \frac{W(x)}{1 + W(x)}\):











#
Combinatorial Run Constraint
Target Weight \(w_L\) (\(L \ge 1\))
Target Run OGF \(W(x) = \sum_{L \ge 1} w_L x^L\)
Signed Transfer OGF \(F(x) = \frac{W(x)}{1 + W(x)}\)
Signed Coefficient \(f_s = [x^s] F(x)\) (\(s \ge 1\))




1
Smirnov Words (\(a_i \neq a_{i+1}\), no adjacent equal)
\([L = 1]\)
\(x\)

\((-1)^{s-1}\)


2
Bounded Runs (\(1 \le L \le k\), no \(k+1\) equal)
\([1 \le L \le k]\)
\(\frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x}\)
\(\frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x^{k+1}}\)
\(\begin{cases} +1 & s \equiv 1 \pmod{k+1} \\ -1 & s \equiv 0 \pmod{k+1} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}\)


3
Forbidden Exact Run (\(L \neq k\))
\([L \neq k]\)
\(\frac{x}{1 - x} - x^k\)
\(\frac{x - x^k + x^{k+1}}{1 - x^k + x^{k+1}}\)
Sparse recurrence of order \(k + 1\)

\([2 \nmid L]\)

\(\frac{x}{1 + x - x^2}\)

5
Bivariate Run Marker (weight \(y\) per maximal run)
\(y\)
\(\frac{y x}{1 - x}\)
\(\frac{y x}{1 - (1 - y)x}\)
\(y (1 - y)^{s-1}\)



Look at Row 5: \(f_s = y(1 - y)^{s-1} = (-1)^{s-1} y(y - 1)^{s-1}\) shows that Row 1 (Smirnov Words) is simply the \(y = 1\) specialization of counting runs by choosing a subset of internal adjacent equalities \((a_i = a_{i+1})\) weighted by \(y - 1 \mapsto -1\)!



Critical Failure Mode: The Labeled Order-of-Operations Trap
What if the sequences we are counting have fixed per-color frequencies \((c_1, c_2, \dots, c_m)\) (a colored multiset), or what if the elements being arranged into runs are labeled? Here lies one of the most notorious traps in generating function combinatorics:






WarningFailure Mode & Remedy: The Labeled Order-of-Operations Trap (OGF Transfer First, EGF Scaling Second)




The Trap: Suppose each maximal contiguous block of size \(s\) is built out of labeled atoms (or you plan to interleave formal sub-blocks across independent color classes using an Exponential Generating Function \(\widehat{P}_i(x)\)). A common mistake is to write the EGF of a single block \(\widehat{W}(x) = \sum_{s \ge 1} w_s \frac{x^s}{s!}\) and plug it directly into the transfer formula \(\frac{\widehat{W}(x)}{1 + \widehat{W}(x)}\).
Why It Fails: Inside a single maximal contiguous run of length \(L\) on a timeline, the \(r\) formal sub-blocks of lengths \(s_1 + s_2 + \dots + s_r = L\) occupy contiguous, already-ordered intervals from left to right: the first sub-block occupies the first \(s_1\) slots of the run, the second occupies the next \(s_2\) slots, and so on. There is only \(1\) way to partition an interval of \(L\) contiguous positions into \(r\) contiguous sub-intervals of lengths \(s_1, \dots, s_r\)! If you divide by \(s!\) before computing \(\frac{W}{1 + W}\), multiplying \(\frac{x^{s_1}}{s_1!} \cdots \frac{x^{s_r}}{s_r!}\) introduces a spurious multinomial coefficient \(\binom{L}{s_1, \dots, s_r}\), as if the elements of the \(r\) sub-blocks were interleaved arbitrarily inside the run rather than sitting in contiguous sub-intervals!
The Mandatory Two-Step Remedy:

Step 1 (Unlabeled Interval Split — OGF): First compute the signed sub-block weights \(f_s\) using ordinary generating functions (Cauchy convolution along the timeline): \[F_{\text{OGF}}(x) = \sum_{s \ge 1} f_s x^s = \frac{W_{\text{OGF}}(x)}{1 + W_{\text{OGF}}(x)}\]
Step 2 (Global Block Interleaving — EGF): Once the individual formal sub-blocks of lengths \(s_1, s_2, \dots\) and weights \(f_{s_1}, f_{s_2}, \dots\) are formed, if you now distribute labels among disjoint sub-blocks across the whole sequence (or interleave \(b_i\) formal blocks of color \(i\) across \(m\) colors via \(\frac{(\sum b_i)!}{\prod b_i!}\)), now convert to an EGF by dividing by the block factorial!







The Colored Multiset Smirnov Rule
Let us apply the Two-Step Remedy to Smirnov Words over a Multiset (Row 1 of the Master Dictionary): we are given \(m\) colors where color \(i\) has multiplicity \(c_i \ge 1\) (\(N = \sum_{i=1}^m c_i\)), and we want to count sequences of length \(N\) with no two adjacent elements of the same color (\(a_t \neq a_{t+1}\)).

Step 1 (Per-Color OGF Sub-Block Decomposition): For color \(i\), a single formal sub-block of length \(s \ge 1\) has OGF \(F(x) = \frac{x}{1 + x} = \sum_{s \ge 1} (-1)^{s-1} x^s\). If we partition the \(c_i\) identical items of color \(i\) into \(b\) formal sub-blocks (\(1 \le b \le c_i\)) ordered from left to right, the sum of signed weights over all compositions \(s_1 + \dots + s_b = c_i\) (\(s_r \ge 1\)) is: \[[x^{c_i}] \bigl(F(x)\bigr)^b = [x^{c_i}] \left(\frac{x}{1 + x}\right)^b = [x^{c_i - b}] (1 + x)^{-b} = (-1)^{c_i - b} \binom{c_i - 1}{b - 1}\] (Combinatorial check: choosing \(b\) sub-blocks among \(c_i\) items is equivalent to choosing \(c_i - b\) adjacent same-color bonds among the \(c_i - 1\) internal gaps in \(\binom{c_i - 1}{b - 1}\) ways, each bond carrying PIE weight \(-1\)!)
Step 2 (Interleaving Formal Sub-Blocks Across Colors via EGF): Once color \(i\) is partitioned into \(b_i\) formal sub-blocks, those \(b_i\) sub-blocks of color \(i\) can be interleaved with the sub-blocks of all other colors in any order! Since the \(b_i\) sub-blocks of color \(i\) are indistinguishable (when the \(c_i\) items of color \(i\) are identical), the number of ways to interleave \(b_1, \dots, b_m\) blocks into a sequence of \(B = \sum_{i=1}^m b_i\) blocks is the multinomial coefficient \(\frac{B!}{b_1! b_2! \cdots b_m!}\). Therefore, we define the Per-Color Block EGF \(\widehat{P}_i(x)\): \[\widehat{P}_i(x) = \sum_{b=1}^{c_i} (-1)^{c_i - b} \binom{c_i - 1}{b - 1} \frac{x^b}{b!}\] (Note: If the \(c_i\) items within color \(i\) are distinguishable—as in Problem Int-2 (#089 CF 840C) below—there are \(c_i!\) ways to order the \(c_i\) distinct items of color \(i\) left-to-right before cutting them into \(b\) blocks, so we simply multiply \(\widehat{P}_i(x)\) by \(c_i!\).) Multiplying across all \(m\) colors and restoring \(B!\) for each total block count \(B\) gives the exact count of valid multiset Smirnov sequences: \[\text{Ans} = \sum_{B=m}^{N} B! [x^B] \prod_{i=1}^{m} \widehat{P}_i(x)\]


Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N = 4\)): Multiset \(\{1, 1, 2, 3\}\)
Let us count valid permutations of the multiset \(\{1, 1, 2, 3\}\) (\(c_1 = 2, c_2 = 1, c_3 = 1\)) with no two adjacent \(1\)s.

For color \(1\) (\(c_1 = 2\)): \[\widehat{P}_1(x) = (-1)^{2-1} \binom{1}{0} \frac{x^1}{1!} + (-1)^{2-2} \binom{1}{1} \frac{x^2}{2!} = -x + \frac{1}{2}x^2\]
For colors \(2\) and \(3\) (\(c_2 = c_3 = 1\)): \[\widehat{P}_2(x) = \widehat{P}_3(x) = (-1)^0 \binom{0}{0} \frac{x^1}{1!} = x\]
Multiply the per-color EGFs: \[\widehat{P}(x) = \widehat{P}_1(x) \widehat{P}_2(x) \widehat{P}_3(x) = \left(-x + \frac{1}{2}x^2\right) x^2 = -x^3 + \frac{1}{2}x^4\]
Extract \(\sum_{B=3}^4 B! [x^B] \widehat{P}(x)\): \[\text{Ans} = 3! \cdot (-1) + 4! \cdot \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -6 + 12 = 6\] Indeed, out of \(\frac{4!}{2!1!1!} = 12\) multiset permutations of \(\{1, 1, 2, 3\}\), the \(6\) valid sequences with non-adjacent \(1\)s are (1,2,1,3), (1,3,1,2), (2,1,3,1), (3,1,2,1), (1,2,3,1), (1,3,2,1).





The ez_lcw Bounded-Run Sparsity Theorem (\(F_{\le k}(x) = \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x^{k+1}}\))
Now look at Row 2 of the Master Dictionary: every maximal monochromatic run must have length \(1 \le L \le k\). The target run OGF is the finite geometric series \(W_{\le k}(x) = x + x^2 + \dots + x^k = \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x}\). Substituting \(W_{\le k}(x)\) into the transfer formula produces a dramatic algebraic cancellation: \[F_{\le k}(x) = \frac{W_{\le k}(x)}{1 + W_{\le k}(x)} = \frac{\frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x}}{1 + \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x}} = \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{(1 - x) + (x - x^{k+1})} = \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x^{k+1}}\] Expanding \(\frac{1}{1 - x^{k+1}} = \sum_{j \ge 0} x^{j(k+1)}\) shows that: \[F_{\le k}(x) = \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \left(x^{j(k+1) + 1} - x^{(j+1)(k+1)}\right) = x - x^{k+1} + x^{k+2} - x^{2k+2} + x^{2k+3} - \dots\]






ImportantTheorem 8.3 (The ez_lcw Harmonic Sparsity Theorem for Bounded Runs)



For any maximum allowed run length \(k \ge 1\) and target sequence length \(n\):

\((k+1)\)-Periodic Sparsity: Up to degree \(n\), the transfer series \(F_{\le k}(x) = \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x^{k+1}}\) has at most \(2\lfloor n / (k + 1) \rfloor + 1 = O(n / k)\) non-zero coefficients!
Rational Simplification for \(m\) Symmetric Colors: When all \(m\) colors share the same bound \(L \le k\), the total sequence OGF simplifies to a rational function whose denominator has only two non-zero powers beyond the constant term: \[S_{\le k}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - m F_{\le k}(x)} = \frac{1 - x^{k+1}}{1 - m x + (m - 1) x^{k+1}}\] Consequently, for a single \(k\), extracting \([x^n] S_{\le k}(x)\) via the 2-step recurrence \(dp[i] = m \cdot dp[i-1] - (m - 1) \cdot dp[i - k - 1]\) takes \(O(n)\) time; and even for an arbitrary general composition \(G\bigl(F_{\le k}(x)\bigr)\), evaluating it for all \(k = 1, 2, \dots, n\) simultaneously via sparse polynomial operations (Ch 02) takes total time bounded by the harmonic series: \[\sum_{k=1}^{n} O\!\left(\frac{n}{k}\right) = O(n \log n)\]




Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n = 4, m = 2, k = 2\)): Binary Words Without 000 or 111
Let us count binary sequences of length \(n = 4\) (\(m = 2\)) where every maximal monochromatic run has length \(L \le 2\) (\(k = 2\)).

Here \(k + 1 = 3\), so \(F_{\le 2}(x) = \frac{x - x^3}{1 - x^3} \equiv x - x^3 + x^4 \pmod{x^5}\).
Using \(S_{\le 2}(x) = \frac{1 - x^3}{1 - 2x + x^3} \pmod{x^5}\), the denominator recurrence is \(d_i = 2d_{i-1} - d_{i-3}\) with \(d_0 = 1\): \[d_0 = 1,\quad d_1 = 2,\quad d_2 = 4,\quad d_3 = 2(4) - 1 = 7,\quad d_4 = 2(7) - 2 = 12\]
Multiplying by the numerator \((1 - x^3)\) gives \([x^4] S_{\le 2}(x) = d_4 - d_1 = 12 - 2 = 10\). Checking by hand: out of \(2^4 = 16\) binary strings of length \(4\), the strings containing 000 or 111 are 0000, 0001, 1000 and 1111, 1110, 0111 (\(6\) bad strings), leaving \(16 - 6 = 10\) valid strings!







NoteAlgorithm Contract: Universal Run-Length IE Transfer & Colored Smirnov Engine (run_length_ie_transfer)




Signature:

universal_run_transfer(W, N) -> F: Given target run weight OGF \(W(x) = \sum_{L=1}^N w_L x^L\) with \(W(0) = 0\), returns \(F(x) = W(x)(1 + W(x))^{-1} \bmod x^{N+1}\).
colored_smirnov_multiset(c[1..m], distinguishable_flag) -> Ans: Given color multiplicities \(c_1, \dots, c_m\) (\(\sum c_i = N\)), constructs \(\widehat{P}_i(x) = (\text{distinguishable} ? c_i! : 1) \sum_{b=1}^{c_i} (-1)^{c_i - b} \binom{c_i - 1}{b - 1} \frac{x^b}{b!}\) and returns \(\sum_{B=m}^N B! [x^B] \prod_{i=1}^m \widehat{P}_i(x)\).
harmonic_coalescence_sieve(G, N) -> Ans[1..N]: Evaluates \([x^N] G\bigl(F_{\le k}(x)\bigr)\) for all \(k = 1, \dots, N\) using the \((k+1)\)-periodic sparsity of \(F_{\le k}(x) = \frac{x - x^{k+1}}{1 - x^{k+1}}\).

Preconditions:

\(W(0) = 0\) so that \(1 + W(0) = 1 \in \mathbb{F}_p^\times\) is always invertible in \(\mathbb{F}_p[[x]]\).
For EGF block interleaving across colors or labeled sets, prime \(p > N = \sum_{i=1}^m c_i\) so that \(1/b!\) and \(B!\) are well-defined in \(\mathbb{F}_p\).

Postconditions:

For every true maximal monochromatic run of length \(L \ge 1\), the sum over all \(2^{L-1}\) ordered compositions \(s_1 + \dots + s_r = L\) of formal sub-blocks satisfies \(\sum_{s_1+\dots+s_r=L} f_{s_1}\cdots f_{s_r} = [x^L] \frac{F(x)}{1 - F(x)} = w_L\).

Core Invariant:

The Labeled Order-of-Operations Invariant: Formal sub-block splitting \(F(x) = \frac{W(x)}{1 + W(x)}\) is performed in the Ordinary Generating Function ring before dividing by \(b!\) (or \(s!\)) to interleave sub-blocks across distinct colors or labeled sets.

Complexity:

General run transfer \(F(x) = W(x)(1 + W(x))^{-1} \bmod x^{N+1}\): \(O(N \log N)\) time, \(O(N)\) space.
Multiset Smirnov via Divide-and-Conquer NTT: \(O(N \log^2 N)\) time (or \(O(N^2)\) via 1D knapsack DP), \(O(N)\) space.
All-\(k\) bounded-run harmonic sieve (\(k = 1 \dots N\)): \(\sum_{k=1}^N O(N / k) = O(N \log N)\) time (or \(O(N \log^2 N)\) for general outer series), \(O(N)\) space.

section: 8.3 Forbidden-Edge Path Cover IE & Eulerian Ascent/Run Sieves
text:
8.3 Forbidden-Edge Path Cover IE & Eulerian Ascent/Run Sieves

Permutations Avoiding a Sparse Graph of Forbidden Transitions
Suppose we want to count permutations \(\pi = (\pi_1, \pi_2, \dots, \pi_n) \in S_n\) such that no adjacent pair \((\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})\) belongs to a forbidden edge set \(E\) on vertex set \(V = [n]\) (for instance, \(\lvert \pi_i - \pi_{i+1} \rvert \neq 1\), or \((\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})\) is not an edge of a given tree or sparse graph \(G = (V, E)\)).
Let us apply the Bivariate Sieve (§8.1) to the \(n - 1\) adjacent transitions \((\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})\):

A subset \(F \subseteq E\) of \(j = \lvert F \rvert\) designated forbidden edges can appear simultaneously as adjacent transitions in some permutation \(\pi \in S_n\) if and only if \(F\) forms a vertex-disjoint collection of paths in \(G\)! Why? Because in any permutation \(\pi\), every vertex \(v \in [n]\) has at most one immediate predecessor (\(\text{in-degree} \le 1\)) and at most one immediate successor (\(\text{out-degree} \le 1\)), and no cycle can be formed on a subset of vertices.
If a valid path cover \(F\) contains \(j\) edges, it fuses \(n\) vertices into \(c = n - j\) connected path components. When we contract each path component into a single oriented super-element, there are \((n - j)! = c!\) ways to order the \(c\) components into a permutation!

However, when counting the ways to orient each path component, we must distinguish whether the forbidden edges in \(E\) are directed or undirected:






WarningFailure Mode & Remedy: The Undirected Path Factor-of-\(2\) Trap (\(s \ge 2\) vs. \(s = 1\))




The Trap: When forbidden transitions are given by an undirected graph \(G = (V, E)\) (symmetric non-transitive conflict, such as \(\lvert \pi_i - \pi_{i+1} \rvert = 1\) or tree edges \(\{u, v\} \in E\)), a common bug is to assign every path component of \(s\) vertices the weight \((-1)^{s-1}\) (or to multiply every component, including singletons \(s = 1\), by \(2\)).
Why It Fails: An undirected path \(v_1 - v_2 - \dots - v_s\) of length \(s \ge 2\) vertices (\(s - 1\) edges) can appear in a permutation in two distinct directions: either \(v_1, v_2, \dots, v_s\) or its reversal \(v_s, \dots, v_2, v_1\). By contrast, a trivial path of \(s = 1\) isolated vertex (\(0\) edges) equals its own reversal and has only \(1\) orientation! Conversely, if the forbidden relation is directed (or transitive, such as forbidden descents \(\pi_i > \pi_{i+1}\)), any chosen subset of \(s\) vertices has at most \(1\) valid ordering along the directed edges, so the factor of \(2\) does not appear!
The Exact Component EGF Remedy:

Directed Path Component EGF (1 orientation for all \(s \ge 1\)): \[\widehat{P}_{\text{dir}}(x) = \sum_{s \ge 1} (-1)^{s-1} \frac{x^s}{s!} = 1 - e^{-x}\]
Undirected Path Component EGF (1 orientation for \(s = 1\), 2 orientations for \(s \ge 2\)): \[\widehat{P}_{\text{undir}}(x) = x + \sum_{s \ge 2} 2 (-1)^{s-1} \frac{x^s}{s!} = 2 - x - 2e^{-x}\]




For example, when \(G = K_n\) is the complete undirected graph, \(n! [x^n] \widehat{P}_{\text{undir}}(x)\) counts undirected path covers of \(K_n\); and when \(G = (V, E)\) is a tree on \(n\) vertices, we can compute the polynomial \(C(y) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} c_j y^j\) of vertex-disjoint path covers with \(j\) edges (where each path of \(s \ge 2\) vertices gets a factor of \(2\)) via a \(O(n^2)\) tree DP (track vertex degree \(0, 1, 2\) in the cover), and then evaluate \(\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (-1)^j c_j (n - j)!\)!



Rising-Run Sieve, Eulerian Numbers \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\rangle\) & Worpitzky’s Identity
Now consider a directed, transitive relation on labels: in a permutation \(\pi = (\pi_1, \dots, \pi_n) \in S_n\), an index \(i \in \{1, \dots, n - 1\}\) is an ascent if \(\pi_i < \pi_{i+1}\). The number of permutations of \([n]\) with exactly \(k\) ascents is the Eulerian Number \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\rangle\) (for \(n \ge 1, 0 \le k < n\), and \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{matrix} \right\rangle = 1\)). Let \(A_n(y) = \sum_{k=0}^n \left\langle \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\rangle y^k\) be the \(n\)-th Eulerian Polynomial.
How do we derive the closed-form Bivariate EGF of all Eulerian numbers? We combine the Structural Substitution Rule (§8.1, Pipeline 2) with the Transitive Path Property:

Step 1 (Relaxed Rising Clusters): Suppose we designate \(j\) ascent positions \(\pi_i < \pi_{i+1}\). These \(j\) designated inequality links partition the \(n\) positions into \(c = n - j\) contiguous increasing blocks of lengths \(s_1 + s_2 + \dots + s_c = n\). Crucially, because < is a strict total order on \([n]\), once we choose which subset of \(s_r\) labels from \([n]\) goes into the \(r\)-th block, there is exactly \(1\) way to arrange those \(s_r\) labels in strictly increasing order (\(\pi_{a} < \pi_{a+1} < \dots < \pi_{a+s_r-1}\))! Thus, a relaxed increasing block of size \(s \ge 1\) contains \(s - 1\) designated ascents and has relaxed EGF: \[\widehat{C}_{\text{relaxed}}(x, y) = \sum_{s \ge 1} y^{s-1} \frac{x^s}{s!} = \frac{e^{yx} - 1}{y}\]
Step 2 (Structural Taylor Shift \(y \mapsto y - 1\) Inside \(\operatorname{SEQ}\)): A permutation with designated ascents is an ordered sequence \(\operatorname{SEQ}\bigl(\widehat{C}_{\text{relaxed}}(x, y)\bigr)\) of relaxed increasing blocks. By Pipeline 2 of Theorem 8.1, replacing \(y \mapsto y - 1\) inside \(\widehat{C}_{\text{relaxed}}\) immediately gives the exact Eulerian Bivariate EGF: \[\widehat{C}_{\text{exact}}(x, y) = \widehat{C}_{\text{relaxed}}(x, y - 1) = \sum_{s \ge 1} (y - 1)^{s-1} \frac{x^s}{s!} = \frac{e^{(y-1)x} - 1}{y - 1}\] Applying \(\operatorname{SEQ}\) (\(\frac{1}{1 - \widehat{C}_{\text{exact}}}\)) yields: \[A(x, y) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} A_n(y) \frac{x^n}{n!} = \frac{1}{1 - \frac{e^{(y-1)x} - 1}{y - 1}} = \frac{y - 1}{y - 1 - \bigl(e^{(y-1)x} - 1\bigr)} = \frac{1 - y}{e^{(y-1)x} - y}\]


Deriving Worpitzky’s Identity & \(O(n \log n)\) Single-Row Extraction
How do we extract the \(n\)-th Eulerian polynomial \(A_n(y) = n! [x^n] A(x, y)\) in \(O(n \log n)\) time for a single fixed \(n\)?

Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Normalizing the \(y^0\) Denominator Term): If we expand \(A(x, y) = \frac{1 - y}{e^{(y-1)x} - y}\) directly around \(x = 0\), the powers of \((1 - e^{(y-1)x})^m\) produce \((1 - y)\) in the denominator: \[\begin{aligned}
A(x, y) &= \frac{1 - y}{e^{(y-1)x} - y} = \frac{1 - y}{1 - y - \bigl(1 - e^{(y-1)x}\bigr)} = \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} \frac{\bigl(1 - e^{(y-1)x}\bigr)^m}{(1 - y)^m}
\end{aligned}\] To avoid expanding \(\bigl(1 - e^{(y-1)x}\bigr)^m\) by binomial theorem, look instead at the denominator \(e^{(y-1)x} - y\) as a linear expression in \(y\): its \(y^0\) term is \(e^{(y-1)x}\). Factoring out \(e^{(y-1)x}\) from the denominator normalizes the \(y^0\) constant term to \(1\): \[e^{(y-1)x} - y = e^{(y-1)x}\bigl(1 - y e^{-(y-1)x}\bigr) = e^{(y-1)x}\bigl(1 - y e^{(1-y)x}\bigr).\] Multiplying numerator and denominator by \(e^{(1-y)x}\) turns \(\frac{1}{e^{(y-1)x} - y}\) into a clean geometric series in \(u = y e^{(1-y)x}\) where every term is a single exponential \(e^{(m+1)(1-y)x}\): \[\frac{A(x, y)}{1 - y} = \frac{1}{e^{(y-1)x} - y} = \frac{e^{(1-y)x}}{1 - y e^{(1-y)x}} = \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} y^m e^{(m + 1)(1 - y)x}\] Now extract \(n! [x^n]\) from both sides using \(n! [x^n] e^{(m+1)(1-y)x} = (m + 1)^n (1 - y)^n\), and divide by \((1 - y)^n\): \[\frac{A_n(y)}{(1 - y)^{n+1}} = \sum_{m=0}^{\infty} (m + 1)^n y^m \quad \text{(Worpitzky's Identity)}\] Multiplying both sides by \((1 - y)^{n+1}\) modulo \(y^{n+1}\) gives an explicit \(O(n \log n)\) single-convolution formula for the entire \(n\)-th row of Eulerian numbers: \[A_n(y) = \left( \sum_{j=0}^{n} (-1)^j \binom{n + 1}{j} y^j \right) \left( \sum_{m=0}^{n} (m + 1)^n y^m \right) \bmod y^{n+1}\]



Hand-Checkable Trace (\(n = 3\)): Computing \(A_3(y)\) via Worpitzky’s Convolution
For \(n = 3\), let us compute \(A_3(y) \bmod y^4\) (in fact \(\deg A_3 = 2\)):

First polynomial \((1 - y)^4 \equiv 1 - 4y + 6y^2 - 4y^3 \pmod{y^4}\).
Second polynomial \(\sum_{m=0}^3 (m + 1)^3 y^m = 1^3 + 2^3 y + 3^3 y^2 + 4^3 y^3 = 1 + 8y + 27y^2 + 64y^3\).
Multiply modulo \(y^4\):

\([y^0] = 1 \cdot 1 = 1\).
\([y^1] = 1 \cdot 8 - 4 \cdot 1 = 4\).
\([y^2] = 1 \cdot 27 - 4 \cdot 8 + 6 \cdot 1 = 27 - 32 + 6 = 1\).
\([y^3] = 1 \cdot 64 - 4 \cdot 27 + 6 \cdot 8 - 4 \cdot 1 = 64 - 108 + 48 - 4 = 0\). Thus \(A_3(y) = 1 + 4y + y^2\), matching \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} 3 \\ 0 \end{matrix} \right\rangle = 1\) (321), \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{matrix} \right\rangle = 4\) (132, 213, 231, 312), and \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{matrix} \right\rangle = 1\) (123)!






The David–Barton Theorem (Bounded Increasing Runs \(< k\))
What if instead of counting permutations by total ascents, we want to count permutations of \([n]\) in which every maximal increasing contiguous run has length \(< k\) (i.e., no \(k\) consecutive elements satisfy \(\pi_i < \pi_{i+1} < \dots < \pi_{i+k-1}\))?
Because \(s\) labels have exactly \(1\) strictly increasing order, when we split a maximal increasing run of length \(L\) into formal sub-blocks of lengths \(s_1 + \dots + s_r = L\) and force the ascents within each sub-block, the elements inside each sub-block of length \(s\) are sorted uniquely (contributing \(\frac{x^s}{s!}\) to the EGF), while the \(r\) sub-blocks themselves are already ordered by their labels if and only if we force the boundary between sub-blocks to also be an ascent! Specifically, in the transitive increasing-run algebra, forcing the boundary between adjacent sub-blocks to be an ascent (<) means the \(r\) sub-blocks of sizes \(s_1 + \dots + s_r = L\) merge into a single sorted run of size \(L\) with weight \(\frac{x^L}{L!}\). Thus the formal sub-block weights \(f_s\) are determined in the ordinary composition algebra (Row 2 of the Master Dictionary with \(k\) replaced by \(k - 1\): \(f_s = +1\) for \(s \equiv 1 \pmod k\), \(f_s = -1\) for \(s \equiv 0 \pmod k\), and \(0\) otherwise), and we then divide by \(s!\) to form the EGF (David & Barton, 1962): \[\widehat{S}_{< k}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - \widehat{F}_{< k}(x)} = \left( 1 - \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} \left( \frac{x^{jk + 1}}{(jk + 1)!} - \frac{x^{jk + k}}{(jk + k)!} \right) \right)^{-1}\] Notice that when \(k = 2\) (no increasing run of length \(\ge 2\), meaning the permutation is strictly decreasing \(\pi_1 > \pi_2 > \dots > \pi_n\)), \(\widehat{S}_{< 2}(x) = \left(\sum_{s \ge 0} (-1)^s \frac{x^s}{s!}\right)^{-1} = \frac{1}{e^{-x}} = e^x\), giving \(n! [x^n] e^x = 1\) permutation for every \(n\), as expected!






NoteAlgorithm Contract: Forbidden-Edge Path Cover & Bounded-Ascent Permutations (path_cover_and_ascent_sieve)




Signature:

eulerian_row(n) -> A[0..n]: Returns the \(n\)-th Eulerian polynomial \(A_n(y) = \sum_{k=0}^n \left\langle \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\rangle y^k\) via Worpitzky’s single-convolution identity.
david_barton_bounded_runs(n, k) -> Ans: Returns the number of permutations in \(S_n\) with every maximal increasing run of length \(< k\) via \(n! [x^n] (1 - \widehat{F}_{< k}(x))^{-1}\).
tree_path_cover_sieve(G = (V, E)) -> Ans: Given an undirected tree \(G\) of forbidden transitions on \(n\) vertices, computes the path-cover polynomial \(C(y) = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} c_j y^j\) (weighting each path of \(s \ge 2\) vertices by \(2\)) and returns \(\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} (-1)^j c_j (n - j)!\).

Preconditions:

Prime modulus \(p > n\) so that \(1 / j! \in \mathbb{F}_p\) exists for Worpitzky’s binomial coefficients and David–Barton EGF coefficients.
For general forbidden transition graphs \(G = (V, E)\), designated edge subsets \(F \subseteq E\) must have maximum degree \(\le 2\) and no cycles (vertex-disjoint simple paths).

Postconditions:

eulerian_row(n) returns \(\left\langle \begin{matrix} n \\ k \end{matrix} \right\rangle \bmod p\) for all \(0 \le k \le n\).
david_barton_bounded_runs(n, k) returns the exact count of permutations \(\pi \in S_n\) avoiding \(k\) consecutive ascents \(\pi_i < \pi_{i+1} < \dots < \pi_{i+k-1}\).

Core Invariant:

Directed vs. Undirected Orientation Invariant: In transitive directed relations (such as ascents \(\pi_i < \pi_{i+1}\)), any subset of \(s \ge 1\) labels has exactly \(1\) valid path orientation (\(\frac{x^s}{s!}\)); in symmetric undirected conflict graphs, a path of \(s \ge 2\) vertices has \(2\) reversible orientations while a singleton \(s = 1\) has \(1\) orientation (\(\widehat{P}_{\text{undir}}(x) = 2 - x - 2e^{-x}\)).

Complexity:

Single-row Eulerian polynomial \(A_n(y)\) via Worpitzky NTT convolution: \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) space.
David–Barton bounded increasing runs via FPS inv: \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) space.
Tree path-cover sieve DP: \(O(n^2)\) time (or \(O(n \log^2 n)\) via heavy-light centroid NTT), \(O(n)\) space.

title: Chapter 08: The Sieve & Inclusion–Exclusion Engine: Run-Length Transfer (连续段容斥) & Goulden–Jackson Cluster Method
text:
8.4 The Goulden–Jackson Cluster Method (All 4 Regimes)

Why Overlapping Forbidden Substrings Require a Cluster Matrix
Suppose we want to count strings of length \(n\) over an alphabet \(\Sigma\) of size \(\alpha = \lvert \Sigma \rvert\) that avoid a dictionary of forbidden contiguous substrings \(\mathcal{P} = \{w_1, w_2, \dots, w_m\}\).

Why Naive Inclusion–Exclusion Fails: Two occurrences of forbidden substrings in a word can overlap (for example, \(w_1 = \texttt{ABA}\) can overlap with itself in \(\texttt{ABABA}\) at positions \(1\dots 3\) and \(3\dots 5\)). Because overlapping occurrences share characters, we cannot simply fuse \(j\) designated occurrences into \(j\) independent blocks of lengths \(\lvert w_i \rvert\).
Why Aho–Corasick DP Can Be Too Slow: Building the Aho–Corasick automaton on \(\mathcal{P}\) creates \(S = \sum_{i=1}^m \lvert w_i \rvert\) states. If \(m \le 15\) is small but each pattern has length \(\lvert w_i \rvert \approx 2 \times 10^4\), the automaton has \(S \approx 3 \times 10^5\) states—far too large for matrix exponentiation or multi-state DP!

The Goulden–Jackson Cluster Method (1979) resolves both obstacles at once: it groups any set of designated bad occurrences into maximal overlapping chains called clusters, and shows that the generating function of all clusters can be solved from an \(m \times m\) polynomial linear system (indexed only by the \(m\) patterns, completely eliminating the \(S = \sum \lvert w_i \rvert\) internal prefix states!).



The Correlation (Overlap) Polynomial \(C_{i, j}(x)\)
Before building clusters, we must impose a fundamental structural precondition on the dictionary \(\mathcal{P}\):






ImportantLocal Structural Precondition: The Antichain (Factor-Free) Property



For avoidance problems (Regimes 1, 2, and 4), the pattern set \(\mathcal{P} = \{w_1, \dots, w_m\}\) must be an antichain under the contiguous substring relation: no pattern \(w_i\) may be a contiguous substring of another pattern \(w_j\) (\(i \neq j\)). If \(w_i\) occurs inside \(w_j\), any string avoiding \(w_i\) automatically avoids \(w_j\), so \(w_j\) is redundant and must be deleted from \(\mathcal{P}\) before constructing the correlation matrix!


Given an antichain \(\mathcal{P} = \{w_1, \dots, w_m\}\), for each ordered pair \((w_i, w_j)\), define the overlap set \(\mathcal{O}(w_i, w_j)\) as the set of all overlap lengths \(k \in \{1, 2, \dots, \min(\lvert w_i \rvert, \lvert w_j \rvert)\}\) such that the length-\(k\) suffix of \(w_i\) equals the length-\(k\) prefix of \(w_j\): \[\mathcal{O}(w_i, w_j) = \Bigl\{ k \in \bigl[1, \min(\lvert w_i \rvert, \lvert w_j \rvert)\bigr] \;\Big|\; w_i\bigl[\lvert w_i \rvert - k + 1 \dots \lvert w_i \rvert\bigr] = w_j\bigl[1 \dots k\bigr] \Bigr\}\] When \(w_j\) overlaps the end of \(w_i\) by \(k\) characters, appending the remaining suffix of \(w_j\) extends the word to the right by \(\lvert w_j \rvert - k\) new characters. This motivates the Correlation Polynomial \(C_{i, j}(x)\): \[C_{i, j}(x) = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{O}(w_i, w_j)} x^{\lvert w_j \rvert - k}\]
Let us check the constant term \([x^0] C_{i, j}(x)\):

Because \(\mathcal{P}\) is an antichain, \(\lvert w_j \rvert - k = 0\) (\(k = \lvert w_j \rvert\)) can happen if and only if \(i = j\) and \(k = \lvert w_i \rvert\) (the trivial full overlap of \(w_i\) with itself)!
For all other overlaps (\(i \neq j\), or \(i = j\) with \(k < \lvert w_i \rvert\)), the extension length satisfies \(\lvert w_j \rvert - k \ge 1\). Therefore, the \(m \times m\) Correlation Matrix \(C(x) = \bigl(C_{i, j}(x)\bigr)_{1 \le i, j \le m}\) decomposes cleanly as: \[C(x) = I_m + C^{\text{strict}}(x), \qquad \operatorname{val}\bigl(C^{\text{strict}}_{i, j}(x)\bigr) \ge 1 \quad (\forall i, j)\] Because \(C(0) = I_m\) has determinant \(1 \in K^\times\), \(C(x)\) is always invertible in \(M_m(K[[x]])\)!




Cluster Decomposition & The 4 Canonical Regimes
Consider any string \(S \in \Sigma^*\) together with a designated subset \(M\) of occurrences of patterns from \(\mathcal{P}\) in \(S\), where each designated occurrence in \(M\) carries Inclusion–Exclusion weight \(-1\) (from \(y - 1\) at \(y = 0\)). Two designated occurrences in \(M\) are linked if the intervals of positions they cover in \(S\) share at least one character. Taking the connected components of \(M\) under this overlap relation partitions the string \(S\) uniquely into a sequence of:

Isolated characters \(c \in \Sigma\) not covered by any designated occurrence in \(M\) (contributing \(\alpha x\) to the OGF), and
Clusters \(\mathcal{C}\): maximal connected chains of overlapping designated pattern occurrences \(w_{i_1}, w_{i_2}, \dots, w_{i_r}\) (\(r \ge 1\)), ordered from left to right by their starting (and ending) positions, where each \(w_{i_{t+1}}\) strictly overlaps the suffix of \(w_{i_t}\) by some \(k_t \in \mathcal{O}(w_{i_t}, w_{i_{t+1}})\) with \(1 \le k_t < \min(\lvert w_{i_t}\rvert, \lvert w_{i_{t+1}}\rvert)\).

Therefore, if \(R(x)\) denotes the OGF of all clusters (weighted by \((-1)^r x^{\text{length}}\)), every marked string is a free sequence \(\operatorname{SEQ}(\Sigma + \mathcal{C})\), so the OGF of \(\mathcal{P}\)-avoiding strings is: \[F_{\text{avoid }\mathcal{P}}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - \alpha x - R(x)}\]
Let us now solve for \(R(x)\) across all four canonical regimes.


Regime 1: Single Pattern \(w\) of Length \(L = \lvert w \rvert\) (Guibas–Odlyzko Formula)
When \(\mathcal{P} = \{w\}\) consists of a single pattern of length \(L\), write \(C(x) = C_{1, 1}(x) = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{O}(w, w)} x^{L - k} = 1 + C^{\text{strict}}(x)\), where \(\mathcal{O}(w, w)\) is the set of KMP border lengths of \(w\) (including \(k = L\)). Every cluster either consists of a single occurrence of \(w\) (weight \(-x^L\)), or is formed by taking an existing cluster \(R(x)\) and extending its last \(w\) by a strict overlap (weight \(-C^{\text{strict}}(x) = -\bigl(C(x) - 1\bigr)\)): \[R(x) = -x^L - R(x)\bigl(C(x) - 1\bigr) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad R(x) C(x) = -x^L \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad R(x) = \frac{-x^L}{C(x)}\] Substituting \(R(x) = -x^L / C(x)\) into \(F_{\text{avoid } w}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - \alpha x - R(x)}\) yields the Single-Pattern Goulden–Jackson / Guibas–Odlyzko Rational OGF: \[F_{\text{avoid } w}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - \alpha x + \frac{x^L}{C(x)}} = \frac{C(x)}{(1 - \alpha x) C(x) + x^L}\]

Hand-Checkable Trace (\(N \le 4\)): Binary Strings Avoiding \(w = \texttt{ABA}\)
Let \(\Sigma = \{\texttt{A}, \texttt{B}\}\) (\(\alpha = 2\)) and \(w = \texttt{ABA}\) (\(L = 3\)).

Find KMP Borders of \(\texttt{ABA}\):

\(k = 3\): \(\texttt{ABA} = \texttt{ABA}\) (extension \(L - 3 = 0 \implies x^0 = 1\)).
\(k = 2\): suffix \(\texttt{BA} \neq\) prefix \(\texttt{AB}\).
\(k = 1\): suffix \(\texttt{A} =\) prefix \(\texttt{A}\) (extension \(L - 1 = 2 \implies x^2\)). Thus the autocorrelation polynomial is \(C(x) = 1 + x^2\).

Substitute into the Single-Pattern Formula: \[F_{\text{avoid }\texttt{ABA}}(x) = \frac{1 + x^2}{(1 - 2x)(1 + x^2) + x^3} = \frac{1 + x^2}{1 - 2x + x^2 - x^3}\]
Trace Coefficients up to \(n = 4\) via the denominator recurrence \(d_n = 2d_{n-1} - d_{n-2} + d_{n-3}\): \[\begin{aligned}
F_{\text{avoid }\texttt{ABA}}(x) &= (1 + x^2)\bigl(1 + 2x + 3x^2 + 5x^3 + 9x^4 + \dots\bigr) \\
&= 1 + 2x + 4x^2 + 7x^3 + 12x^4 + \dots
\end{aligned}\]

At \(n = 3\): \(2^3 - 1 = 7\) (only \(\texttt{ABA}\) is bad).
At \(n = 4\): \(2^4 - 4 = 12\) (the \(4\) bad strings are \(\texttt{ABAA}, \texttt{ABAB}, \texttt{AABA}, \texttt{BABA}\); notice that \(\texttt{ABABA}\) first appears at \(n = 5\) where the \(x^2\) overlap correction prevents double subtraction!).






Regime 2: \(m \times m\) Multi-Pattern Avoidance (\(\mathcal{P} = \{w_1, \dots, w_m\}\))
Let \(r_j(x)\) be the OGF of clusters whose rightmost (last) pattern is \(w_j\). A cluster ending in \(w_j\) either consists of \(w_j\) alone (weight \(-x^{\lvert w_j \rvert}\)), or is formed by taking a cluster ending in some \(w_i\) (\(1 \le i \le m\)) and extending it by a strict overlap of \(w_j\) onto \(w_i\) (weight \(-C^{\text{strict}}_{i, j}(x)\)): \[r_j(x) = -x^{\lvert w_j \rvert} - \sum_{i=1}^{m} r_i(x) C^{\text{strict}}_{i, j}(x) \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \sum_{i=1}^{m} C_{i, j}(x) r_i(x) = -x^{\lvert w_j \rvert}\] In matrix notation, let \(\mathbf{r}(x) = \bigl(r_1(x), \dots, r_m(x)\bigr)^\top\) and \(\mathbf{w}(x) = \bigl(x^{\lvert w_1 \rvert}, \dots, x^{\lvert w_m \rvert}\bigr)^\top\). Then: \[C(x)^\top \mathbf{r}(x) = -\mathbf{w}(x) \quad \Longrightarrow \quad R(x) = \mathbf{1}^\top \mathbf{r}(x) = -\mathbf{1}^\top C(x)^{-1} \mathbf{w}(x)\] (Note: If you instead group clusters by their leftmost starting pattern \(w_i\), the vector \(\tilde{\mathbf{r}}(x)\) satisfies \(C(x) \tilde{\mathbf{r}}(x) = -\mathbf{w}(x)\), which gives the exact same scalar total \(R(x) = \mathbf{1}^\top \tilde{\mathbf{r}}(x) = -\mathbf{1}^\top C(x)^{-1} \mathbf{w}(x)\)!) Therefore, the multi-pattern avoidance OGF is: \[F_{\text{avoid }\mathcal{P}}(x) = \frac{1}{1 - \alpha x - \sum_{j=1}^{m} r_j(x)} = \frac{1}{1 - \alpha x + \mathbf{1}^\top C(x)^{-1} \mathbf{w}(x)}\]



Regime 3: Bivariate Exact-\(K\) Occurrence Marking (\(-1 \mapsto t - 1\))
What if we want the Bivariate Generating Function \(F(x, t) = \sum_{n, K \ge 0} f_{n, K} x^n t^K\), where \(f_{n, K}\) is the number of strings of length \(n\) containing exactly \(K\) (possibly overlapping) occurrences of patterns in \(\mathcal{P}\)? By the Structural Substitution Rule (§8.1, Pipeline 2), the relaxed BGF where each designated occurrence carries weight \(y\) is \(G(x, y)\), and the exact BGF is \(F(x, t) = G(x, t - 1)\). Therefore, we simply replace every Inclusion–Exclusion weight \(-1\) in Regimes 1 & 2 by \((t - 1)\)!

In the Single-Pattern Case, replacing \(-1\) by \((t - 1)\) gives \(R(x, t) = (t - 1)x^L + (t - 1)R(x, t)\bigl(C(x) - 1\bigr)\), so: \[R(x, t) = \frac{(t - 1) x^L}{1 - (t - 1)\bigl(C(x) - 1\bigr)}, \qquad F(x, t) = \frac{1 - (t - 1)\bigl(C(x) - 1\bigr)}{(1 - \alpha x)\Bigl(1 - (t - 1)\bigl(C(x) - 1\bigr)\Bigr) - (t - 1)x^L}\]
In the Multi-Pattern Case (assuming \(\mathcal{P}\) is an antichain), replacing \(-1\) by \((t - 1)\) replaces \(C(x) = I_m + C^{\text{strict}}(x)\) with \(I_m - (t - 1)C^{\text{strict}}(x)\) and \(-\mathbf{w}(x)\) with \((t - 1)\mathbf{w}(x)\).




Regime 4: Cyclic Strings / Necklaces Avoiding \(w\) (\(-x Q'(x) / Q(x)\))
Suppose the positions of a length-\(n\) string are arranged cyclically modulo \(n\) (\(0, 1, \dots, n - 1 \bmod n\)), and for \(n \ge L = \lvert w \rvert\), we want to count cyclic words of length \(n\) that contain no cyclic occurrence of \(w\).






TipDiagnostic Signal & Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad: Cyclic Goulden–Jackson Trace Formula




The Diagnostic Signal: You need to count cyclic strings of length \(n \ge L\) avoiding a pattern \(w\) of length \(L\) (where occurrences of \(w\) may wrap around the boundary from index \(n - 1\) back to \(0\)).
The Reverse-Engineering Scratchpad (Two Complementary Views):

View 1 (Automaton Transfer Matrix Trace): In the \(L\)-state KMP avoidance automaton for \(w\) with \(L \times L\) transition matrix \(T\), a linear string of length \(n\) avoiding \(w\) is a walk starting at state \(0\), with OGF \(F_{\text{avoid } w}(x) = \mathbf{e}_0^\top (I - x T)^{-1} \mathbf{1} = \frac{C(x)}{Q(x)}\), where the denominator \(Q(x) = \det(I - x T) = (1 - \alpha x) C(x) + x^L\) is the characteristic polynomial of \(T\). A cyclic string of length \(n \ge L\) avoiding \(w\) is a closed walk of length \(n\) in the KMP automaton, whose count is \(\operatorname{tr}(T^n)\)! By Jacobi’s logarithmic derivative identity for \(\det(I - x T)\): \[\sum_{n \ge 1} \operatorname{tr}(T^n) x^n = -x \frac{d}{dx} \ln \det(I - x T) = \frac{-x Q'(x)}{Q(x)}, \qquad Q(x) = (1 - \alpha x) C(x) + x^L\]
View 2 (Why the Numerator \(C(x)\) Cancels on a Circle): On a circle of length \(n \ge L\), designated occurrences of \(w\) either:

Leave at least one gap or decompose into a rooted cycle of linear clusters \(\Sigma + \mathcal{C}\), whose generating function is \(-x \frac{d}{dx} \ln\bigl(1 - \alpha x - R(x)\bigr) = -x \frac{d}{dx} \ln\frac{Q(x)}{C(x)} = \frac{-x Q'(x)}{Q(x)} + \frac{x C'(x)}{C(x)}\); or
Wrap all the way around the circle as a single pure periodic overlap cycle where the last occurrence of \(w\) overlaps the first occurrence of \(w\), whose generating function is \(-x \frac{d}{dx} \ln\bigl(1 + C^{\text{strict}}(x)\bigr) = -\frac{x C'(x)}{C(x)}\). Adding (1) and (2) cancels \(+\frac{x C'(x)}{C(x)}\) against \(-\frac{x C'(x)}{C(x)}\) identically, leaving \([x^n] \frac{-x Q'(x)}{Q(x)}\) for every \(n \ge L\)!









Canonical Failure Modes in Goulden–Jackson Implementations






WarningFailure Mode & Remedy: Three Classic Goulden–Jackson Bugs




Forgetting Antichain Filtering (vs. Blindly Filtering When \(t \neq 0\)):

In Regimes 1, 2, 4 (Avoidance, \(t = 0\)): If \(w_i = \texttt{AB}\) and \(w_j = \texttt{CABD}\), then \(w_i\) occurs strictly inside \(w_j\). If you do not remove \(w_j\) first, a cluster can contain \(w_i\) nested inside \(w_j\), which is not a left-to-right chain of suffix-prefix extensions! Remedy: Always delete any \(w_j\) that contains another \(w_i\) as a substring (e.g., via Aho–Corasick fail-tree reachability) before building \(C(x)\).
In Regime 3 (Bivariate Occurrence Counting, \(t \neq 0\)): If a problem asks for the number of strings with exactly \(K\) total occurrences of patterns from \(\mathcal{P}\) (\(t \neq 0\)) and \(w_i\) is a substring of \(w_j\), you cannot simply delete \(w_j\), because whenever \(w_j\) appears, both \(w_j\) and \(w_i\) contribute to the occurrence count \(K\)!

The Exponent Direction Trap (\(x^k\) vs. \(x^{\lvert w_j \rvert - k}\)): When a suffix of \(w_i\) of length \(k\) matches a prefix of \(w_j\) of length \(k\), the number of newly appended characters is \(\lvert w_j \rvert - k\), not \(k\)! Writing \(\sum_{k \in \mathcal{O}(w_i, w_j)} x^k\) reverses the correlation polynomial and produces completely wrong coefficients whenever \(\lvert w_j \rvert\) has asymmetric borders.
Trap 3: Sign Convention in the Overlap Matrix (\(I_m + C^{\text{strict}}(x)\) vs. \(I_m - C^{\text{strict}}(x)\)): In the cluster decomposition for avoidance (\(t = 0\)), every designated occurrence of a pattern in a cluster carries Inclusion–Exclusion weight \(t - 1 = -1\). Consequently, extending an existing cluster \(\mathbf{r}(x)\) by a non-trivial overlap multiplies by \(-C^{\text{strict}}(x)\), which moves to the left-hand side of \(\mathbf{r}(x) = -\mathbf{w}(x) - \bigl(C^{\text{strict}}(x)\bigr)^\top \mathbf{r}(x)\) with a plus sign: \[\bigl(I_m + C^{\text{strict}}(x)^\top\bigr) \mathbf{r}(x) = C(x)^\top \mathbf{r}(x) = -\mathbf{w}(x)\] A classic implementation bug is to treat cluster extension like an ordinary unsigned walk \(\bigl(I_m - C^{\text{strict}}(x)^\top\bigr)^{-1}\) or to forget the minus sign on \(-\mathbf{w}(x)\), which flips the signs of all odd/even overlap chains!









NoteAlgorithm Contract: Multi-Pattern Goulden–Jackson Cluster Engine




Input: Alphabet size \(\alpha \in K\), antichain of \(m\) patterns \(\mathcal{P} = \{w_1, \dots, w_m\}\) of lengths \(L_i = \lvert w_i \rvert\) (\(L_{\max} = \max L_i\)), and target length \(N\).
Preconditions: \(\mathcal{P}\) is factor-free (for all \(i \neq j\), \(w_i\) is not a substring of \(w_j\)). Over \(K\), \(C(0) = I_m\) is automatically invertible in \(M_m(K[[x]])\).
Pipeline & Complexity:

Antichain Filter & Overlap Matrix Construction: Build the Aho–Corasick automaton on \(\mathcal{P}\) in \(O(\sum L_i)\) time, discard any pattern whose node (or prefix node) can reach another pattern’s terminal node via fail links, and compute all \(m^2\) polynomials \(C_{i, j}(x) = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{O}(w_i, w_j)} x^{L_j - k}\) in \(O(\sum L_i + m^2 L_{\max})\) time.
Solving \(C(x)^\top \mathbf{r}(x) = -\mathbf{w}(x)\):

Regime A (\(N \le 2 \times 10^5\), small \(m\)): Truncate modulo \(x^{N+1}\) or solve over \(K[x]\) (since \(\deg C_{i, j} < L_j\), \(\det C(x)\) has degree \(\le \sum L_i\)) using polynomial Gaussian elimination in \(O(m^3 (\sum L_i) \log(\sum L_i))\) or \(O(m^3 N \log N)\) time, then invert \(1 - \alpha x - \sum r_j(x) \bmod x^{N+1}\) via FPS inv in \(O(N \log N)\) time.
Regime B (\(N \le 10^{18}\), small \(\sum L_i\)): Express \(F(x) = \frac{\det C(x)}{(1 - \alpha x)\det C(x) + \dots} = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) as a rational function of degree \(D \le \sum L_i\) and extract \([x^N] \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)}\) in \(O(D \log D \log N)\) time.


Core Invariant: Every string \(S\) with \(k \ge 1\) actual occurrences of patterns in \(\mathcal{P}\) has \(2^k\) ways to designate a subset \(M\) of those occurrences, each decomposing uniquely into a sequence of free characters and maximal overlap clusters, summing to \((1 - 1)^k = 0\).
